texts.pms-address-at-the-shabad-kirtan-on-the-:
Guru Pyari Saadh Sangat Ji, Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh!

Revered saints of the Sikh community, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Taranjit Singh Sandhu ji, Chief Minister of Delhi Sister Rekha Gupta ji, my colleagues in Parliament, other ministers of the Delhi Government, all distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

In this sacred atmosphere, I respectfully bow to Guru Nanak Dev Ji. I extend lakh-lakh greetings to all the people of the country on the occasion of Prakash Parv. On this holy occasion of Guru Purab, I sincerely thank Taranjit Singh Sandhu ji for giving me the opportunity to participate in this Shabad Kirtan.

Friends,

Every word of Gurbani and every note of Kirtan is not merely music. It is a form of spiritual practice in itself. It is like diving into an ocean of knowledge. Therefore, whenever I receive an invitation to such an event, whenever I get an opportunity, I make it a point to be present in the Sangat and Kirtan.

Friends,

Guru Nanak Dev Ji used to say: Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako, Naam Japo. These teachings have been a natural part of my life. Bowing my head at Gurdwaras, immersing myself in Gurbani and experiencing spiritual bliss, finding joy in service, and then partaking in Langar, this has been a continuous part of my journey from childhood to my days as an organisational worker. Many times, I have had the good fortune of bowing my head at Sri Harmandir Sahib. Old colleagues know that I spent a considerable amount of time in Punjab as well, and that period remains one of the most special memories of my life.

Brothers and sisters,

By Guru’s grace, I have continued to receive the company of Sikh saints. At the Prime Minister’s residence too, I have had the privilege of hosting many Sikh saints and Gyanis. Even today, the presence of our saints at this gathering is creating a unique spiritual energy. On this occasion, I bow to all the saints and Gyanis. I extend my greetings to all Sikh brothers and sisters.

Friends,

This year’s Prakash Parv is accompanied by another sacred remembrance. This year marks 350 years since the martyrdom of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. It was here on the soil of Delhi that Guru Sahib sacrificed his life for the protection of the identity of this nation, for faith, belief, and values. Three hundred and fifty years have passed since that event, yet the inspiration of that sacrifice remains deeply embedded in the soil of India and in every particle of this nation. The people of this country will always remain grateful to him.

Friends,

The spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture has always been synonymous with the Sikh tradition. The martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, and Bhai Dayala Ji reminds us of this. This spirit continued uninterrupted even during the struggle for Independence. As our Lieutenant Governor explained in detail, Sardar Teja Singh Samundri Ji himself is a shining example of this tradition. He played an important role in the Gurdwara Reform Movement. He dedicated his entire life to service. This year also marks one hundred years since his martyrdom. On this occasion, I respectfully pay tribute to him as well.

Friends,

India endured centuries of slavery. During the most difficult periods in our history, our Gurus kept the flame of protecting the nation burning. Today, when great national resolutions stand before us, when the goal of a Developed India lies ahead of us, this journey can be completed only through the inspiration of our Gurus and the strength of their ideals. Therefore, it is our responsibility to keep Sikh traditions and the heritage of Sikhi shining before society like a beacon of light.

Friends,

Over the past twelve years, we have sincerely tried to fulfil this responsibility. We celebrated the 350th Prakash Parv of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. We celebrated the 550th Prakash Parv of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Numerous ceremonies were organised across India and abroad. Commemorative coins and postage stamps were issued. Special trains were operated. Programmes dedicated to Gurbani were organised throughout the country. Similarly, on the 400th Prakash Parv of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, a national event was held at the Red Fort. With the same spirit, we are currently commemorating the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.

Friends,

One month from now, on 26 December, the country will observe another Veer Baal Diwas. We began observing this day nationally because it is our responsibility to take to the younger generation the immortal saga of the martyrdom of the Sahibzadas, the resolve of Mata Gujri, and that unparalleled courage and valour. When our children learn about the circumstances of those times, when they understand how the Sahibzadas and the Gurus made the supreme sacrifice and how our faith was protected through their sacrifices, that knowledge and inspiration will create youth dedicated to the nation.

Our efforts to honour the Gurus are not limited to India. Just a few days ago, I was in the Philippines. There too, I visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara, the oldest Gurdwara in the Philippines. The Government of India is also supporting the redevelopment of the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara. Our effort is that the light of our Gurus should reach every person. With their blessings, India should continue to reach new heights.

Friends,

In our Ardas, we say: Nanak Naam Chardi Kala, Tere Bhaane Sarbat Da Bhala. This teaching of wishing well for all comes to us from Gurbani. And the thought of working for everyone’s welfare arises only when we begin to regard everyone as our own.

Friends,

Today, conflicts are taking place in many parts of the world. Many innocent people and families are facing violence and unrest. In such times, the spirit of Sarbat Da Bhala, Sarbat Da Bhala, becomes even more important, so that there may be peace everywhere, every family may remain safe, and every individual may have the opportunity to live with dignity.

Friends,

The greatest test of the values given to us by Guru Sahib comes in our everyday lives. Today, one such challenge before our society is the problem of drugs. Because when a young person falls into the grip of addiction, the dreams of an entire family are shattered along with him.

Friends,

Every young person in the country should be free from addiction. They should fulfil their dreams, study well, progress in life, and bring honour to their family and the nation. In this effort, the role of families is extremely important. Our Sangat, our Gurdwaras, and our social institutions can together guide young people and give them the courage to choose the right path. I am confident that with Guru Sahib’s blessings and the collective efforts of society, we will be able to provide a safe and bright future for our younger generation. With this sentiment, I once again extend lakh-lakh greetings to all of you on the sacred Prakash Parv of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj.

Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh!

Come, join me in raising the Jaikara – Bole So Nihal! Sat Sri Akal!

Thank you very much!
texts.pms-statement-at-the-21st-east-asia-summ:
Your Excellency, President Marcos, Your Majesty, Excellencies,

Namaskar!

I warmly congratulate President Marcos for the excellent organisation of the East Asia Summit.

Friends,

Since the COVID pandemic, the world has been facing one crisis after another. Conflicts are putting increasing pressure on food, fuel, and fertiliser supplies.

Ships and seafarers are also being targeted on international waterways. Alongside the serious threat of terrorism, new forms of cross-border crime, such as cyber fraud and online scams, are also on the rise.

Friends,

Today, what the world needs most is peace, stability, and predictability.

For many years, the East Asia Summit has served as an important platform for finding solutions to shared challenges and strengthening mutual cooperation. This very spirit of dialogue, mutual respect, and cooperation is the cornerstone of India’s foreign policy.

ASEAN unity and centrality are at the heart of our Act East Policy. We are committed to a Free, Open, Inclusive, and Rules-based Indo-Pacific. Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we will continue to support every effort towards peace.

Friends,

Our seas are the lifelines of our shared prosperity. Ensuring their security and freedom of navigation is the responsibility of us all.

In this direction, we are launching a Seafarers’ Safety Initiative, under which we will enhance cooperation in joint training and emergency response.

Friends,

Ensuring trust and security in the digital world is equally essential. At the AI Impact Summit held in India this year, we emphasized the development of human-centric, inclusive, and safe AI. We also emphasized the need for technologies such as digital watermarking to combat deepfakes and misinformation.

We welcome the Joint Statement issued today on combating online scams.

To effectively address this growing threat, we propose hosting the East Asia Summit Cyber Crime Conference at India’s National Forensic Sciences University.

Friends,

The foundation of our relationship lies in a shared heritage that goes back thousands of years. The National Maritime Heritage Complex, being developed at Lothal in India, will soon showcase this shared heritage to the world. To further strengthen our historical and cultural ties, we will also host the East Asia Summit Maritime Heritage Festival at Lothal.

Next year, we will host the East Asia Summit University Heads Conclave at Nalanda, which will provide fresh impetus to our cooperation in the fields of education and research.

Friends,

This year, we are commemorating the 50th anniversary of the historic Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia.

Fifty years ago, this region gave the world an important message, the message of peace, respect for sovereignty, and dialogue. Today, that message has become even more relevant. Our shared future will be shaped not by conflict, but by mutual respect and cooperation.

With this vision, India will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with ASEAN, remaining committed to regional peace, stability, and shared prosperity.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-opening-remarks-at-the-23rd-asean-in:
Your Excellency, President Marcos, Your Majesty, Excellencies,

Namaskar!

It is a great pleasure to reconnect once again with our ASEAN family. I warmly congratulate and thank President Marcos for his successful ASEAN Chairmanship and his valuable contribution as India’s Country Coordinator.

This is my thirteenth interaction with ASEAN leaders in this format. Over the past few years, our Act East Policy has given new momentum and greater depth to India-ASEAN relations. Our partnership has now expanded beyond our shared culture and heritage, acquiring new dimensions in areas such as digital technology, defence, and space.

Since 2014, we have undertaken more than 100 initiatives to strengthen people-to-people ties, launched nearly 250 Quick Impact Projects, and provided over 10,000 skill-building scholarships.

Today, direct flights between India and nine ASEAN countries, along with growing tourism, are further evidence of our close ties.

Friends,

Over the past few years, the world has faced one crisis after another. Today, what the world needs most is peace, stability, and predictability. In this context, this year’s theme, “Navigating Our Future, Together,” holds special significance.

Together, India and ASEAN represent nearly one-fourth of the world’s population. That is why it is essential to ensure that our future is shaped not by competition, but by cooperation. We have both the capabilities and the shared resolve to achieve this. Together, we can make this region a symbol of peace and stability.

Friends,

This is my third visit to an ASEAN country this year, reflecting the special importance ASEAN holds for India. We firmly believe that India’s growth and ASEAN’s prosperity are deeply interconnected.

In the coming years, both the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and Viksit Bharat 2047 can help us turn our shared aspirations into reality.

Over the past twelve years, we have given fresh momentum to our partnership. Now, together, we must give a new direction to the future of our region. India’s commitment to ASEAN unity and centrality in this partnership has been, and will remain, unwavering.

I am confident that today’s meeting will take our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights and contribute to building a secure, inclusive, and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

I look forward to hearing your views and suggestions.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-address-at-the-janjatiya-gaurav-diwa:
Johar!

Heartiest greetings to all of you across the country who are connected with this celebration of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. On the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, I bow to him with deep reverence. Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas is a national occasion that is linked to the pride of the tribal community and to the inspiration of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. With this same spirit, programmes are being organized across the country today to mark Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. The nation is proudly remembering its tribal heroes and heroines. Especially in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, such a massive gathering is taking place. As far as my eyes can see, there are people everywhere. Gadchiroli has a rich tribal cultural heritage. The heroic stories of Raghuji Bhangare, Bhagoji Naik, and Veer Baburao Shedmake are connected to this land. On this occasion, I respectfully pay tribute to all tribal heroes. I also congratulate all the Governors, respected Chief Ministers, Deputy Chief Ministers, and every public representative participating in this event from across the country.

Friends,

The observance of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, which began on 15 November 2021, has now become a national celebration. Last year, on the 150th birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, more than two lakh programmes were organised across the country. Crores of citizens participated in these events. There was a time when many commemorative days and celebrations in our country were shaped through a foreign perspective. But today, India is proudly remembering its heritage, its history, and its heroes with indigenous self-respect. This is a symbol of a major transformation in our national consciousness.

Friends,

Whether it was Tirot Sing’s struggle in the Khasi Hills, the Kol movement in Chota Nagpur, or the Santhal revolution led by Sidho and Kanho, the tribal community has always raised its voice against injustice. On the land of Mangarh, the followers of Govind Guru made the supreme sacrifice. Rani Gaidinliu, Tantya Bhil, and many other heroes and heroines inspired the nation through their courage. Great personalities such as Alluri Sitarama Raju and Rani Durgavati also energized tribal movements. Alongside all these stories of courage, Bhagwan Birsa Munda’s Ulgulan and his struggle at such a young age continue to inspire crores of Indians even today.

Friends,

On the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas today, more than 170 projects related to tribal development have been inaugurated across different states of the country, and foundation stones have been laid for more than 70 projects. In Mizoram, a museum dedicated to the great freedom fighter Ropuiliani Ji has been inaugurated. In Arunachal Pradesh, a new building of the Tribal Research Institute has also been inaugurated. In addition, among the projects being inaugurated and launched are educational institutions, healthcare facilities, marketing centres for tribal products, and numerous initiatives related to expanding basic amenities in villages. Across different states of the country, projects worth nearly ₹3000 crore have been inaugurated or had their foundation stones laid. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you and to the people of the country for these projects.

Friends,

Today’s programme is taking place at a time when two major achievements of the country are being discussed everywhere. The first achievement is that nearly 50 crore people have overcome extreme poverty and risen out of it. The second achievement is that the country has become free from Naxalism and Maoist terror. Both these achievements are deeply connected with the lives of our tribal brothers and sisters. A few weeks ago, the World Bank report stated that nearly 50 crore people in India have emerged from extreme poverty over the past 12–13 years. This is a very large number, 50 crore people. I consider this one of the greatest achievements of the country since Independence. This achievement belongs to the entire nation. The credit does not belong to any one government. Behind it is the collective strength of society, the effort and hard work of every citizen. The decisions taken by the central government and the schemes launched for tribal welfare in recent years have also played a major role in this achievement. I congratulate all the citizens of the country, especially my tribal brothers and sisters, for this accomplishment.

Friends,

Such a large number of people rising out of poverty is a major transformation in itself. This transformation is the story of a long journey from resolve to achievement. It has created confidence that India can fulfil its resolutions and that every Indian can achieve great goals. We had taken a pledge that those who had remained deprived of the benefits of development for decades would be given priority. As our resolutions began turning into reality on the ground, a chain of positive changes began to emerge. Our government devoted its full strength to those tribal regions that were among the most backward of the backward, where even the most basic facilities of life had not reached. For the PM-JANMAN Scheme and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, we allocated a budget of more than ₹1 lakh crore. Our effort was that the families who received facilities the latest after Independence should now receive them the fastest.

Friends,

Priority to the deprived, priority to the deprived, this has been our priority. We built more than four crore permanent houses for poor families across the country. Electricity was provided to 18,000 villages where it had not reached even after so many decades of Independence. Through the Ayushman Bharat scheme, free healthcare worth up to ₹5 lakh was provided. More than 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were established across the country, allowing healthcare benefits to reach even remote tribal areas. When poor families received toilets and sanitation facilities improved, the risk of many diseases was also reduced.

Friends,

To defeat poverty, it was equally important to increase income opportunities for poor families. Through the Mudra Yojana, we provided collateral-free loans. Under this scheme, assistance worth lakhs of crores of rupees was provided. The benefits of all these schemes reached the poor, reached Dalits, reached backward communities, and reached our tribal brothers and sisters as well. This created a new confidence within them to move forward.

Friends,

We also gave special attention to those areas that had remained behind in development for a long time. A special campaign was launched in more than 100 Aspirational Districts and over 500 Aspirational Blocks for development, better facilities, and protection of citizens’ rights. A large number of these regions have significant tribal populations. Now, under the PM Krishi Dhan Dhanya Yojana, special attention is also being given to 100 districts that are backward in agriculture. Our effort is to create new opportunities for farmers, poor families, and tribal communities in these regions. These collective efforts, and the mantra of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, have given new confidence to the poor of the country, and crores of poor people have succeeded in overcoming poverty.

Friends,

The second achievement that I referred to is freedom from Naxalism and Maoism. The people of Gadchiroli, and of tribal regions across the country, know very well that Naxalite violence caused the greatest harm to our tribal communities. In 2014, nearly 125 districts of the country were affected by Maoism and Naxalism. Hundreds of incidents of violence occurred every year. Thousands of innocent people lost their lives in these incidents. A very large number of them were our tribal brothers and sisters.

But friends,

During that period, the people affected by Maoism and Naxalism, these very brothers and sisters of mine, had been left to their fate by the governments of that era. Their rights had been taken away. Everyone sat in silence and remained quiet. You would be shocked to know that these brothers and sisters from our tribal communities were not even allowed to vote. The governments of that time remained mere spectators and sat with their eyes closed. Maoists and Naxalites would take away small children from poor mothers, and nobody could do anything. Naxalites would abduct the daughters of our homes, and everyone could only watch helplessly in anguish.

Friends,

Now that Maoism and Naxalism have been defeated, those mothers, the mothers and sisters of my tribal community, are showering countless blessings upon us. The sister who now feels safe is blessing us. The child whose childhood was once snatched away is today joining us as a young person. He is receiving opportunities for education and employment. In Chhattisgarh, areas like Bastar, where people were once afraid to go, I myself celebrated Diwali with our security forces in the heart of that region just a short while ago. This Diwali, people in all former Naxal-affected regions, including Gadchiroli, have received not only the light of lamps but also the light of hope.

Friends,

Today, our tribal society, our Janjatiya community, is contributing enthusiastically to the progress of the nation. Today, even the leadership of the country is in the hands of a daughter from the tribal community. We are all proud of President Droupadi Murmu ji.

Friends,

Today is the time for us to draw inspiration from Bhagwan Birsa Munda and devote all our energy to fulfilling the dream of a Developed India. With this call, and while bowing to Bhagwan Birsa Munda, I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. And I urge you that every year, 15th November should be eagerly awaited. The birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, and even more than that, Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, is the pride of the entire nation and the self-respect of the entire nation. Every 15th November, with greater strength than before, with greater enthusiasm than before, and on a greater scale than before, we should continue to celebrate this day. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, we should keep taking new resolutions and dedicate all our strength towards fulfilling those resolutions within a fixed timeframe. What could not be achieved during so many decades after Independence, we must accomplish within a short period. Once again, as I look at the screen and see people gathered at so many places, I can see the enthusiasm and excitement in all of them. This very sight has become the pride, glory, and grandeur of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. For such a successful effort, all of you from the tribal community deserve congratulations. I wholeheartedly congratulate all of you. I thank all of you very much.

Johar.
texts.pms-interaction-with-beneficiaries-and-s:
Program Coordinator- On this proud occasion, to begin the dialogue program of the most respected Prime Minister with the beneficiary property card holders of four states and one union territory, I first invite Manohar Mewada ji, a beneficiary property card holder from Sehore district of Madhya Pradesh.

Manohar Mewada – Hello Sir.

Prime Minister- Hello Manohar ji, Hello.

Manohar Mewada – Hello Sir. My name is Manohar Mewada.

Prime Minister – How are you,

Manohar Mewada – Very well Sir.

Prime Minister – Well, who else is there in the family.

Manohar Mewada – My family consists of me, my wife and two sons. One of my sons is married, he has a daughter-in-law and I have a grandson too.

Prime Minister – Manohar Ji, I have been told that you have taken a loan on property papers. How much did this loan help you? What changes have come in your life because of this? People from all over the country are listening to you, so Manohar Ji, tell us your experience.

Manohar Mewada – I got a lease under the ownership scheme Sir. I am happy, my family is happy too, I salute you, I thank you, I thank you.

Prime Minister – Thank you very much too. I would like to know Manohar Ji, please tell me in detail what happened?

Manohar Mewada – In detail Sir, I mean I got a lease, I took a loan on the lease, Sir I took a loan for a dairy farm, I took a loan of ten lakhs.

Prime Minister – Ten lakhs.

Manohar Mewada – Yes, I took a loan of ten lakhs Sir.

Prime Minister – Then what did you do with it?

Manohar Mewada – Sir, I have opened a dairy farm. I work in the dairy farm, I work in it, my children also work in it and because of that I also do farming and look after the dairy farm.

Prime Minister – How many animals do you have?

Manohar Mewada – Sir, I have five cows and one buffalo, out of which I have six cattle. That is my business. I get a lot of profit from it.

Prime Minister – Well, earlier there was no reason for not getting a loan, now you got a loan because you have the papers of the house.

Manohar Mewada – Sir, earlier I did not have the papers of the house, so it was not convenient for me to take a loan. Today I have the papers of the house, so today I have the benefit of taking a loan, because when I go to any bank, I get a loan.

Prime Minister – Well, it will not happen that the loan will also be spent and the children will become debtors, it will not happen.

Manohar Mewada – No, the children are not like that Sir, because whatever I am doing, my children also do the same.

Prime Minister – No, you are earning well.

Manohar Mewada – Sir, I mean you are earning well.

Prime Minister – You are paying back the loan,

Manohar Mewada – Yes

Prime Minister – You must be paying back the loan also.

Manohar Mewada – No Sir, I mean my installment comes around 16000, so what I mean is that my income is 30 thousand rupees per month, so I pay the installment from that and I also manage the rest of my household expenses from that.

Prime Minister – Well Manohar Ji, it was very good, the difficulties in your life have reduced due to your central government scheme, it is very pleasant for me and it was very good to see that through the ownership scheme, the income of lakhs of families like yours is also increasing.

Manohar Mewada – Yes Sir.

Prime Minister – Our government’s priority is that every citizen of the country should hold his head high with pride, his life should become easy, the ownership scheme is an extension of this thought. Many congratulations to you Manohar ji and tell everyone in the village also that everyone should get their card made and also take a loan from it, do some business, definitely tell this to everyone, okay, many thanks to you Manohar ji.

Manohar Mewada – Sir, on my behalf as well as on my family’s behalf, many thanks to you, Namaskar Sir.

Prime Minister – Thank you.

Program Coordinator- Now Mrs. Rachna ji, a property card holder and beneficiary of SVAMITVA from Sri Ganganagar district of Rajasthan is joining for the dialogue.

Rachna – My greetings to the Honorable Prime Minister.

Prime Minister- Hello Rachna ji, Namaskar. Rachna ji, tell me what work you do, who all are there in your family, how did you get in touch with this SVAMITVA scheme.

Rachna – Sir, in my family, my husband is Naresh Kumar Bishnoi and I have a son and a daughter.

Prime Minister – And tell me about this scheme.

Rachna – Sir, I have been living here for 20 years, I have a small house, I did not have any documents for it and even now I got this card under SVAMITVA scheme, so sir, I have taken a loan of 7 lakh 45 thousand and I have also opened a shop, put goods in the shop and I have fulfilled my children’s dream of higher education.

Prime Minister- So before getting the card, you did not have any information about any property, you had nothing.

Rachna – No sir, I did not have anything.

Prime Minister- Then there must be problems, people are also troubled.

Rachna – I was very worried Sir, I got the Swamitva Yojana card Sir, I and my family are very happy.

Prime Minister – Well, did you ever think that when 20 years have passed and you had nothing, you must have given up hope, did you ever think that this would ever happen.

Rachna – Sir, I never thought that this would ever happen, I have been living in the same house for 20 years Sir.

Prime Minister – Well, can you tell me what other benefits you have got from the Swamitva Yojana.

Rachna – Yes Sir, I will tell you, through this I have got SBM scheme and Sir, I have also taken a Mudra loan of Rs 8 lakh and I am associated with Rajivka and my family’s Ayushman card has also been made Sir.

Prime Minister – Business is going well.

Rachna – It is going absolutely fine Sir, I also work in MNREGA.

Prime Minister- So you have taken a loan of Rs 15 lakh, you run a shop, you also work in MNREGA, your husband must also be doing something.

Rachna- Sir, he is a driver.

Prime Minister- Well, I was told that your daughter wants to study abroad, will you give the credit for this to the Swamitva Yojana?

Rachna- Sir, I want to send her abroad, she wants to go.

Prime Minister- Please tell me, please tell me.

Rachna- Right now she is doing AILET, my daughter is with her.

Prime Minister- Where else do you want to send her?

Rachna- Australia.

Prime Minister- Australia, so this will be possible for you because of the Swamitva Yojana.

Rachna- Yes Sir.

Prime Minister- Let’s go Rachna ji, I pray to God that this dream of yours and your daughter is fulfilled very soon. It is a matter of great happiness that the Swamitva Yojana is not only fulfilling the need but it is also strengthening the wings of aspirations of our citizens. In the true sense, the significance of any scheme is that people are connected to it and are empowered. Rachna ji, you wanted to say something in the middle.

Rachna – Sir, I want to say that if you are a leader like me, then I thank you from the bottom of my heart on behalf of me and my family for the scheme that you have started for the welfare of the poor.

Prime Minister – Thank you very much, please convey my greetings to all the people of the village that I can see. Come on, let’s see who is joining us now.

Program Coordinator – Now, Mr. Roshan Sambhaji Patil, a beneficiary of ownership and property card holder from Nagpur district of Maharashtra is joining for the dialogue.

Prime Minister – Hello Roshan ji.

Roshan – Hello Sir.

Prime Minister – Roshan ji said.

Roshan – Yes Sir, Sir, from Maharashtra of saints and great men and from the holy land of initiation Nagpur, I Roshan Patil greet you Sir.

Prime Minister – Hello.

Roshan – Hello Sir.

Prime Minister – What is your son’s name?

Roshan Patil – Sir, my son’s name is Sharvil, today is also his birthday.

Prime Minister- It’s his birthday today…

Roshan Patil- Yes Sir, it’s his birthday…

Prime Minister- Please give me your blessings.

Roshan Patil- Your blessings are with him.

Prime Minister- Ok Roshan ji, what do you do and how many people are there in your family?

Roshan- Sir, I am a farmer, I do farming and also have a private job, Sir. There are a total of six people in my family, my wife, my mother and father, my two brothers, and now my younger son, Sir.

Prime Minister- So how did you get this ownership card, property sheet, all these activities related to this and what benefit did you get from it in future?

Roshan- Sir, since I got the ownership card, I was able to take a loan on it. Earlier, Sir, I was not able to get a loan in my house, I mean I have a big house, I have an old house in the village, so I was able to get a loan because I had a property card, Sir. I took a loan of 9 lakh rupees from the bank and with some of that money, I built a house and with some of that money, I arranged for irrigation in the fields. Because of that, my crop yield increased and my income also increased. Two-three years ago, I used to have only one crop, but now I have three crops and my income has also increased and I also get a good profit from farming.

Prime Minister – Well, when you had such strong documents, papers, did you face any problem in taking a loan from the bank? Then bring this, bring that, bring this, bring that, does it happen?

Roshan – Yes, sir, earlier there were a lot of problems with documents, I mean bring this, bring that, the bank people used to make me run around for each and every paper. But since I have received the ownership card, there is no need for any document, the ownership card alone is enough for everyone.

Prime Minister – You have confidence.

Roshan – I am very grateful to you for this, sir.

Prime Minister – The bank people have complete confidence.

Roshan – Yes Sir, the bankers have a lot of faith in it and loans are easily available on it.

Prime Minister – But now that you have built a house, how will you repay the loan?

Roshan – Yes Sir, I grow vegetables in farming, I also get profit from that. There are other two-three crops. There is also profit from that, due to the means of irrigation, other crops also come out well, sir, hence there is more profit, so I can easily repay the loan sir.

Prime Minister – Ok Roshan ji, which other schemes of the Central Government have you benefited from?

Roshan – Yes Sir, I am getting the benefit of the Ujjwala Gas Scheme of the Central Government, I am getting the benefit of PM Samman Nidhi Yojana, I am getting the benefit of PM Pick Insurance Scheme, I am getting the benefit of such schemes sir.

Prime Minister – Ok Roshan ji, it is a matter of happiness that people are getting so many types of help from the ownership scheme. When the ownership scheme was brought, Roshan was saying something.

Roshan – Yes Sir, people are getting a lot of benefit due to the ownership scheme sir. Some people in our village have taken loans to open shops. Earlier, they could not do anything, they could not get loans on the basis of their farming, they could not get loans on the basis of their houses, but due to the ownership card, everyone is getting loans easily, because of this people are doing their small businesses and farming too, so their income has doubled, Sir, and they are easily raising their families and children, and are living a happy life, Sir.

Prime Minister – Well, Roshan ji, you have described that other people of your village are also taking advantage of this, and I would also like that all the people of the village should take advantage of these arrangements, and you have also built a house, improved farming, and your income has also doubled, and when a house is built, there is a concrete roof, then the status also increases in the village, so does yours.

Roshan – Yes, Sir, all the credit for this goes to you, Sir, I want to thank you very much, Sir.

Prime Minister – Well, I wish you all the best, Sir, and best wishes to the people of Nagpur as well.

Roshan – Thank you Sir, thank you, thank you Sir.

Prime Minister – Who is it now?

Program Coordinator – Now the most respected Prime Minister will interact with another beneficiary ownership property card holder Smt. Gajendra Sangeeta ji from Rayagada district of Odisha.

Sangita – My salutations to the Honorable Prime Minister.

Prime Minister – Hello Sangeeta ji.

Sangeeta – Hello.

Prime Minister – Sangeeta ji, tell me what work you do.

Sangeeta – I do sewing work, I do tailoring.

Prime Minister – Yes and how many people in the family have responsibilities?

Sangeeta – There are four people in my family, two children and my husband. One daughter is studying in the final year of M.Com, the second son is working in Andhra Pradesh in Kadapa, and my husband is also working in a private company.

Prime Minister – Well, Sangeeta ji, getting the property rights of the house, getting the papers is not like that, let’s say after the government papers, another paper has come, has it brought a big change in your life?

Sangeeta – Yes sir, there has been a big change. Earlier there was no paper, there was no permanent paper, sir, the permanent paper that we got also increased our confidence that we are living in the village and we are also feeling very good about it.

Prime Minister – What have you done now that you have got the papers.

Sangeeta – Yes, we have just received the papers. I have applied for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana but it did not happen. I also do small household chores.

Prime Minister – Have you taken any loan from the bank yet?

Sangita – Yes Sir, I have not taken it yet, I am thinking of taking it now.

Prime Minister – But have you contacted the bank, do you want to take a loan?

Sangita – Yes Sir, I am thinking of taking a loan now.

Prime Minister – So what will you do with the loan?

Sangita – I want to expand my business a bit by taking a loan, I want to expand my tailoring business a bit, Sir.

Prime Minister – So I will focus more on my business.

Sangita – Yes, it can be useful for my children’s education too, if some money is saved.

Prime Minister – Come on Sangeeta ji, expand your work and your home, best wishes to you for this from now onwards. Through the ownership scheme, your biggest worry has ended. You have received the papers of your house and you are also a member of the self-help group. What were you saying Sangeeta ji, Sangeeta ji you were saying something.

Sangeeta – It was 60 years. We did not have any permanent papers Sir, we just got it through the ownership scheme, I am very grateful to you Sir.

Prime Minister – Well, your blessings are my biggest strength. See, you also work in the Self Help Group and our government is also continuously helping the women SHGs. See, the ownership scheme is going to transform the entire village. Come on, more people are waiting for us, now who is left, brother, which way to go.

Program Coordinator – Jammu Kashmir. Now the most respected Prime Minister will interact with another ownership beneficiary and property card holder Shri Virendra Kumar ji of Samba district of Jammu and Kashmir.

Prime Minister – Hello Virendra ji.

Virendra – Hello.

Prime Minister – Virendra ji, please tell me about yourself.

Virendra – Prime Minister ji, I am a farmer and I and my family are very happy that I got the property card. We were living on this land for many generations and now after getting its documents, my heart feels proud. Prime Minister ji, that is why I am very grateful to you.

Prime Minister – Well, earlier there were no cards and documents and other villagers may not have them either.

Virendra – Sir, none of the people in our village had any papers. Many generations were living in this village for more than 100 years, but there were no papers. Now, everyone in the village is happy with the papers that we have received under the ownership scheme.

Prime Minister – Well, we have received the property card, what difference has it made in your life?

Virendra – I have received the property card, but there was a dispute regarding one of my lands. Because of this property card, that dispute regarding one of my lands has also been resolved. Now, because of this property card, I can take a loan from the bank by mortgaging my land and can repair my house and strengthen the financial condition of my family.

Prime Minister – Well, in your village, have others also taken any benefit due to the ownership scheme? Has there been any change there as well?

Virendra – Yes, sir, there has definitely been a change, Prime Minister. Whatever property cards we have received in our village under the ownership scheme, now the ownership rights of every villager have been clearly decided. As all the disputes related to land and property have been resolved to a great extent, so the villagers can take loans by keeping their land and property as collateral in the bank and are also adopting many other types of schemes, so on behalf of the villagers, I thank you from the bottom of my heart.

Prime Minister – Virendra ji, it was nice to talk to you all, I am happy. Yes Sir, and it is a matter of great happiness for me that you have not just considered the card received under the ownership scheme as a paper for the house, you are also making it a way of your progress. I wish you all the best. It is cold weather, all the people of Jammu and Kashmir should take care of their health, many congratulations to you.

Virendra – Thank you Sir.

Program Coordinator – Now I would like to humbly request the most respected Prime Minister to address him.

Namaskar!

Today is a very historic day for the villages of the country, for the rural economy of the country. Honorable Governors of many states are associated with this program. Chief Ministers of Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, UP, Maharashtra and Gujarat have also joined us. Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir, Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh are also with us. My colleagues from the Union Cabinet are present in different parts of the country, in different programs. Ministers of state governments are also present, MPs and MLAs are also present, all other public representatives are also present.

All the colleagues associated with thousands of Gram Panchayats, lakhs of beneficiaries of the Swamitva Yojana, this is such a wide and huge program in itself and you all have joined it with great enthusiasm, I congratulate all of you.

Friends,

Swamitva Yojana was started five years ago, so that the people living in the villages could be given legal proof of their house. Somewhere it is called Gharauni, somewhere it is called Adhikar Abhilekh, somewhere it is called Property Card, somewhere it is called Malmatta Patra, somewhere it is called Residential Land Lease. The names are different in different states, but these are certificates of ownership. In the last 5 years, these ownership cards have been given to about 1.5 crore people. Now today, in this program, more than 65 lakh families have received these ownership cards. That is, under the ownership scheme, about 2.25 crore people of the village have received permanent legal documents of their houses. I congratulate all of them, give my best wishes. And because of today’s program, those who have now received their government papers related to the land, how can they take advantage of it, you will definitely get ideas from the conversation I just had.

Friends,

In the 21st century world, there are so many challenges like climate change, water shortage, health crisis, epidemic. But there is another very big challenge in front of the world. This challenge is of property rights, authorized papers of property. Many years ago, the United Nations did a study on land property in many countries of the world. This study revealed that in many countries of the world, people do not have permanent legal documents of property. The United Nations has clearly stated that if poverty is to be reduced, then it is very important for people to have property rights. A leading economist of the world has written an entire book on the challenge of property rights. And in this book, he says that the little property that people have in villages is dead capital. That is, this property is a kind of dead property. Because the villagers, the poor people, cannot do any transaction in exchange for that property. It cannot help in increasing the family’s income.

Friends,

India was also not untouched by this big challenge facing the world. Our situation was also the same. You also know that despite having property worth lakhs and crores of rupees in the villages of India, it was not worth that much. The reason was that people often did not have legal documents of their houses, so there were disputes regarding the ownership of the house. In many places, powerful people would occupy the houses. Without legal documents, even the banks would stay four steps away from such property. This was going on for decades. It would have been good if the previous governments had taken some concrete steps in this direction, but they did not do much in this direction. Therefore, when our government was formed in 2014, we decided to deal with this challenge of property papers, no sensitive government could leave the people of its village in such trouble. And we want everyone’s development, we also want everyone’s trust, our minister Rajiv Ranjan ji explained it very well. Therefore, we started the Swamitva Yojana. We decided that with the help of drones, mapping of the land of houses will be done in every village of the country, villagers will be given papers of their residential property.

Today, when we are seeing the benefits of this scheme, it gives us satisfaction that we were able to work for the poor of the village. I was just talking to the beneficiaries of the Swamitva Yojana. How this scheme has changed their lives, how they are now getting help from banks on their property. You had property, you lived there but there were no papers, the government should have solved that problem and that is why we took up the work and are doing it and I was seeing in their talks the satisfaction on their faces, the happiness, the confidence, the dreams of doing something new, how enjoyable this conversation felt to me, I consider this a great blessing.

Brothers and sisters,

There are more than 6 lakh villages in our country. Nearly half of these villages have been surveyed by drones. After getting legal documents, lakhs of people have taken loans from banks on the basis of their houses and their properties. With this money, they have started their own small business in the village. Many of these are small and medium farmer families. For them, these property cards have become a big guarantee of economic security. Our Dalit, backward and tribal families were the most troubled and affected by illegal encroachments and long disputes in the court. Now, with the availability of legal proof, they are getting relief from this crisis. It is estimated that after the property cards are made in all the villages, the way for economic activity worth more than Rs 100 lakh crore will open. You can imagine how much capital is going to be added to the country’s economy.

Friends,

Today our government is trying to bring Gram Swaraj on the ground with full honesty. With the ownership scheme, the planning and implementation of village development are now improving a lot. Today we will have clear maps, we will know the populated areas, so the planning of development work will also be accurate and we will also get relief from the wastage and obstacles that used to happen due to wrong planning. There are many disputes about which land belongs to the Panchayat and which land is pasture. Now, by getting property rights, the problems of the Gram Panchayats will also be solved and they will also be able to become economically strong. There are incidents of fire in the village, floods, landslides, and many such disasters. By getting property cards, disaster management will be better, it will be easy to get a proper claim in case of disaster.

Friends,

We also know that there are many disputes about the land of farmers. There are difficulties in getting land documents. One has to go to the Patwari again and again, and have to make rounds of the Tehsil. This also opens the way for corruption. To reduce these problems, land records are being digitized. Ownership and Bhu-Aadhaar – these two systems are going to become the basis for the development of villages. Land has also been given a special identity through Bhu-Aadhaar. About 23 crore Bhu-Aadhaar numbers have been issued. With this, it is easy to know which plot belongs to whom. In the last 7-8 years, about 98 percent of land records have been digitized. Maps of most lands are now available digitally.

Friends,

Mahatma Gandhi used to say- India lives in villages, the soul of India is in villages. The realization of this sentiment of Pujya Bapu has been done in the last decade. Most of the more than 2.5 crore families who have received electricity in the last 10 years are from villages. Most of the more than 10 crore families who have received toilets in the last 10 years are also from villages. Most of the 10 crore sisters who have received Ujjwala gas connections live in villages. More than 12 crore families who have received tap water in the last five years are also from villages. Most of the more than 50 crore people who have opened bank accounts are also from villages. More than 1.5 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have been built in the last decade, and they are mostly in villages, serving the health of the people of the villages. For so many decades after independence, our villages and crores of people in the villages were deprived of such basic facilities. The families of our Dalit, backward and tribal society were the most deprived. Now these families have benefited the most from all these facilities.

Friends,

Unprecedented efforts have been made in the last decade to ensure good roads in villages. In the year 2000, when Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the Prime Minister, the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana was started. Since then, about 8.25 lakh kilometers of roads have been built in villages. 8.25 lakh kilometers in so many years…. Now you see, in 10 years, we have built almost 4.75 lakh kilometers, that is, almost half of the roads in the last 10 years. Now we are also running the Vibrant Village program to increase connectivity to remote villages located on the border.

And friends,

Not only roads, providing internet to villages has also been our priority. Before 2014, less than 100 panchayats of the country were connected with broadband fiber connection. In the last 10 years, we have connected more than 2 lakh panchayats with broadband fiber connection. Before 2014, there were less than one lakh Common Service Centers in the villages of the country. In the last 10 years, our government has built more than 5 lakh new Common Service Centres. And these are not just figures, with these figures, facilities have reached the villages, modernity has reached. The facilities that people used to see in cities earlier, are now available in the villages. This is not only increasing facilities in the villages, but also economic strength.

Friends,

2025 has also started with big decisions for the villages, for the farmers. The government has decided to continue the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. Under this, till now, farmers have received claim amounts of about 1.75 lakh crore rupees, insurance money has been received. Another decision has also been taken regarding DAP fertilizer, whose prices have increased a lot in the world. The government has again made arrangements of thousands of crores of rupees, so that farmers keep getting cheap fertilizers. In the last decade, about 12 lakh crore rupees have been spent to provide cheap fertilizers to the farmers. This is almost double the amount compared to the decade before 2014. Under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi, about three and a half lakh crore rupees have reached the accounts of farmers so far. This shows the commitment of the Central Government towards farmer welfare.

Friends,

Women power has a very big role in building a developed India. Therefore, in the last decade, we have kept the empowerment of mothers and daughters at the center of every major scheme. Schemes like Bank Sakhi and Bima Sakhi have given new opportunities to women in villages. The Lakhpati Didi Yojana has made more than 1.25 crore women in the country Lakhpati Didis. The Swamitva Yojana has also strengthened the property rights of women. In many states, the names of wives have also been included in the property cards along with the husband. At some places, the first name is the wife’s, while at other places it is the second name, but it has been done with the participation of both. Most of the houses given to the poor under the PM Awas Yojana have also been registered in the name of women. And it is such a pleasant coincidence that the drones of the Swamitva Yojana are also helping in giving property rights to women today. Drones are doing the mapping work in the Swamitva Yojana. With the Namo Drone Didi Yojana, the sisters of the village are becoming drone pilots. They are helping in farming with drones and are earning extra income.

Friends,

With the Swamitva Yojana, our government has given such a capability to the people of the village that can completely transform the rural life of India. If our villages and our poor are empowered, then our journey towards developed India will also be pleasant. Due to the steps taken in the interest of villages and the poor in the last decade, 25 crore people have defeated poverty. I am confident that with schemes like Swamitva, we will be able to make villages strong centers of development. Once again, best wishes to all of you. Thank you!
texts.pms-address-at-the-inauguration-of-cosmo:
My Greetings to everyone!

Governor of Karnataka, Sudha Yadav Ji, Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar Ji, my Cabinet colleague, Nirmala Sitharaman Ji, Minister in the State Government, Basavaraj Rayareddy Ji, my colleague in Parliament, Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar Ji, all the scientists, researchers, teachers, other distinguished dignitaries, and my dear brothers and sisters of Mysuru.

First of all, I respectfully bow to Tai Chamundeshwari. I am very happy to be here in Mysuru once again. Just a few months ago, I had come among you for the inauguration of the Viveka Smaraka. And today, we have gathered here to dedicate the COSMOS Planetarium to the nation. Both these occasions convey a profound message about India’s values and our culture. Viveka Smaraka inspires us to look within ourselves and seek spiritual knowledge. At COSMOS, on the other hand, our eyes are lifted towards the sky. We are inspired to explore this vast universe and understand its mysteries. This is an example of how the traditions of spirituality and science in India have always progressed side by side.

Friends,

Our ancestors used to study the sky very closely. They understood the movements of stars and planets, prepared calendars and calculated the timings of solar and lunar eclipses. India was home to many great astronomers such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Nilakantha Somayaji. The advanced instruments and technologies that are available today did not exist at that time. Despite this, they made great discoveries and carried out even the most difficult calculations.

Friends,

Mysuru has a tradition of establishing institutions that encourage the pursuit of knowledge. The University of Mysore was established during the reign of Maharaja Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. The Wadiyar family also played an important role in laying the foundation of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru. These institutions have provided generations of students and researchers with opportunities to advance. And today, when India is achieving one milestone after another in the field of science, Mysuru, too, is adding a new chapter to India’s scientific journey in the form of this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium. Today, this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium is being dedicated to the youth and the people of the country. It is India’s first LED Dome Planetarium. I have just had the opportunity to watch a show here. It was a remarkable experience in itself. I congratulate the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, the University of Mysore, various government departments and everyone associated with its construction. I extend my congratulations to the nation on this occasion.

Friends,

For a long time, there has been a call in our country, which Nirmala Ji mentioned in her speech just now – Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan. Atal Ji added Jai Vigyan to it, and then I added Jai Anusandhan as well. The India of the 21st century is moving forward with this very vision. And our country’s youth are performing exceptionally well in this regard. Last year, India hosted the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics in Mumbai. Our young people participated in it with great enthusiasm. And this year, for the next edition of the same Olympiad, five students from India went to Vietnam. Four of them won gold medals and one won a silver medal. This is a matter of pride for the entire country.

Friends,

Our young students are also performing remarkably well in other fields of science. This year, Indian students achieved major successes in the International Olympiads as well. These included subjects such as Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology. All the students won either gold or silver medals. This has been a record achievement for India. This means that when our youth get opportunities, when they receive the necessary resources to learn, and when they get the support of technology, tools and institutions, they demonstrate their ability to achieve great things. This COSMOS Planetarium, too, is now going to help them greatly in giving shape to their dreams.

Friends,

Technology is changing the world very rapidly today. And no country can afford the risk of moving slowly in this area. Over the past decade, India has made unprecedented progress in astronomy, astrophysics and the space sector. We have installed new telescopes in the country. In several challenging areas of space exploration, India has today become one of the few countries in the world. Through Chandrayaan-3, ISRO made India the first country in the world to land near the Moon’s South Pole. In the form of Aditya-L1, India has received its first solar observatory in space. Just last year, India became the fourth country in the world to demonstrate the capability of docking and undocking in space.

Friends,

During this period, an Indian also reached the International Space Station and conducted several new experiments. The experience gained from this mission is also proving useful for our own human spaceflight programme, Gaganyaan.

Friends,

Our government opened up the space sector. This created new opportunities for the private sector. India’s startups also got an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities. Today, our youth are launching their own rockets, placing satellites into orbit and undertaking many such activities in the space sector that had never been carried out in India before. This is the scientific approach of a New India, where new discoveries are being encouraged, new technologies are being developed and new opportunities are being created for our youth.

Friends,

India has always moved forward with the mantra of Humanity First. India’s space missions, too, have been dedicated to the welfare of humanity. For example, ISRO has developed a satellite communication system for our fishermen brothers.

With the help of this system, when boats equipped with receivers are at sea, officials can send timely alerts to them during storms. And they can also track their safe return to the shore.

Friends,

Many of you must be checking the live location of trains. This tells you where a train has reached and when it is expected to arrive at a station. This information is provided by the Real-Time Train Tracking System developed by Indian Railways and ISRO. Similarly, satellite data is also used in the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. Under this, information collected from fields, along with satellite data, is used to estimate crop yields. Farmers’ insurance claims are being determined on the basis of these estimates. This means that today, our satellites are reaching the heights of space, while at the same time, they are being used to improve people’s lives on Earth.

Friends,

Science for Society- this is our approach. We are continuously promoting research and innovation in the country. More than one crore students have so far benefited from the country’s over 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs. These labs provide children with opportunities to work on their ideas, conduct new experiments and innovate.

Friends,

To advance research, it is essential that our students and researchers have access to the world’s best research. With this objective, we launched One Nation One Subscription. It is now greatly helping the country’s educational and research institutions gain access to leading scientific journals from around the world. We established the Anusandhan National Research Foundation. Through this, we are helping an increasing number of universities undertake new research.

Friends,

Last year, we also launched a Research, Development and Innovation Scheme worth Rs. 1 lakh crore, so that our country’s researchers continue to receive adequate funding. This is helping take new technologies out of laboratories and bring them to practical use.

Friends,

Today, a strong ecosystem for science and research is taking shape in the country. Curiosity among young people is essential for making progress in the field of science. Planetariums and science centres play an important role in nurturing this curiosity. I urge everyone associated with COSMOS to work in this area so that schools and colleges here can organise visits for as many students as possible, and arrangements can be made to bring them here. The children who come here to learn about the universe may well be among those who return here one day and tell us about the new discoveries they have made about the universe. And that will be the greatest achievement of this COSMOS Planetarium. With this confidence, I wish you all the very best for the journey ahead. I extend my best wishes to all of you. Thank you very much.
texts.pms-address-at-the-laying-of-the-foundat:
Greetings to My Brothers and Sisters of Bengaluru! Governor of Karnataka, Sudha Yadav Ji, Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar Ji, Minister in the State Government, Krishna Byre Gowda Ji, and my colleague in the Lok Sabha, who have sent a brilliant young leader from Bengaluru, Tejasvi Surya Ji, other distinguished dignitaries present here, ladies and gentlemen.

This is the first occasion on which I have had the opportunity to share the stage at a programme with our Governor, Sudha Yadav Ji. Perhaps the people of Karnataka are not yet fully familiar with her. But I would certainly like to speak about her life. What does service to the nation mean? What does dedication to the nation mean? We can learn this from the life of Sudha Ji and her family. When the Kargil war was being fought, her husband was martyred in the war. Even after that, in the memory of her husband, she has continued to uphold her resolve to serve Mother India and has been working with a spirit of service to this day. Having served in Parliament for many years, she guided the nation on several important issues. And today, from the land of Karnataka, she is contributing towards the happiness, peace and prosperity of the people of Karnataka. I extend my very best wishes to Sudha Ji.

First of all, I respectfully pay my obeisance to Annamma Tai, the presiding deity of Bengaluru, and to Nada Prabhu Kempegowda Ji. This day is going to give a new impetus to the development journey of Bengaluru and Karnataka. Projects worth more than Rs. 15,000 crore, related to connectivity and energy security, are being launched from here today. From projects related to metro and railways to initiatives for energy security, all these projects will give new strength to Karnataka’s infrastructure.

Friends,

Infrastructure plays a very important role in the development journey of any country. Better connectivity creates new opportunities for progress, employment and industries. And when these opportunities for development reach every section of society, the fight against poverty also becomes stronger. As a result, around 50 crore citizens of the country have come out of extreme poverty in recent years. The projects being launched today will also take this development journey forward. They will give a new impetus to the development of a Viksit Karnataka and, through a Viksit Karnataka, to the creation of a Viksit Bharat. They will also further strengthen Bengaluru’s identity as a tech city. I extend my very best wishes to the people of Karnataka for all these projects.

Friends,

Just a short while ago, the new Pink Line of Bengaluru Metro was dedicated to the people of Bengaluru. With this new metro line, connectivity to IIM Bengaluru and several educational institutions will become even better. In addition, many areas that are known as major business, technology and commercial centres of Bengaluru will also be connected by the metro. This means that lakhs of people in Bengaluru will not only have greater convenience in commuting, but will also save both money and time.

Friends,

Yesterday was the death anniversary of the late Anant Kumar Ji. He had a special attachment to this region. Seeing this metro line today, his soul too must have felt delighted. I pay my heartfelt tributes to him.

Friends,

Bengaluru is India’s Silicon Valley. It accounts for more than one-third of the country’s IT exports. This city is a major engine of India’s innovation and economic growth. Therefore, the rapid development of the entire Bengaluru region and the expansion of modern public transport are major priorities of the Central Government. With this vision, the Central Government is supporting the expansion of Namma Metro. In 2014, Namma Metro was only seventeen kilometres long. Today, its total network has grown to more than 100 kilometres. We are continuously scoring centuries. Shivakumar Ji, I was telling you: you may have heard a few days ago that India scored a century in Grandmasters Chess. India now has 100 chess grandmasters, and they have emerged during this very period.

Friends,

After Delhi-NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Bengaluru has become the third city in the country to have a metro network of over 100 kilometres. This success of Namma Metro is not limited to just one project. It is the result of the country’s new approach towards ease of living and ease of travel. It is the outcome of the country’s commitment to improving the lives of middle-class families.

Friends,

Today, Indian Railways is leaving behind the old mindset of the era of slavery. The country’s Railways is now creating a new heritage, a new legacy. Our railway stations, our railway engines and our railway coaches – everything now bears India’s own imprint and identity. Vande Bharat trains and Amrit Bharat Stations are a glimpse of the railway services of Viksit Bharat. More than sixty railway stations in Karnataka, including Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road stations, have also now become Amrit Bharat Stations. These stations reflect both sensitivity and modernity. Special facilities are available for every passenger, including senior citizens and persons with disabilities. An effort is being made to provide the same facilities at railway stations to poor and middle-class families that were earlier available at airports.

Friends,

Over the past 10–12 years, India’s railway budget has increased several times over. During this period, as Tejasvi Ji has just mentioned, Karnataka’s railway budget has also increased ninefold. Even today, Karnataka has received four Amrit Stations and two projects relating to doubling and electrification. A few days ago, Karnataka received its first Vande Bharat Sleeper train, and today Karnataka has received a Vande Bharat train connecting it with Goa. Through this train, people in Karnataka, including those in Mangaluru and along the entire coastal route, will get a new experience of travelling by a semi-high-speed train.

Friends,

Along with connectivity, energy security also plays a major role in the creation of Viksit Bharat. The ongoing war around Iran and the Gulf countries has shown how important energy security is. This has also been a challenging time for India. However, the steps taken over the past decade towards energy security have helped us face this crisis with strength. We have increased our capacity to produce petrol, diesel and LPG; developed arrangements for storing crude oil; expanded solar, hydro and wind energy; achieved almost 100 per cent electrification of the Railways; and strengthened public transport such as the metro. The three projects whose foundation stones have been laid or which have been inaugurated in Karnataka today will also give new strength to India’s energy security. The LPG project in Mangaluru will increase the country’s LPG storage capacity by 80,000 metric tonnes. The Devanagundi Marketing Terminal will make the supply of petrol, diesel and aviation fuel more organised and reliable. Meanwhile, the CBG plant in Bengaluru will produce around 13 tonnes of biogas every day. This will improve waste management and also save the money spent on importing natural gas.

Friends,

An important aspect of energy security is electricity generation. Today, India is moving forward with the goal of leadership in new technologies, from chips to ships, and from AI and data centres to quantum computing. Continuous efforts are also being made to ensure that the country has adequate electricity for this purpose. Today, India’s renewable energy capacity has crossed 300 gigawatts. To achieve clean energy, India is also increasing the number of its nuclear power plants.

Friends,

Because of the schemes of the Central Government, today the citizens of India are becoming producers of electricity along with being consumers of electricity. Under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, more than 60 lakh families across the country have installed solar plants on their rooftops. These include more than 40,000 families in Karnataka as well. The Central Government has provided assistance of around Rs. 80,000 to each family. To every family. Similarly, under the PM-KUSUM scheme, arrangements are being made for irrigation through more than 8 lakh solar pumps for farmers in Karnataka. This means that the food providers of Karnataka are now also becoming energy providers. These schemes are reducing electricity expenses, while also creating new opportunities for income and employment.

Friends,

When a country moves forward with a mission, when every citizen becomes a part of development, and when the resources contributed by taxpayers are properly invested in development, the results are also encouraging and meaningful. In 2014, we began our work with the resolve of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas. Today, as a result of these very efforts, the middle class is expanding in the country, and a new Aspirational Class is emerging. This is a section of society whose aspirations are growing. It wants a refrigerator and a washing machine for its home. It wants a scooter or a motorcycle for its family. It wants to provide better education, nutrition and healthcare facilities to its children. It wants to spend on tourism and have new experiences. These growing aspirations are creating new demand in the country. From automobiles to electronics, and from tourism to the services sector, new industries, factories and employment opportunities are emerging. In other words, this neo-middle class is becoming a major engine of growth for India’s economy. The interests of this neo-middle class, which is present in large numbers in Karnataka and Bengaluru as well, are among the priorities of the Central Government.

Friends,

The Central Government is continuously working to increase the savings of the middle class and put more money in their hands. We have exempted annual incomes of up to Rs. 12 lakh from income tax. By changing the TDS rules, we have provided relief to senior citizens and those earning rental income. Through the next-generation GST reforms, we have made everyday goods cheaper. By removing GST on personal health and life insurance, we have made insurance more affordable.

Friends,

Our effort is to increase the savings of the middle class, strengthen its purchasing power and enable it to fulfil its family’s dreams while also contributing to the country’s economic progress. The event being held in Karnataka today will also give a new impetus to this development journey. I extend my very best wishes to all of you for the new projects. Thank you very much to all of you!
texts.pms-address-in-the-golden-jubilee-celebr:
My Greetings to Everyone!

Hon’ble Governor of Karnataka, Sudha Yadav Ji, Sarkaryavah of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and our guide, Shri Dattatreya Hosabale Ji, President of S-VYASA, H. R. Nagendra Ji, Vice-President, Dr. R. Nagarathna Ji, Chancellor, H. R. Dayananda Swami Ji, Vice-Chancellor, Manjunath N. K. Ji, Member of Parliament, C. N. Manjunath Ji, Mayor of Miryang City, South Korea, other distinguished dignitaries present here, ladies and gentlemen!

Today, here in Bengaluru, I have the opportunity to experience the extraordinary energy of yoga. This land of Karnataka has been a centre of yoga for centuries. Many great yoga teachers and scholars were born here and have also enriched the tradition of yoga. We all know that the legendary Kannada cinema actor, Dr. Rajkumar Ji, was also among those who practised yoga and contributed to the world of art as well as to the field of yoga.

Friends,

Amidst this great legacy of Karnataka, the 50-year journey of Prashanti Kutiram is an extraordinary and unprecedented saga of service and dedication, which every Indian should know about. How an ordinary yoga centre transformed into such a large movement is, in itself, a source of inspiration.

Friends,

On this occasion, several new facilities have also been launched. I extend my best wishes to the S-VYASA family for these initiatives as well. I also congratulate all of you and the millions of practitioners associated with Prashanti Kutiram on its Golden Jubilee.

Friends,

Along with the Golden Jubilee of Prashanti Kutiram, we are also celebrating the birth centenary of the revered H. V. Seshadri Ji this year. I pay my respectful tributes to him. Seshadri Ji devoted his entire life to advancing the mission of ‘Nation Building through Individual Development’. He understood that if the country was to be taken to the pinnacle of success, it required dedicated, capable and disciplined citizens. Seshadri Ji devoted himself wholeheartedly to preparing such individuals. The goals he pursued while serving in the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh continue to inspire crores of Swayamsevaks even today.

Friends,

Whenever we remember him, the first image that comes to mind is his simple personality. Dattaji has just described his simplicity in such wonderful words. Such a towering personality, such vast experience, and yet such humility in his conduct! To remain in the background while encouraging others to move forward, to bring people together and prepare them for the nation—this was the great discipline of his life. During conversations, he would often cite an example. He used to say that we should learn from the conduct of a mother. Just as a mother stays awake throughout the night to serve her child, nurtures the child and works selflessly for the child, if we extend this very sentiment to society, imagine how much society would benefit.

Friends,

With the same selflessness as a mother, Seshadri Ji remained devoted to serving society. And I have been fortunate to receive his affection and guidance continuously. The memories of the time spent with him and his words remain invaluable to me even today.

Friends,

There is another thing that Seshadri Ji used to say which I can never forget. He would say that if we give to society with both our hands, society gives back to us with millions of hands. I have personally witnessed this principle bearing fruit time and again in my own life. While serving the people, the Janata Janardan, the people have always showered their blessings upon me, and this is one of the greatest assets of my life.

Friends,

We also see the same spirit of service in Seshadri Ji’s family. Dr. Nagendra Ji and Dr. Nagarathna Ji are carrying forward his mission through their work. I appreciate all their efforts and extend my congratulations to them as well.

Friends,

When the country was shackled by the chains of colonial rule, millions of freedom fighters were fighting for independence on one hand, while on the other, great sages of the nation like Swami Vivekananda were awakening India’s spiritual consciousness and showing the path of yoga to the youth of India.

Friends,

The inspiration drawn from sages like Swami Vivekananda gave rise to institutions such as Prashanti Kutiram. Here, an initiative was undertaken not only to connect yoga with the masses, but also to conduct new research by putting it to the test of modern science. This institution has not merely produced yoga practitioners; it has also prepared trainers and philosophers for society. These teachers, doctors and researchers are serving people across the country and the world through yoga. S-VYASA, which evolved from Prashanti Kutiram, has become an important institution in the fields of yoga education, scientific research and healthcare services. Along with yoga, you have also developed a holistic wellness ecosystem comprising facilities related to Ayurveda, naturopathy and modern medical science. The research work undertaken in areas such as stress-related challenges and lifestyle diseases has served the entire world. I commend Prashanti Kutiram for these efforts.

Friends,

Over the past 12 years, India has been presenting its culture, identity and knowledge systems to the world with complete confidence, and I say this with a sense of responsibility, with complete confidence. One outcome of this is that, at India’s initiative, the entire world now celebrates International Yoga Day. On the occasion of Yoga Day, programmes related to yoga are organised across the world, from Australia to Africa and America. Crores of people participate in them. Today, in many countries across the world, yoga has reached our schools, institutions and workplaces. For instance, in Saudi Arabia, yoga has been recognised as a sporting activity. The Sports Ministry there has entered into an agreement with India’s Ministry of AYUSH to promote yoga. We are continuously witnessing examples of foreign nationals promoting yoga. And I have personally experienced this. Wherever I travel across the world, during lunch or dinner, when I sit with foreign guests or Heads of State, there is hardly any lunch or dinner where yoga does not come up in the conversation. Earlier, I had to explain to them that I am not a yoga expert, but a practitioner. I then tell them about its various benefits, and they ask numerous questions. I have met many world leaders who tell me that their wives visit India once a year to learn yoga and teach yoga there. Some tell me that their daughters are learning yoga, while others say that their daughters have dedicated themselves to yoga. In the families of some of the world’s most prominent Heads of State, there is someone or the other associated with yoga. This shows how far India has reached through yoga. It seems that yoga has become a gateway to understanding India. I have also seen foreign nationals, whether from the Royal Family of Qatar or from elsewhere, who are completely dedicated to yoga.
