India has also honoured many such individuals with the Padma Shri, thereby enhancing their prestige.

Friends,

As people across the world become more familiar with yoga, their curiosity to know India also grows. A new attraction develops towards our culture and traditional knowledge systems. This opens up a new avenue of engagement between India and the world. And all this has been made possible through our collective efforts. If I talk about Ayurveda, more than 150 Ayurveda training courses have been recognised in different countries across the world. Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) have been signed with 28 countries to facilitate cooperation in the expansion of Ayurveda.

Friends,

Our endeavour is to ensure that the benefits of Ayurveda and yoga reach every citizen of the country. Today, holistic healthcare has emerged as a new global movement. As a result, there is a natural attraction towards Ayurveda and naturopathy.

And friends,

When there is such excellence and enthusiasm all around, alongside promoting and propagating yoga, we have also made several changes to rules as per the requirements. In India, Yogasana has also been recognised as a competitive sport. New opportunities have been created for Yogasana in events such as Khelo India and the National Games. These changes are very significant for India. Just a few days ago, an international yoga competition was held in Ahmedabad. And I was amazed. When I visited Uzbekistan, they had secured the number one position in the world, and they had gathered all the winners and gold medallists there, who were citizens of that country. This shows that wherever I go, I see and meet people, yoga has become a subject of discussion everywhere. This has also opened up avenues for those associated with yoga to participate in competitive events.

Friends,

Just as with yoga, the Government of India is continuously promoting Ayurveda as well. There are many things in our country that do not receive the attention they deserve, even from well-informed people, including those who have an interest in these subjects. After so many years of independence, for the first time, a separate Ministry of AYUSH was established in the country. We have encouraged research related to Ayurveda and patents based on Ayurveda. And today, we are witnessing the results of these efforts. Exports of AYUSH and herbal products from India are continuously increasing. The economy associated with the AYUSH sector has grown to several lakh crore rupees. Our turmeric which Indian families have been using for generations in their food habits and household traditions, is now witnessing growing demand across the world. India is exporting turmeric in quantities that were once beyond imagination. Its exports have been continuously increasing. We have also established the National Turmeric Board to give a new impetus to the production, quality and exports of turmeric.

Friends,

We must also share the benefits of our ancient sciences and modern research with humanity and also realise the opportunities associated with these fields for our youth. With this objective, the Government has introduced the facility of an e-Ayush Visa. This is making it easier for people from abroad to come to India for treatment. The World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Centre for Traditional Medicine has been established in Jamnagar. Through this centre, research and international cooperation in traditional medicine are being promoted.

Friends,

Today, 140 crore citizens of the country are working continuously with a shared goal. And that goal is to build a Viksit Bharat! The latest World Bank report has given a new impetus to this mission. The World Bank report states that over the past 12–13 years, nearly 50 crore Indians—this is a very significant figure—have been lifted out of extreme poverty. New opportunities for a better life now lie ahead of these millions of families. The possibilities of adopting a healthy lifestyle and paying attention to their family’s health have increased. Our endeavour is to make a healthy lifestyle a priority for every family. Yoga can play a very significant role in this, and I always say that yoga liberates us from diseases, and yoga also liberates us from indulgence. Moreover, it is the most effective health remedy that comes at zero cost. Prashanti Kutiram is part of this mission, and several new initiatives are also being undertaken by the institution. It has also been extending its support. Their contribution has been very valuable to this work. Therefore, I would like you to start preparing a roadmap for new goals from now onwards. Since I have come here, I will also entrust Dr. Nagendra Ji with a few tasks before I leave. Dr. Nagendra Ji has, in fact, written to me in a letter just a few days ago that he feels younger than ever before. And therefore, his youthful energy will benefit Prashanti Kutiram as well as the nation. However, I would like you to ensure that when Prashanti Kutiram completes 75 years, the country would have become a Viksit Bharat. So, keeping this vision of a Viksit Bharat in mind, start planning now for what your next 25 years should look like, and dedicate yourselves to this mission, so that the path you follow also contributes to strengthening the nation, and your journey towards the 75th year of Prashanti Kutiram, your next 25-year journey, also becomes a source of strength for a Viksit Bharat. I urge you all to think in this direction. With this conviction, I once again extend my congratulations to all of you on the Golden Jubilee celebrations. I also once again bow in reverence at the feet of the revered Seshadri Ji. Thank you very much to all of you!
texts.pms-address-at-the-kisan-tak-bharat-agri:
You also have my heartfelt greetings on this sacred festival of Diwali, and with the programme of Chhathi Maiya also approaching, I extend my very best wishes for that as well. My greetings to all of you.

Chairman and Editor-in-Chief of the India Today Group, Shri Arun Puri ji, the agricultural scientists, agri-entrepreneurs, farmer friends, and all distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen who have come from across the country for this programme.

First of all, I wholeheartedly congratulate the India Today Group for this innovative initiative. When the country launched the cleanliness campaign, the India Today Group participated in it very enthusiastically. Now you have organised this Kisan Mela, and dedicated two full days to it. This is a very positive beginning. I congratulate all of you. And Arun ji speaks such excellent Hindi, so double congratulations for that.

Friends,

This event is taking place at a time when the country is in a festive mood. Two or three days ago, we celebrated the festival of Diwali, and now the spirit of the Chhath Mahaparva is all around us. The festival of Chhath is deeply connected with agricultural life, and in our country, most festivals are linked with farming and agriculture. Bihu, Pongal, Onam, Baisakhi, Sarhul, Pola, many such festivals are connected with agriculture. In other words, farming is our culture, our tradition, and the foundation of our social life.

Friends,

From the Red Fort, I had spoken about the seven streams of strength for a Viksit India, and among these, agriculture is a principal stream. Building a Viksit India is simply not possible without developing agriculture, without making farming smarter, and without empowering farmers. That is why the importance of such farmer conferences becomes even greater.

Friends,

You can understand the relationship between farming and the country’s progress through two important facts. Recently, a World Bank study on poverty was released, and it is being discussed across the world. It states that within just 12–13 years, 50 crore poor people in India have defeated poverty. It also states that poverty has declined very rapidly in villages. This means that a large number of small farmers and agricultural labourers have overcome poverty. Now look at the coincidence. During the past decade, India’s agricultural growth rate has remained above 4 percent. This is the first decade after Independence in which the country’s agriculture sector has achieved an average growth rate of more than 4 percent, for the first time since Independence. And during this same period, a large number of poor people in villages have defeated poverty. But unfortunately, people trapped in angles and agendas of news coverage fail to notice this achievement of the country.

Friends,

Those engaged in farming and experts connected with agriculture know how necessary continuous change in agricultural policies and methods is. Those who governed for decades became satisfied merely because the country’s farmers had filled the grain warehouses of the nation. But what did farmers receive after that? Merely filling grain warehouses is not enough. Over time, the world changed, markets changed, people’s needs changed, eating habits changed, the weather changed, and technology changed. Along with these changes, we needed to empower our farmers in a new way. But earlier, even this was not given attention.

Friends,

Over the past decade, the country took steps to match this pace, and the results are before all of us. Today, India exports agricultural products worth more than four lakh crore rupees every year, and this money is increasing the income of our farmers. Today, India is number one in the world in milk production. Today, India is number one in pulse production. India is number one in jute production. India has also become number one in rice production. It is number two in the world in wheat production. It is number two in the production of cotton, fruits, and vegetables. It is number two in fish production, and India is also the world’s largest producer of millets. These are not just statistics. They show how much the capability of India’s farmers has grown.

Friends,

One more thing is necessary for the prosperity of India’s farmers. It is necessary that they do not remain dependent only on traditional crops such as wheat, rice, and sugarcane. I repeat, farmer brothers should not remain dependent only on wheat, rice, and sugarcane. Therefore, the government is also placing emphasis on other crops and other activities related to agriculture. Let me remind the India Today Group of something. The word “revolution”, kranti, is something the India Today Group is particularly fond of. Therefore, I am now going to talk about a few revolutions.

Friends,

There was a time when the country took a historic step towards self-reliance in food grain production through the Green Revolution. After that, the White Revolution made India the world’s largest milk producer. Today, I will give you some more figures that show how this journey is now moving forward with remarkable momentum. Over the past decade, India’s milk production has increased by nearly 70 percent, 70 percent. Egg production has also increased by nearly 90 percent, 90 percent. And if we talk about the Blue Revolution, India’s fish production has more than doubled in a decade. New opportunities have emerged in the field of beekeeping through the Sweet Revolution. Honey production has increased from around 80 thousand tonnes to 150 thousand tonnes. In horticulture as well, India’s production has increased from 280 million tonnes to more than 350 million tonnes.

Friends,

When we connect all these revolutions with a broader vision, multiple sources of income are created for the country’s farmers, and this is very essential for the future of agriculture. Let me give you another example. Another revolution, the solar power revolution. This revolution has transformed the food provider into an energy provider. Under the PM-KUSUM Scheme, nearly 12 lakh solar pumps have already been distributed. This is reducing farmers’ electricity bills, and farmers have also begun earning income by installing solar plants on their fields. Along with production, we have also focused on productivity and on farmers’ profits.

Friends,

Recently, I completed 25 years as the head of government. When I was the Chief Minister of Gujarat, I was continuously working to modernise agriculture even then. At that time, I started large agricultural festivals. I remember that in May and June, in temperatures of 40–45 degrees Celsius, hundreds of agricultural scientists, agricultural experts, and progressive farmers would come together. We would prepare Kisan Raths and travel in them. We would go to villages and to fields. We would visit farmers’ fields and interact directly with them. What type of soil the area had, what the availability of water was, which crops could perform well there, what kind of farming was required, every such issue would be discussed directly with farmers. Our effort was that the knowledge present in scientists’ laboratories should directly reach farmers’ fields. In other words, we moved forward with the concept of Lab to Land, and Gujarat’s farmers benefited greatly from it.

Friends,

The experience from my Gujarat days has been extremely useful after coming to the central government. In 2014, there were only a few hundred soil-testing laboratories in the country. Today, their number has increased to more than 8,400. Just as pathology laboratories are expanding in medical science, today soil-testing laboratories are expanding. Today, there are more than 750 Krishi Vigyan Kendras across the country. We are also prioritising the protection of animals from diseases. To protect livestock from Foot and Mouth Disease, more than eight crore farmers’ animals have received free vaccinations. During COVID, we provided free vaccines, and everyone remembers that. But this is Modi; he provides free vaccines even to animals.

Friends,

Often, some people with old ways of thinking believe that the use of large-scale technology will not be possible in our villages. The Namo Drone Didis have proved such people wrong. Once, while speaking with all the Drone Didis through video conferencing, I was talking to a daughter from a village, perhaps in Jharkhand. She told me, “Now my status has changed.” I asked, “Why?” She said, “The entire village calls me a pilot, and even my younger brothers-in-law call me ‘Pilot Bhabhi’.” Just imagine how much self-respect increases. At present, the Namo Drone Didis are using drones for spraying fertilisers and pesticides. Now the scope of their use is also being expanded.

Friends,

Today’s India is also expanding the role of engineering in agriculture. Our agricultural scientists, engineers, and youth are together developing such tools and machines that are reducing the cost of farming. In some places, machines are being developed that are making sowing and harvesting easier. And I would especially like to urge the people from industry present here, those engaged in manufacturing equipment for farmers, as well as our startup founders, that whatever equipment you build from now on should be powered by solar energy, because we are taking solar power to every farm. Just as the whole world has now rushed towards electric vehicles, I am in favour of making every type of agricultural tool solar-powered. And I am also making considerable efforts in that direction. But I would urge all MSMEs and small-scale industries to focus on this. This is going to become a very large area of revolution. Not only that, sensor-based equipment equipped with AI technology is now being developed that can provide precise information to farmers and can be affordable even for the smallest farmers. Arrangements are now being developed for soil testing through mobile phones. You simply place a little soil on the mobile-based device, and your phone immediately provides a report identifying which crop your soil is suitable for, how much fertilizer is required, and what type of fertilizer is needed. In other words, just see how rapidly change is taking place. Today, from agricultural engineering to agri-startups, India is full of opportunities. We must transform our food providers into agri-preneurs, that is, agricultural entrepreneurs. Work is now progressing rapidly across the country on how value addition can take place right where production happens.

Friends,

In the past few years, small farmers, working together with the government, have built a large network of 10,000 FPOs, that is, Farmer Producer Organizations. These are turning groups of small farmers into value creators and connecting them with the food-processing business. I clearly remember one incident from my days in Gujarat. In Gujarat, we introduced the Jyotigram Yojana. We separated agricultural feeders from domestic feeders and began supplying as much electricity to farmers as possible. This greatly benefited farmers. There are some villages near Gandhinagar where most people cultivate chillies. But farmers there faced a problem. If production increased, prices would fall, and if production declined, earnings would decline. They suffered in both situations. If too many chillies were produced, they could not sell them. But after the arrival of electricity through the Jyotigram Yojana, they started converting chillies into red chilli powder. They packaged that powder, got advertisements made, printed photographs of personalities on the packaging, and began selling chilli powder on a large scale. Through this value addition, they became highly successful earners. Earlier, they could not even obtain a proper price for their chillies, but now their products became brands. This shows what becomes possible when attention is given to every small aspect. Efforts to connect small farmers with export markets are also progressing rapidly.

Friends,

Our policy and our intent are absolutely clear. It is our priority that farming should not become a burden on farmers. To ensure affordable fertilizers for farmers, the country has spent ₹16 lakh crore over the last 12 years. Friends, this is an enormous figure. Sixteen lakh crore rupees is more than the annual budget of many countries. Amid the war currently taking place around Iran and the Gulf countries, a bag of DAP fertilizer that costs ₹5,000 is being made available to Indian farmers for only ₹1,300. A bag of urea that costs ₹3,000 in the international market is being provided to Indian farmers for less than ₹300.

Friends,

I would like to mention one more subject, and I have spoken about this before as well. For your network, what I am about to say today is exclusive.

Friends,

When the war situation in West Asia was escalating, the price of crude oil rose from 70 dollars to 122 dollars per barrel within just a few weeks. At that time, India also faced a major challenge. India was in a situation where diesel prices should have been increased by at least ₹50 per litre. An increase of ₹50 per litre had become necessary. At that time, the government took a decision in the interest of farmers. We decided that the full burden of the shock in international markets would not be passed on to citizens and farmers. The government increased diesel prices by only ₹7 per litre, whereas the required increase was ₹50. The government itself absorbed a burden of ₹43 per litre. In neighbouring countries as well, diesel prices had increased by 40 to 50 percent. But that did not happen in India. Since then and up to today, the government has been bearing a loss of ₹14,000 crore every month. Every month. Yet we did not allow harm to come to the country’s farmers. When the welfare of farmers is the highest priority, when there is a spirit of Citizen Devo Bhava, such sensitive decisions are taken.

Friends,

Amid so many discussions about the national interest, I am sure the people of Aaj Tak must be wondering that no negative headline has emerged so far. So perhaps now we should discuss something that can become a headline. Until now, I have been talking about the country, and perhaps that has not attracted as much media attention. So now let me talk about controversy.

Friends,

Nowadays, some people pull the Constitution out of their pockets. The country understands very well what they are doing. They seem to think that the nation’s Constitution and democracy are sitting in their pocket. Even while not being in power, they remain intoxicated with the mindset of power. But when these very people were in power, what were their actions like? Let me narrate a small incident.

Friends,

You may remember that there was a time when people in the media used to rank the best-performing states. In one such ranking related to the economy, Gujarat was ranked number one, and at that time I was the Chief Minister of Gujarat. The institution that gave Gujarat the number one ranking was named after a former Prime Minister of India. That hint is enough; you can find the name yourselves. This ranking was based on research conducted by some of the country’s most respected economists. But the people sitting in power in Delhi did not like Gujarat receiving that recognition. They formally instructed those conducting the research that things could not continue this way. They said that from then onward, no report could be published without their approval first.

Friends,

That was the situation then, and today those very people go around delivering lectures on tolerance and democracy. And when exactly did this happen? What happened after that? You can research and find those details yourselves. Let me now move towards concluding my remarks.

Friends,

Without doubt, the achievements of the country’s farmers over the past years have been remarkable. To build a Viksit India, we now have to expand our efforts even further. We must create a future where farmers are prosperous, villages are prosperous, and agriculture is modern and profitable. I am confident that the deliberations taking place here will benefit the country. The government will also work upon the best suggestions and solutions that emerge from here. And since I have come among you today, I would certainly like to make one appeal. At the beginning, Anjana ji said in her introductory remarks that farmers are connected to two things: the food provider and Mother Earth. I want to ask my farmer brothers and sisters: are we really protecting this Mother Earth of ours? Ask yourselves honestly. The way we are destroying Mother Earth through excessive use of chemicals, and we are her children. We are killing this mother before our own eyes. If we do not wake up in time, if we do not make efforts to save Mother Earth, then the mother who nourishes us today may one day leave our hands. Such a situation could arise. That is why the government has emphasized natural farming. Those who have experimented with natural farming have achieved great success. A single cow can provide sufficient manure for natural farming on 30 acres of land. No chemical inputs are required. Many such subjects must have emerged during your discussions today. Therefore, I appeal to all farmers that we should move towards chemical-free farming. I am not talking about organic farming; I am talking about natural farming, and every farmer can adopt it easily. We can take steps to save our soil by becoming free from chemicals. One challenge with our farmer brothers and sisters is that until they see something with their own eyes, they do not accept it. No matter how many long speeches are delivered, farmers do not simply accept something. They believe only after seeing it. Otherwise, all that stays in their minds is that they must apply the yellow powder, use the green bottle, use the green container, bring the red container, and if the neighbour uses two bags, they will use two bags too; if the neighbour uses four sacks, they will use four sacks too. This is the responsibility of all of us, and especially of progressive farmers, to free them from this mindset. We must help them move towards chemical-free natural farming. The first task is to save our Mother Earth. This mother is capable of providing everything we need. She will never let us feel any shortage, provided we protect her. We are the children of Mother Earth. It is our duty to fulfil this responsibility as her sons and daughters, as the children of Mother Earth. With this confidence, I extend my best wishes to all of you. I also congratulate the India Today Group. You have undertaken a task that will greatly help the nation in the years ahead.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-speech-during-interaction-with-the-s:
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

My dear countrymen,

Today, crores of Indians across the country and in every corner of the world are celebrating the sacred festival of lights. People are travelling from far and wide to reach their homes. It is a great festival of meeting and spending time with family and loved ones. And I too have come among you to celebrate Diwali. Whether on the borders or within the country, all of you who defend the nation, all of you who stand guard over the nation, all you brave sons and daughters of Mother India, are my own people, a part of my family. From Kargil in the lap of the Himalayas to Lepcha, from Sir Creek on the seashore to INS Vikrant in the embrace of the sea, every Diwali spent with our brave soldiers has been memorable for me.

My brave soldiers,

This time, I have come to celebrate Diwali in the forests of Bastar, among all of you. This is the land where Naxalite terror once held sway, and because of your sacrifice, dedication, and perseverance, that very land has now been freed from the scourge of Naxalite terror and has begun a new journey of development.

And friends,

This Diwali of 2026 is truly special. After forty or fifty years, such a Diwali has arrived for all of you. This is the first Diwali when the country has won its decades-long battle against Naxalism and Maoist terror. This is the first Diwali when every district of the country is free from Naxalism. This is the first Diwali when crores of citizens have overcome the fear of Naxalism. This is an extraordinary achievement. A very large share of the credit belongs to you, to lakhs of brave personnel like you, to our soldiers, sons and daughters, and security personnel. Therefore, today I have come to celebrate Diwali with you. And I have also come to express, on behalf of 140 crore Indians, gratitude for your sacrifice, dedication, and spirit of service.

Friends,

Our visionary ancestors said: “Abhyantaram bhayam rakshyam, asaram bahyato bhayam.” This means that when a nation’s internal security is strong, external enemies cannot do much harm. But when internal security weakens, external enemies also begin to raise their heads. Therefore, the role that our armed forces play on the borders is the same role that all of you security personnel play within the country. You have made countless sacrifices for the unity and integrity of the nation. You have shown limitless dedication. The security forces engaged in preserving internal security, our CRPF, CoBRA, BSF, ITBP, every single jawan, the SSB, IRB, the police personnel of the states, the commandos of special forces such as the Bastar Fighters, and our women fighters, this nation is indebted to all of you for your service. Crores and crores of citizens are proud of you. With this feeling of gratitude and affection, I extend my heartfelt Diwali greetings to every one of you, wherever you are standing guard. I also convey my greetings to our soldiers deployed on the borders for the defence of the nation.

Friends,

This battle against Maoist terror and Naxalism was not easy. There was a time when more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states of the country were affected by Naxalism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill in these areas. It became impossible to step outside one’s home. These Naxalites had even snatched away the people’s right to vote. Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh, a very large part of the country was affected by Left-wing extremism. Thousands of villages and crores of people were trapped by it. There were as many as two thousand Naxalite attacks in a single year. Just remember, in 2010, nearby in Dantewada, 76 CRPF personnel were martyred in an encounter with Naxalites. In the same year, another incident in Dantewada claimed the lives of 44 innocent civilians. This land was consecrated by the blood of our brave men. But not a single cry of grief was heard from those privileged leaders living in their palaces. Not even a single tear emerged from their eyes. Such attacks occurred repeatedly. This cycle continued for decades. During this period, more than one thousand security personnel sacrificed their lives in Chhattisgarh alone. Many soldiers lost their arms and legs in IED blasts. If you look at the figures from 2004 to 2013, every year more of our brave soldiers were martyred than the number of Naxalites eliminated. The leaders of Naxalite organisations considered this their victory and celebrated it. And unfortunately, the governments of that time had accepted Naxalism as an incurable disease and simply left it unattended. My tribal families were left to survive on their fate. It had been accepted that this would continue endlessly, bullets would keep flying, soldiers would keep dying, and innocent citizens would keep suffering.

Friends,

No nation can function with an attitude of “this is how things will continue.” To move a nation forward, its enemies must be crushed with determination, courage, and a clear strategy. The political will that was lacking in the country for this task was restored in 2014. You gave this Pradhan Sevak an opportunity to serve Mother India. And after 2014, we saw both the situation and the statistics begin to change. For years, discussions revolved around the number of security personnel being killed compared to the number of Naxalites. But after 47 years, for the first time, not a single CRPF jawan lost his life during duty over the past year. This is the victory of the country’s correct policies and firm resolve. This is the victory of your bravery, your courage, and your restraint. I repeat, this is the victory of your bravery, your courage, and your restraint.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Victory to these brave soldiers.

Our security forces and police personnel remained steadfast even in the most adverse circumstances. This is the victory of that devotion to duty.

Friends,

Success requires the right intentions and the right policies. For national security, we took one tough decision after another. Many such steps were also taken that are still not known to the public. Through these decisions and efforts, a major blow was dealt to the funding networks of Naxalites and separatists. The nexus of fake currency was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply chain. As a result, the supply of weapons stopped, and restrictions were imposed on the movement and recruitment of Naxalites.

Friends,

Previous governments had also tied the hands of the security forces fighting on the ground. Naxalite attacks kept taking place, but the security forces did not have the freedom to retaliate decisively. We gave the security forces the freedom to take every necessary decision. We also worked to stop the support that Left-wing extremism used to receive from certain people sitting within the government and the system.

Friends,

We were pursuing a very large goal. Our goal was that no mother’s lap should be left empty, no family should be trapped in a cycle of destruction, no child should pick up weapons and walk the path of violence, and no young person’s future should be ruined. Therefore, until this goal was achieved, we continued to work with determination. There was no publicity, no display. Working with sensitivity, we broke the backbone of Maoist terror. Through a spirit of service, we transformed lives in Naxal-affected regions. That is why people who had suffered from Naxalism also stood firmly with the government and the security forces. Even here today, there are citizens present who contributed greatly to this major victory. I express my gratitude to all of them as well.

Friends,

When we work with the spirit of Nation First, the country’s peace and security are ensured, the nation reaches new heights of development, and the participation of every poor and deprived citizen in development also increases. Therefore, over the past twelve years, the country has not only won the fight against Naxalism and separatism, but it has also won a major battle against poverty.

Friends,

Just before Diwali this year, a piece of news emerged that is being discussed across the country and around the world. A few days ago, the World Bank stated in its report that in India, over the past twelve years, fifty crore people, fifty crore people, have risen out of extreme poverty. What decades of slogans about removing poverty could not achieve, the country accomplished in just twelve years. Just imagine how great an achievement this is. Think about how it became possible.

Friends,

During Diwali, we create rangoli designs. At first, only a few lines are drawn, and the initial patterns appear small and separate. But as one small part after another comes together, a beautiful and complete picture emerges. Over the past twelve years, something similar has happened in India. We created a rangoli of welfare schemes that continuously empowered the poor. Through the Jan Dhan Yojana, crores of people became connected to the banking system. Through the PM Awas Yojana, crores of families received permanent homes. Under the Mudra Yojana, we provided loans without collateral. Through the SVANidhi Scheme, street vendors also received support and opportunities to expand their businesses. Under Ayushman Bharat, we provided free healthcare to the poor. Crores of families received free food grains every month. Policies were created for children’s education. In other words, we ensured free medicine, free education, and free kitchen support for every poor family. Not only that, schemes such as the Swachh Bharat Mission and Har Ghar Jal removed many basic concerns of daily life. As a result, crores of people have come out of poverty today. Families to whom poverty was once passed on as an inheritance are now inheriting the foundation of a better future. Families whose entire lives were spent in anxiety now have the confidence that comes from trust in the government and a renewed sense of self-belief.

Friends,

A major foundation of this victory against poverty is also linked to the country’s fight against Naxalism and separatism. The people of Bastar and all of you know that wherever Naxalites held influence, their first agenda was to stop development and harm the lives of ordinary people. Schools for children were not allowed to function and were often set on fire. Hospitals for the sick were not allowed to be built, and doctors were prevented from entering. Facilities such as medical stores, which help save lives, were not permitted. These Naxalites even prevented children from receiving polio vaccinations. They did not allow mobile towers to be installed. You have seen for years how railway tracks were blown up with bombs and how industries and businesses were prevented from functioning. And the result was that lakhs of poor and innocent citizens, my brothers and sisters, and my young brothers and sisters, remained deprived of opportunities. Their lives never escaped the cycle of poverty. Therefore, when we began the fight against Naxalism, we simultaneously launched special campaigns for the development of Naxal-affected regions. We built more than 15,000 kilometres of roads in areas affected by Left-wing extremism, with complete security arrangements. More than 9,500 mobile towers were installed in these regions. Around 175 Eklavya schools were opened for the education of tribal children. Nearly 50 Industrial Training Institutes were established to connect youth with employment opportunities. Around 50 Skill Development Centres were created. Thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs were opened. The PM Janman Yojana was launched for the development of the most backward tribal regions. Through this, facilities such as water, electricity, and roads reached thousands of remote villages for the first time. Not only this, surrendered Naxalites were also given an opportunity. Special schemes were created for their rehabilitation.

Friends,

This campaign of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas” has given the country’s fight against poverty new energy and new confidence. That is why, on one hand, 50 crore people have come out of extreme poverty, and on the other hand, Naxalite violence has also come to an end in the country. Just look at Bastar itself. Today, the Bastar Olympics is being held in Bastar. Children are no longer picking up guns; they are trying their hands at sports.

Friends,

Amid these achievements, we must remember one more thing. The Naxalites have been eliminated, but the danger has not completely disappeared. Armed Naxalites have vanished from the forests, but intellectual Naxalites have captured many organisations. Even today, they are provoking people against the Constitution and democracy of the country. These intellectual Naxalites have also infiltrated several political parties and various organisations. We must identify them, defeat them, and secure the nation.

Friends,

Today’s achievements inspire us, but they are not a pause. I say again, they are not a pause. These victories, these successes, are platforms for a new flight. This flight will carry the dreams of the nation, dreams that our generations have cherished for centuries. These will be the dreams of those freedom fighters who made countless sacrifices for independence. These will be the dreams of those brave soldiers who laid down their lives for Mother India on the nation’s borders. These will be the dreams of those courageous personnel who sacrificed their lives in the fight against Naxalism and terrorism. Every day, you live by this spirit: “May your glory remain eternal, Mother. May your glory remain eternal, Mother. Whether we live for a few more days or not, May your glory remain eternal, Mother.” Now is the time for this spirit of yours to transform into a new confidence. Now is the time to live for the nation and to take the nation to new heights.

Friends,

Whatever resolve our nation takes, it also possesses the capability to fulfil it. We had promised that we would remove Article 370 from Kashmir, and we fulfilled that promise. We had promised that we would build toilets in every household, and we fulfilled that promise. We had promised to expand the scope of vaccination, and we fulfilled that promise. Therefore, when we speak today about eliminating poverty, when we speak about a drug-free India, a narcotics-free India, when we speak about a Developed India, when we speak about a Self-Reliant India, these goals too will certainly be achieved. We must witness these dreams becoming reality before our very eyes. I have faith in you. I have faith in the youth power of my country. I have faith in the people of my nation. The country will certainly reach these goals. Your sacrifice and hard work will become the strong foundation of the grand edifice of a Developed India. With this faith, I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on the occasion of Diwali. Thank you all very much.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-speech-during-interaction-with-india:
My colleagues in the Cabinet, Shri Mansukh Mandaviya ji and Smt. Raksha Khadse ji, all representatives of the Paralympic Committee of India and the National Sports Federations, other distinguished guests, all medal-winning athletes, ladies and gentlemen.

I had been eagerly waiting to meet all of you. Just a few weeks ago, I met the athletes who participated in the Asian Games, and now I have got the opportunity to meet all of you energetic companions who participated in the Para Asian Games. Your outstanding performance shows that India is rapidly emerging as a major power in the world of sports. On such a large platform, you have not only won medals, but you have also won the hearts of crores of Indians. Once again, all of you para-athletes have demonstrated that the highest flights are achieved through determination and courage. On behalf of 140 crore countrymen, I congratulate all of you wholeheartedly.

Your families, trainers, and coaches have also played a crucial role in this achievement. I congratulate them as well. And as I have said before, the amount of effort a coach has to put in for an athlete is immense, but for a Paralympic athlete, many times more effort is required. Only then do such remarkable results emerge. Therefore, I extend special congratulations and appreciation to them.

Friends,

There was a time when India’s participation in most sports was considered merely a formality. In para-sports too, the country was far behind. At the 2010 Asian Para Games, India won only one gold medal. Altogether, we managed to win just fourteen medals in that tournament. Fourteen. This time, however, our athletes have returned with one hundred and fourteen medals. Just think about this journey from fourteen to one hundred and fourteen. It is the result of the highest level of your hard work. It is the outcome of your dedication to sports and the ecosystem that has developed around it. This time, with thirty golds, thirty-five silvers, forty-nine bronzes, five new world records, and nine Asian records, you have filled the entire nation with pride. Out of fifty-six women athletes, thirty-four daughters became medal winners. And in four events, all three podium positions belonged to India. India won the gold, and in the same event, India also won the silver and the bronze. Even on the last day of the competition, you performed wonders by winning nine gold medals. It seemed as though you had decided that as long as the Games continued, the medal-winning streak would not stop.

Friends,

This time, our athletes won gold medals in disciplines where India had never achieved such success before. Mona Agarwal created a world record in para shooting. Honey broke his own previous world record. Himanshu, Ravi, and Jehan showed the world through their performances how physical challenges can be overcome.

Friends,

Whether it is the personal achievement of an athlete or the collective success of a nation, the world sees only the shine of victory. But the years of hard work behind that moment, the sweat shed day and night, and the unwavering dedication and perseverance required to reach that point are what form the foundation on which the towering structure of success stands. For example, Rinku ji lost her mother just two months before the Asian Para Games. Even amidst such great sorrow, she maintained her courage. And when she won the gold medal, she raised her mother’s photograph and dedicated that medal to her. That moment touched the hearts of all Indians.

Friends,

Your struggles and achievements are an inspiration to every Indian. And in this journey, your path and the nation’s path have been very similar. That is why today, your efforts and the efforts of the nation are combining and creating an even greater force together.

Friends,

After 2014, when the country began its journey towards bigger goals, the situation was very different. Most parents were afraid to send their children into sports and the children themselves were often hesitant. There was disorder in the system, a lack of resources, a lack of support, and a lack of transparency. People used to say that nothing could change in such a system. They had accepted it as a reality. But just as you never accepted defeat before any challenge, the country too kept its eyes fixed only on its goals. We resolved that we would not allow the talent of our youth to go to waste. Therefore, we decided to change the very system that prevented young people like you from moving forward. As a result, a new approach towards sports emerged. Today, if a young athlete has faith in his or her talent, that athlete also believes that the country stands with them. Our para-sports ecosystem itself is one of the biggest examples of this. In sports where India’s representation was once extremely limited, our presence is now growing stronger. In archery, athletics, shooting, swimming, table tennis, badminton, judo, powerlifting, and many other sports, new young athletes are emerging. We are discovering new champions. This time, sixty-one of our athletes participated in the Asian Para Games for the first time. Sixty-one completely new athletes. And among those first-time participants, thirty-six returned home with medals. Sandeep even created a world record in his debut itself. This participation of young athletes reflects the India of today and announces the India of the future.

Friends,

We do not view sports merely as a collection of national and international events. For us, sports are also a powerful medium for character-building and nation-building. It is sports that teach young people how to win after losing. Sports teach discipline and the meaning of team spirit.

Friends,

With this vision, we are building a modern sports ecosystem for the country. Campaigns are being run at schools and at the grassroots level. A large number of Khelo India Centres have been established. We also launched the TOPS Scheme so that athletes could receive Olympic-level training. Keeping the Olympics in mind, I called upon young people from the Red Fort this time to come forward through the Talent Hunt campaign.

Friends,

Para-sports are being given equal importance in all these efforts. As a result, athletes like you are emerging with excellence and bringing glory to the nation at major events. We saw this once again in the recently concluded Para Games. In this competition, athletes receiving support under TOPS won forty-one medals, while Khelo India athletes won nineteen medals. This shows that our efforts are moving in the right direction.

Friends,

Today, modern sports policies in India are creating many new opportunities for young people, even beyond the playing field. Sports infrastructure development, sports equipment production, and the sports broadcasting economy are all expanding rapidly.

Friends,

Just a few days ago, the government approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme worth more than ₹1,800 crore. Now it is time for our sports goods manufacturing industry to achieve new milestones. When an Indian or foreign athlete steps onto a field anywhere in the world, their sports gear should also be Made in India. Their clothing and footwear should also be Made in India. We want India to produce not only world-class athletes but also world-class sports equipment. We want Indian sports products to reach markets across the world. This will strengthen India’s MSME sector and create new opportunities in small towns and rural areas.

Friends,

After today’s event, all of you will also be invited to schools, colleges, and various institutions, where young people will want to listen to you and learn from you. When you speak with them, teach them the secrets of winning on the field, but also tell them about the opportunities connected with sports beyond the field. And you should also explain to them the extensive efforts being made by the country to make life easier for our differently-abled brothers and sisters. Just a few days ago, the Cabinet took an important decision regarding pensions for persons with disabilities. We increased the pension amount. The disability benchmark that was previously 80 percent has been reduced to 40 percent. Earlier, a person had to be eighteen years old to become eligible for a pension. Now, the path for pensions has been opened even for eligible children with disabilities from birth. Similarly, significant efforts have been made to promote Indian Sign Language. A sign language dictionary containing more than ten thousand words has been developed. School textbooks are also being made available in sign language. Through the Accessible India Campaign, public places are being made more accessible for persons with disabilities. Our effort is to ensure that every differently-abled person in the country receives both dignity and equal opportunities, and is able to move forward in life on the strength of their own abilities.

Friends,

The podium at Aichi-Nagoya is not the final destination of your journey. Keep that in mind. You should use this success as a launching pad for even bigger goals. The next target for India, and for most of you athletes, is L.A. 2028. Avani and Manish have already secured their quota places for Los Angeles. Our goal should be to ensure that as many Indian athletes as possible participate in L.A. 2028 and bring home as many medals as possible. Therefore, celebrate this moment wholeheartedly, but also begin preparing for the next challenge right away. The country stands with you, and so do I. The entire nation is waiting for your next victory. Once again, many congratulations and best wishes to all of you.

The grand festival of Diwali has already begun. This time, celebrate Diwali with great pride, enthusiasm, and splendour. But along with celebrating Diwali, also set your next goal in your mind and move forward with a new resolve. My very best wishes to all of you.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-address-during-lays-foundation-stone:
Governor of Maharashtra Shri Jishnu Dev Varma ji, Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet Shri Manohar Lal ji, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde ji, Smt. Sunetra Ajit Pawar ji, all ministers, Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assembly, other public representatives, and my dear brothers and sisters of Pune!

Diwali is just around the corner. First of all, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on the occasion of Diwali!

Friends,

The joy of festivals becomes even greater when a new facility is added to people’s lives. Today is such a happy occasion for the people of Pune. I am pleased that another line of the Pune Metro is being inaugurated today. Ten years ago, I had the opportunity to lay the foundation stone for the first phase of this project in Pune. With the metro now starting between Hinjawadi and Shivajinagar, one of Pune’s major IT hubs will receive improved connectivity. The new line whose work has commenced today will further strengthen connectivity between the old and new parts of Pune. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the people of Pune and Maharashtra.

Friends,

Pune has always been a centre of ideas that have given new direction to the nation and to society. Today, Pune is also providing direction to the new energy of a Viksit Bharat. From IT, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, startups, innovation, and manufacturing, Pune is a place of dreams and aspirations for the youth of the country. In such a situation, the strengthening metro connectivity here is set to give a new momentum to the development of Pune city.

Friends,

The inauguration and expansion of the Pune Metro demonstrates how we are building cities for a Viksit Bharat. Earlier, a city’s identity was defined by its industries, or by its famous cuisine, fruits, or crops. But today, two more benchmarks have been added to the identity of cities. First, how competitive a city is. Second, the level of ease of living it offers. Metro projects help improve both these parameters for any city. As Pune Metro expands, it is saving time and providing greater convenience to the residents of Pune. And we all know that when a city’s time is saved, its productivity increases. When a city’s productivity increases, the country’s economy gains momentum. And when the economy grows, both the poor and the middle class benefit.

Friends,

Today is also an example of pro-people, proactive good governance. The first metro in our country began operating in 1984. In the thirty years that followed, only 248 kilometres of metro lines were built. Two hundred and forty-eight kilometres. Until 2014, metro services existed in only five cities of the country. Had the same old thinking continued, had the old government remained in place, had the old work culture continued, it would have taken many more decades for the metro to reach Pune. But when the people gave the NDA an opportunity to serve in 2014, we moved forward with a resolve. That resolve was to improve ease of living and ease of transportation for the middle class living in our cities. Today, we can see the results. Over the past twelve years, metro transportation in the country has undergone a complete transformation. From 248 kilometres of metro routes in 2014, the network has now expanded to nearly 1,200 kilometres. From only five cities having metro services in 2014, metro systems are now operating in 26 cities. More than one crore people are now travelling by metro every day. Today, India’s metro network is counted among the top three metro networks in the world.

Friends,

The situation in Maharashtra was similar to that in the rest of the country. When the NDA’s double-engine government was formed for the first time in 2014, Maharashtra had only around 10–11 kilometres of operational metro lines. Today, nearly 175 kilometres of metro lines are in service in Maharashtra. Work is underway on more than 680 kilometres of metro corridors. Today, investments of more than ₹2.5 lakh crore are being made in Maharashtra’s metro infrastructure alone. This money is going into the pockets of workers. This money is generating employment for engineers. This money is creating jobs in shops and factories.

Friends,

This metro project is special for another reason as well. This metro line has been constructed on a PPP model. That is, it has been built through the joint efforts of the government and the private sector. This is a development model whose success will further accelerate the country’s progress.

Friends,

Today, every citizen of India, every young son and daughter of India, is working with full strength to build a Viksit Bharat. Today everyone is confidently saying: We Will Do It. We Will Do It. This spirit exists throughout the country. Over the past twelve years, the nation’s energy has been reflected in village roads, highways, expressways, electrification of new railway lines, long tunnels, and towering bridges. Numerous projects and schemes are taking shape across the country. In the coming years, along with this, the country will devote its energy to making its cities among the best in the world.

Friends,

Our cities are not merely places to live. They are also major centres of economic activity. We must transform hundreds of small cities across the country into growth hubs. It was with this vision that the Urban Challenge Fund was approved in February this year. The central government is providing support of ₹1 lakh crore for this fund. The goal is to attract investments worth many lakh crores of rupees into cities across the country in the coming years. I urge local bodies, our friends in the private sector, and everyone else to come forward. We must all work in mission mode. I am confident that Maharashtra will expand its role further in this effort.

Friends,

There are two additional reasons why India is being discussed throughout the world today. First, India has maintained the fastest growth rate in the world despite difficult global circumstances. Second, within just ten to twelve years, fifty crore people in India have overcome extreme poverty. This fact has emerged in the latest World Bank report. Many generations in the country grew up hearing promises and claims about eradicating poverty. Earlier, the fight against poverty existed only in slogans. Today, India is defeating poverty on the ground.

Friends,

Today, India is the country that is both the fastest-growing economy and the fastest reducer of poverty. These two achievements are interconnected. India’s economy is growing rapidly. India’s budget is expanding. Investments in the people are increasing. The money that earlier disappeared through scams, favoritism, and leakages is now reaching beneficiaries directly. When the nation’s resources are invested in roads, railways, airports, and metro systems, when the government increases investment in electricity, water, and gas pipelines, people’s lives improve and employment opportunities increase.

Friends,

Facilities such as homes for the poor, toilets, tap water for every household, and gas connections have increased people’s confidence and saved their time. And this saved time is being used to earn additional income for their families.

Friends,

Just last month, with your blessings, I completed twenty-five years as the head of government. The motto of our government has always been that when you empower the poor, the poor gain the courage to lift themselves out of poverty. I remember that when I was Chief Minister of Gujarat, I started the tradition of Garib Kalyan Melas with this very thought. These events focused on delivering welfare schemes directly to the poor. Poor citizens were invited onto the stage. They would take a pledge to defeat poverty and return home with renewed confidence.

Friends,

The work that I began twenty-five years ago continues uninterrupted even today. This is what I call Power to Empower. Power to Empower is true good governance. This transformation did not happen overnight. Previous governments grew tired of merely raising slogans. We connected every link. We wove together the dreams of millions of lives. This is the result of years of thoughtful and well-planned efforts. And that is why fifty crore Indians have defeated poverty.

Friends,

When poverty declines, the benefits are not limited to those families that escape it. It injects new energy into the country’s economy. It creates a new middle class. This neo-middle class brings new dreams. Its purchasing power drives markets. New opportunities emerge, from shops to factories. In other words, the reduction of poverty in India is taking the Indian economy to new heights.

Friends,

In this journey towards a Viksit Bharat, our farmer brothers and sisters also have a major role. Therefore, our government is continuously empowering farmers. However, due to adverse weather conditions in Maharashtra, many farming families are facing difficulties at present. Over the past few years, a great deal of work on water conservation has been done under the leadership of Devendra Fadnavis ji. But this natural disaster has created major challenges. I want to assure every farmer brother and sister in Maharashtra that in this difficult time, the NDA government stands firmly with them with full sensitivity and commitment. I am aware of the drought conditions in Maharashtra. The state government has already provided advance assistance as well. I have transferred the PM-Kisan funds. Please do not worry at all. We are standing with every farmer.

Friends,

I would also like to tell the people of the country that this is the season of festivals and celebrations. We must remember our farmer brothers and sisters. We must ensure that the joy of Diwali remains alive in their homes as well. This is also our social responsibility. We must not forget the difficulties faced by our drought-affected citizens, our farmers, and others living in villages. Together, we will face this challenge.

Friends,

Collective effort, united effort, is the lifebreath of a Viksit Bharat. With this spirit, we must remain dedicated to the development of the nation. Once again, my best wishes to all of you for these metro projects. My heartfelt greetings for the upcoming festivals. Thank you very much. People of Pune, repeat after me with full strength, raising both your hands:

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
texts.pms-address-at-the-inauguration-of-bhara:
Union Minister in my Cabinet, Pralhad Joshi ji, Shripad Naik ji, all industry leaders, investors, colleagues from the startup world, senior officials, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen who have come from India and abroad.

I welcome and greet all of you to the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit. This year’s summit is special because it is being held under special circumstances. We have seen how this year has largely been dominated by discussions around energy shocks. The importance of renewable energy in our lives and in our development journey has become even clearer this year. It is also a happy coincidence that the 9th Assembly of the International Solar Alliance is being held alongside this summit. Delegates attending the Fourth Conference on Green Hydrogen are also present here. That means the scale of this year’s event is very large. I extend my best wishes to all of you.

Friends,

Over the past few years, the global economy has witnessed unprecedented crises. From the COVID pandemic to the West Asia crisis, the world has faced several major challenges, and the crisis in West Asia is still continuing. But 140 crore Indians feel proud that we have handled these challenges better than many others, and despite these crises, India’s growth has remained high. Had India not invested in clean energy and not established new systems in this sector over the past decade, our crisis could have been far more severe than that faced by the rest of the world.

Friends,

This global crisis has delivered a clear message to every country: energy security is directly linked to economic security. And we all know that the future of energy security lies in clean energy. If we continue to remain excessively dependent on fossil fuels, the global economy will continue to face repeated disruptions. Fossil fuel reserves are limited and concentrated in only a few regions. Renewable energy, on the other hand, has unlimited potential, and every region and every country can benefit from it.

Friends,

India’s journey in this sector over the past twelve years has been one of promises, passion, and performance. The proof of this is our commitment made at COP-26. At the 2021 Summit, India resolved to achieve 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. We said: We will do it! In our Paris pledge, India had also set the goal of meeting half of its installed power capacity through non-fossil sources. India achieved that target itself in 2025. In other words, we achieved it five years ahead of schedule. Today, more than 50 percent of our installed power capacity is based on non-fossil sources. India is also progressing firmly towards the target of 500 gigawatts. We have already achieved nearly 300 gigawatts. And today, India is among the top three countries in the world in solar and renewable energy. Over the next ten to eleven years, our effort is to add another 500 gigawatts of new non-fossil fuel capacity. This target is somewhat challenging, but I have full confidence in the capabilities of my country. And therefore, I say: We will do it!

Friends,

We want India’s innovations and India’s experiences to benefit all humanity. This is also our approach towards green energy. India’s successes in this field can be useful to many countries around the world. I will explain this through examples.

Friends,

In February 2024, we launched the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. Under this scheme, the target is to install rooftop solar panels on one crore homes. In just the past twenty-four to twenty-five months, more than sixty-five lakh homes have joined this campaign. And as our Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi ji just mentioned, every six days, one lakh new homes become part of this solar movement. The impact of this can also be seen in electricity bills. One study shows that electricity bills for these sixty-five lakh households have fallen by nearly 76 percent. There are lakhs of families whose electricity bills have become zero. There are also many families that are generating surplus electricity and earning income by selling it back to the grid. This scheme can significantly strengthen energy security in many countries, especially in the Global South.

Friends,

India is making solar power a part of the lives of its citizens. Over the past twelve years, we have also tried to connect industries and farms with solar power. More than 44,000 government buildings in India are now connected to solar energy. This is saving nearly ₹700 crore annually. India’s farmers are also benefiting greatly from the KUSUM Scheme. Through it, more than 30 lakh farmers have received access to solar-powered irrigation. It is estimated that every farmer benefiting from a solar pump is saving nearly one lakh rupees every year. Let me also give you the example of the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana. Its concept is to generate electricity by installing solar panels on ponds, lakes, and reservoirs. This allows better utilisation of water bodies. Such projects also reduce the costs associated with acquiring land.

Friends,

Our clean energy ecosystem is not limited only to hydro, solar, wind, and nuclear energy. India is moving in mission mode to take a major leap in the field of green hydrogen. Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, we have set a target of producing five million tonnes of green hydrogen by the end of this decade. We are also connecting our transport sector with green hydrogen. Just a few months ago, India launched its first Green Hydrogen Train.

Friends,

All of you experts know that merely generating electricity is not enough. It is equally important to distribute it efficiently and deliver it where it is needed. In India, solar and wind energy are generated more abundantly in certain regions. We must ensure that areas where power generation is relatively low also benefit from it, so that homes, farms, and industries there can also run on clean power. That is why Green Energy Corridors are being developed. Under these corridors, a dedicated network of transmission lines and substations is being established. This is making it easier to transfer solar and wind power from places of production to places of demand. And in this effort, the contribution of One Nation, One Power Grid has been immense. Over the years, we have integrated five regional grids into a single national network. Today, the entire country is connected through a power grid operating at a common frequency. To further strengthen this Green Energy Corridor system, we have now moved to the next phase. Recently, India set an investment target of nearly ₹2 lakh crore for this purpose.

Friends,

A major reason behind our success in green energy is also our growing manufacturing capacity. Until a few years ago, we were completely dependent on imports even for the smallest components related to solar energy. A decade ago, our solar module manufacturing capacity was only around 2 gigawatts. Today, it has crossed 200 gigawatts. Solar cell manufacturing capacity has also reached nearly 40 gigawatts. We are now expanding the manufacturing of other components as well. In other words, India’s ambitions in green energy are also proof of the success of our Atmanirbhar Bharat mission and the success of the Make in India campaign.

Friends,

India is striving to achieve a great deal within a very short span of time. We cannot stop here. We must connect every government building, every school and college, every hospital, and the entire street-lighting system to solar energy, and we must do so at a rapid pace. I would suggest that healthy competition should be encouraged among states and local bodies, so that those who perform better can be rewarded and others can learn from their success stories.

Friends,

I have a suggestion related to solar power in agriculture as well. We have distributed millions of solar pumps, but we now need to move beyond solar pumps. My vision is that the Annadata should also become an Urjadata – the food provider should become an energy provider. Farmers should install solar panels on unused land. Even the boundaries of fields should not remain unused; solar panels should be installed there as well. We must ensure that this reaches as many villages as possible.

Friends,

This new phase of the solar revolution is not only about adoption; it also depends on innovation. Therefore, I make a special appeal to our startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs: come forward and create models where as many household needs as possible can be met through solar power. We need solutions that make solar power available twenty-four hours a day and in every season. We must move towards a situation where a family can cook food using electricity generated by the solar plant installed on its own rooftop. We need to launch a clean cooking movement. Dependence on imported gas should be reduced as much as possible. We must also create a situation where a larger number of middle-class families have the option of electric vehicles and can charge their scooters, bikes, and cars at home using electricity generated from their own solar systems. This can save middle-class families thousands of rupees every year.

Friends,

We also need products that promote solar power in the dairy sector. Solar-powered equipment should be developed for every activity, from preparing animal feed to harvesting crops and post-harvest operations.

Friends,

None of this will be possible without next-generation innovation. For this, the country needs the necessary hardware. We need indigenous storage solutions. We need to build new battery storage capacity. This is a tremendous opportunity for all of you and for the youth of the country. I urge everyone in the world of research and all investors not to let this opportunity pass by. The solutions you develop in India will serve many countries around the world.

Friends,

India is one of the youngest countries in the world, and every effort in clean energy is creating large numbers of new employment opportunities. Even today, thousands and thousands of people are finding jobs in this sector, and there is tremendous potential for green jobs. These opportunities are being created across different fields, from manufacturing panels and other hardware to installation, servicing, and transportation. In the future, as solar power capacity increases further, just imagine how many more jobs will be created. From kitchen stoves to transportation systems, when everything becomes solar-powered and green-energy-driven, an entirely new industry will emerge.

Friends,

For all of you, for investors across the world, India is opening up enormous opportunities. It is difficult to find elsewhere the kind of demand, scale, and scope that India offers. It is equally difficult to find the kind of political and policy stability that India provides. And we are seeing the results of this. Over the past decade, more than ₹15 lakh crore, that is, 164 billion dollars, has been invested in the renewable energy sector. From the RE-INVEST Summit of 2024 until today, within just two years, investments worth nearly ₹6 lakh crore, that is, more than 63 billion dollars, have come into this sector. It is estimated that by the end of this decade, investment opportunities worth more than ₹20 lakh crore, approximately 220 billion dollars, will be created in this sector. Therefore, a new horizon of opportunities is opening up for all of you in India’s clean energy sector.

Friends,

India has given the world the message of One Earth, One Family, One Future. The same philosophy is reflected in our clean energy journey. This is the thinking behind the International Solar Alliance. Our effort is to ensure that the funding, technology, and expertise required for renewable energy reach every country that needs them. That is why a proposal has been put forward for a 200-million-dollar Africa Solar Facility for Africa.

Friends,

The coming decade is extremely important for our climate goals. And I am confident that everyone present at this summit will play a major role in securing that future. We must connect every country to this mission. Every region must become a participant in this transformation. Only then will we be able to build a clean future, a green future, and a secure future. With these words, I once again extend my heartfelt best wishes to all of you.

Thank you.
texts.pms-speech-during-rashtriya-ekta-diwas:
I will say, “Sardar Patel,” and all of you respond, “Immortal forever, immortal forever.”

Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.

Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.

Sardar Patel – Immortal forever, immortal forever.

My dear countrymen,

Today’s event is somewhat different. Until now, we have always held this programme on Unity Day in the morning. This time, there has been a slight change. We have all gathered in the evening. In the morning, lakhs and lakhs of citizens participated in the Run for Unity with a pledge of national unity. We saw the enthusiasm of the people in the Run for Unity. Yesterday evening, I witnessed magnificent presentations at the Bharat Parv Pavilion. And now, on this national occasion, we are present at the feet of Sardar Patel.

Friends,

This is the world’s tallest statue, the Statue of Unity. The participation of the entire nation in its construction, the unique aura of this place, and the extraordinary energy and inspiration of Unity Day fill one’s heart with pride and gratitude upon coming here. Pride in being a citizen of this great nation, and gratitude towards Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who united more than 550 princely states after Independence. With an iron resolve, he bound this nation together in the thread of unity.

Friends,

Freedom is essential for any nation. When a nation is free, it determines its own future. But freedom receives the right direction through a republic. A republic shows us the path of taking decisions within the framework of the Constitution. The Constitution keeps us accountable to the people. And unity gives us the strength to move forward as one nation. That is why in our country, Independence Day, Republic Day, and Unity Day are all celebrated with great enthusiasm as national festivals.

Friends,

Once again today, in Ekta Nagar, we have witnessed the grand vision of India’s unity. This year’s National Unity Parade has also been extraordinary. This parade is dedicated to the courage and bravery of our police and security forces. Through the tableaux, the nation’s heritage and aspirations have been presented before the country. Therefore, Unity Day is no longer limited merely to official events. Through public participation, it has become a celebration of national pride. On this occasion, I extend my greetings to all countrymen on National Unity Day. I bow with deep reverence at the feet of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

Friends,

Sardar Patel is that great personality in India’s history without whom it is difficult even to imagine present-day India. It was Sardar Patel who shaped the India we know today. Even after Partition, the person who kept India secure from the Himalayas to the Indian Ocean was Sardar Patel.

Friends,

Sardar Patel was able to do this because he understood the character and consciousness of India. He knew that India’s diversity was not its weakness. He knew that India’s diversity was, in fact, the true foundation of its unity. For thousands of years, we have lived in this manner. Through this very strength, we touched the heights of progress and prosperity.

Friends,

Sardar Patel once again laid the foundation of that India. He did not merely shape the geography of the nation; he also bound the country together through emotional unity. Through the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple in Gujarat, he also initiated the cultural renaissance of the nation.

Friends,

This year marks the 75th anniversary of that great work as well. Just as the flag of the Somnath Temple has been flying with pride for a thousand years despite the repeated destruction attempted by aggressors, that same spirit of self-respect inspired us to celebrate the Somnath Swabhiman Parva. And this year, the nation is celebrating that occasion with equal enthusiasm.

My dear countrymen,

Today, these great ceremonies of national unity, India’s rising stature on the global stage, the rapid pace of our economic progress, and the revival of our sacred centres from Kashi Vishwanath to the Ram Temple, all point to the direction in which India is moving. It is a path shown to us by Sardar Patel. And for this, the nation will remain indebted to him forever.

Friends,

Last year, we celebrated the 150th birth anniversary of Sardar Patel. For two years, programmes and celebrations were organised across the country. We took major resolutions for the nation and pledged to fulfil them. And today, as we celebrate his 151st birth anniversary, we can say with satisfaction that the nation has fulfilled those resolutions within a very short period of time. In these two years, the country has achieved several unprecedented accomplishments.

Friends,

On the occasion of Sardar Patel’s 150th birth anniversary, standing here at his feet, I had said, “Until the country is completely free from Naxalism and Maoist terror, we will not rest.” And exactly one year later, as we stand here today, that national resolve has been fulfilled. Today, the backbone of Naxalism has been broken in the country. In 2015, 126 districts of the country were affected by Left-wing extremism. By March 2026, not a single district remained in the country that was still affected by Naxalism. These districts, which suffered for decades from violence and bloodshed, are now becoming part of the mainstream of development. Today, roads are expanding in these areas. Mobile networks are reaching people. Educational and healthcare facilities are increasing. Youth who once faced uncertainty now have new opportunities for education, employment, and progress.

Friends,

This time, at this Unity Day celebration, families from Naxal-affected regions have joined us here as special guests. I welcome all of them and wish them a bright future. Today, I also pay my respects to all those brave security personnel who made the supreme sacrifice to establish peace in these regions of the country.

Friends,

Today, India is more secure than before. Today, India is more determined than before. And one major reason for this is the increased confidence of our citizens. Confidence comes from achievements. Confidence comes from the sensitivity of the government and the system. Today, I would certainly like to speak about one such major national achievement.

Friends,

Talks of removing poverty in India have been going on since Independence. Votes were sought in the name of eradicating poverty. But we all know what the actual condition of poverty in the country was. Those who raised the slogan of removing poverty themselves kept becoming richer. Change in circumstances began to come in recent years. Just a few days ago, a World Bank report was released. The report states that in the ten to twelve years before 2024, fifty crore Indians defeated poverty. That means where earlier 27 out of every 100 people, more than one-fourth of the population, were trapped in extreme poverty, today that number has fallen to less than 3 out of every 100 people.

Friends,

The entire world is acknowledging that this is a major achievement. But how did this happen?
