We have established an Indian Studies Chair in the city of Kraków. Today, we also decided to further strengthen our cooperation in culture and education, as well as in sports and tourism.

Friends,

Today, we also held detailed discussions on regional and global developments. Both India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law. We believe that reforms are necessary to make global governance institutions stronger and more effective.

Whether in Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace

Your Excellency,

Our shared history is deeply rooted in humanity and compassion, while our shared future holds immense possibilities for cooperation in innovation and technology.

I am confident that your visit will give new momentum to the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and take it to new heights. Once again, I extend a warm welcome to you and your delegation.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-address-at-the-vijaya-dashami-celebr:
Victory to Lord Shri Ram!

Victory to Lord Shri Ram!

Victory to Lord Shri Ram!

On this sacred occasion of Vijayadashami, I bow at the feet of Lord Shri Ram, Mother Janaki, and Bajrang Bali. In this holy atmosphere, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all countrymen on Vijayadashami.

Friends,

Today, every corner of India is immersed in devotion to Lord Ram. Village after village, city after city, the nation is absorbed in the spirit of Ramleela. The staging of Ramleelas across the country, the tradition of keeping alive the ideals of Lord Shri Ram, the proclamation of the end of tyranny and terror, and the faith in the eternal victory of truth over falsehood, for us, this is not merely a festival. It is the life force of India. Therefore, today, when every citizen of the nation is proclaiming the victory of righteousness over unrighteousness, come, once again, repeat after me:

Victory to Lord Shri Ram!

Victory to Lord Shri Ram!

Victory to Lord Shri Ram!

Friends,

This nation, its culture, and its ancestors have worshipped Lord Shri Ram for thousands of years. This faith exists not only because Shri Ram brought an end to the demon king Ravana. This faith also exists because Lord Ram gave us ideals that are unparalleled in the history of humanity.

Friends,

Lord Shri Ram faced countless difficulties in his life, yet he never abandoned the path of truth and righteousness. Such was his character: “Prasannatam ya na gata abhishekatah tatha, na mamle vanavasa duhkhatoh.” This means that Lord Ram neither became elated upon receiving the kingdom nor became distressed by the sorrow of exile in the forest. Despite enduring every adversity, he upheld righteousness and established truth. When Lord Ram went into the forest, he embraced Nishadraj and honoured Mother Shabari. He established the highest standards of compassion, kindness, love, and harmony. And when Lord Ram returned and became the king of Ayodhya, he established such a Ram Rajya that even today it is considered the benchmark of good governance. Ram Rajya means a system where there is no discrimination against anyone, where everyone receives justice, where everyone gets equal opportunities, where the purpose of power is not to rule but to serve the welfare of the people. That is why Goswami Tulsidas ji wrote: “Daihik daivik bhautik tapa, Ram raj nahin kahuhi vyapa.” This is the ideal of Maryada Purushottam Lord Shri Ram. Therefore, we must always regard the people as divine and move forward with the mantra of Citizen First. We must place service to the poor and the deprived above everything else.

Friends,

We receive a very great lesson from the life of Lord Ram. No matter how great the crisis may be, no matter how difficult the challenge, we must not sit waiting for others. We must recognise our own strength. We must trust our own resources. We must turn our resolve into power. And we must find solutions through our own hard work. Lord Ram taught us that difficulties on the path cannot stop our journey. The ocean stood before him. Lanka was far away. But the resolve was unwavering. Therefore, Lord Ram awakened the collective strength of the people. He made public participation his support. He united the available resources. And he made a goal that seemed impossible. This is the fundamental mantra of success. Faith in our own strength. Confidence in our own capability. Proper utilisation of our own resources. And unwavering commitment to our goal. Today, we too must move forward with this same mantra. Before us stands the goal of a Developed India. Before us stands the goal of a Self-Reliant India. Through the power of the people and for the welfare of the people, we must fulfil every aspiration of our citizens. And for this too, we must draw inspiration from Lord Ram.

Friends,

A nation progresses only when it possesses self-respect. And heritage plays a very important role in this self-respect. Therefore, today the country is committed to preserving its heritage and identity. For centuries, our treasures were looted and taken abroad. But today, we are bringing those treasures back. In the past twelve years, more than six hundred and fifty ancient idols have been brought back to India. Similarly, India is giving new global recognition to its cultural centres. In recent years, many of our sites have been added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. Last year, even Diwali was included by UNESCO in the list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. This is the result of the collective willpower of millions of Indians. We must continue to work with the same dedication.

Friends,

Vijayadashami is the festival of victory. It is the festival of triumph. This festival gives us the courage to believe that no matter how powerful the enemy may be, when we stand with truth and humanity, victory ultimately belongs to us. This spirit of Vijayadashami has always been India’s guiding philosophy. Our sages inspired us: “Samano mantrah samitih samani, samanam manah saha chittamesham.” This means that our thoughts should be united, our councils should be united, and all institutions of the nation, all political parties, should stand together in the national interest. We must move forward with this spirit. We must unite against the enemies of the nation. Those forces that attack the honour and dignity of the country, those who divide society, and those who harbour hatred towards our culture, are enemies of the nation. On this auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami, we must once again renew our resolve. We must identify the enemies of Mother India. We must defeat them. And, taking the pledge of Nation First, everyone must come together. I am confident that the vision we expressed during the Pran Pratishtha ceremony of the Ayodhya Temple, “From Ram to Nation” and “From Divinity to National Duty,” will certainly be fulfilled. I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all countrymen on Dussehra.

Jai Siya Ram!

Jai Siya Ram!

Jai Siya Ram!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-address-during-interaction-with-the-:
Union Minister for Sports Shri Mansukh Mandaviya ji, Minister of State for Sports Sister Raksha Khadse ji, all of you young athletes, coaches, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.

Coming among all of you fills me with energy as well. So many medal winners gathered together, and meeting all of them at once, is no ordinary thing. It is a very pleasant feeling. All of you young athletes are examples of how, when passion is transformed into victory, it brings not only medals but also a glow on the face. And, of course, it makes the nation shine as well.

Friends,

You have given 1.4 billion countrymen an opportunity to feel proud. Because the greatest achievement, if there is one, is to enhance the honour of the Tiranga. You have enhanced the pride of the Tiranga, you have increased its honour. Therefore, your success is not yours alone; it is the success of millions and millions of citizens of this country. On behalf of all the people of India, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you. At the same time, I also wholeheartedly congratulate your coaches, your support staff, and your families.

Friends,

Today is also the birth anniversary of our former President, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. His life and his vision are an inspiration to all of us. I respectfully pay tribute to him as well.

Friends,

In many ways, these Asian Games have been memorable for us. Both our men’s and women’s hockey teams are present here today. Both teams won gold medals this time. And especially our women’s hockey team, you ended a long wait of 44 years by bringing home the gold medal. In cricket, both our teams won medals for the second consecutive time and, in fact, repeated their own record. In kabaddi too, both our men’s and women’s teams won gold medals. Likewise, five gold medals in archery, and where there are five, there is the grace of the Almighty. Outstanding performances in shooting, major successes in boxing and wrestling, new records in athletics, a medal in weightlifting after twenty-eight years, and India’s success in marathon events for the first time since 1982. All this is truly a matter of great joy.

Friends,

I especially want to appreciate our daughters. Out of the 85 medals won by India, 38 medals were won by our women athletes. Among them were 11 gold medals as well. And these medals are not merely numbers; they represent a powerful image of New India. Today, India is winning medals even in sports where, in the history of the Asian Games, we had never before won a medal. In Mixed Martial Arts, Soft Tennis, and certain sailing events, our players created new history by winning medals for the first time.

Friends,

Now we must reach even greater heights in sports. We have to, don’t we? We have to achieve even more, don’t we? I want to place a few resolutions before you. And all of you must respond with full enthusiasm: We will Do it! So, repeat after me:

The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!

The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!

A new identity for India in sports, We will Do it!

New champions in every sport, We will Do it!

More records in our name, We will Do it!

Friends,

The stadium in which we are gathered today is named after Major Dhyan Chand ji. His dedication towards hockey was so great that he would practise for hours even at night. His hard work repeatedly reminds us that resolutions and dreams are not fulfilled in a single day. They require years of patience and sustained effort.

Friends,

Over the past 12 years, India too has worked with great patience and dedication on its sportspersons and its sports ecosystem. There was a time when India could win only a handful of medals in major tournaments. In many sports, people in the country did not even know that such sports existed. There used to be huge events such as the Olympics, yet India had no representation in more than half of the sports. Just think about it. If we do not even compete, then where will the medals come from?

Friends,

We took a pledge that we would remove this pessimistic mindset. And the result is that today, our representation is increasing on every global platform.

Friends,

How did this transformation happen? It happened through the same spirit that helped you achieve success. Over the past 10–12 years, the country worked continuously with dedication and sincerity, pursued a long-term vision, and built a transparent and modern ecosystem for sports. As all of you know, we launched the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). We launched the Khelo India Scheme. Over time, its scope was expanded further. As Mansukh Bhai mentioned earlier, more than ₹36,000 crore has been allocated for expanding Khelo India and strengthening sports federations.

Friends,

Today, more than one thousand Khelo India Centres have been established across the country. Stadiums, mini-stadiums, and multi-purpose sports halls have been created. Athletics tracks, football grounds, hockey grounds, swimming pools, and thousands of such sports infrastructures are being built in both small and large cities. Under this scheme, direct assistance is being provided to athletes as well. They are being given Out-of-Pocket Allowances. Under the TOPS scheme, athletes receive ₹50,000 per month. If any sport requires training abroad, the government is facilitating it and providing financial assistance.

Friends,

To ensure that young people get maximum opportunities to play and compete, events such as Winter Games have been launched, and Members of Parliament Sports Competitions have been started. The country created a new Sports Policy and a new Khelo Bharat Policy. Our para-athletes are also enhancing the nation’s pride through their talent and capabilities. For them too, better opportunities and modern facilities in sports are being ensured. And that is why every athlete today feels confident that the nation stands beside them throughout their journey. And when an athlete feels that support, what they can achieve for the nation is something all of you yourselves are excellent examples of.

Friends,

This time, many players in Team India at the Asian Games were only 15 to 17 years old. At such a young age, they enhanced the nation’s pride through their outstanding performances. They won the hearts of the people of the country. This shows that age is no barrier to success. In fact, in sports, starting young is an added advantage. That is why our effort is to identify sporting talent from an early age. We are giving special focus to identifying talent among children aged five to fifteen and training them properly. In the coming years, thousands of new athletes will receive opportunities through Khelo India and Emerging Khelo India programmes. We must strengthen our preparations for future sporting events. The Los Angeles Olympics will take place in 2028. India will host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. And hosting the Olympics in 2036 is also India’s aspiration. Keeping this in mind, from the Red Fort I spoke about launching a Talent Hunt campaign. Today, talent is being identified in villages across the country and nurtured. These very athletes will bring medals for India in the years ahead.

Friends,

Our dreams are big. Our resolutions are also big. And today, India has the confidence to achieve them. Every Indian has that confidence. Therefore, with complete conviction, I say:

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!

India among the top sporting nations, We will Do it!

India as a global sports hub, We will Do it!

World-class sports infrastructure in India, We will Do it!

A champion from every corner of India, We will Do it!

Friends,

Our success at the Asian Games is also an example of India’s changing mindset. It shows how today’s youth are impatient to scale every height. There is no summit higher than the determination of India’s youth. There is no goal beyond the capability of our youth power. The limitless sky of possibilities lies before us, and India’s youth are themselves deciding the destination. That is why, in a short span of time, India has become the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Our youth are building companies in the space sector. They are working on satellite technology. The same youth are developing new technologies in the defence sector. They are conducting new experiments in Artificial Intelligence. And this transformation is not limited to big cities. Just as talented individuals from remote areas are now getting opportunities in sports, similarly, in startups, research, and other ventures, young people from small cities and villages are coming forward with new ideas. Behind this confidence lies a deep trust. The systems developed by the country over the past decade have given young people confidence that they can dream big. They know that the full strength of the nation stands behind them to help them realise those dreams.

Friends,

The benefits of our efforts are not limited only to athletes who compete on the field. New career opportunities are being created for youth in areas such as sports coaching, physiotherapy, sports management, and sports broadcasting. As sports develop, many related professions are also advancing. This has opened new avenues of employment and entrepreneurship for young people.

Friends,

Whatever field we may be in today, we must work hard for our own success. At the same time, we must also take responsibility for shaping the next generation. Now you possess the experience of international tournaments. Therefore, I would request that you devote some time to those children who dream of progressing just as you did. You must water their dreams with the sweat of your own efforts. That is how success comes. Whenever you get an opportunity, meet children in your village and your town. Visit different schools. Be sure to visit the grounds where you first began playing. Your experiences can be extremely valuable to those children. Perhaps a single word from you may give a child the courage to move forward in sports.

Friends,

The youth of the country do not draw inspiration from you only in sports. Because the role of sports extends beyond the playing field. Sports teach us discipline in life. They teach us how to rise again after falling. They teach us how to win after losing. Sports teach us how to stay committed to a goal for a long time and how to adapt ourselves to changing circumstances. These lessons become part of our everyday lives. And this sporting spirit serves us throughout our lives.

Friends,

I always say: The one who plays, blossoms. So keep playing, keep blossoming. Once again, my many best wishes to all of you for the upcoming competitions and for all your future efforts. Your enthusiasm and your confidence are the greatest strengths of New India. With this confidence, we must take India to new heights.

So come, once again, with full energy, say with me:

Viksit Bharat, We will Do it!

Viksit Bharat at Twenty Forty Seven, We will Do it!

We will Do it!

Top Three Economy, We will Do it!

Top Three Economy, We will Do it!

Self-Reliant India, We will Do it!

Self-Reliant India, We will Do it!

Global Manufacturing Hub, We will Do it!

Global Manufacturing Hub, We will Do it!

India’s Leadership in Technology, We will Do it!

Steps into Space, We will Do it!

Hosting the Olympics, We will Do it!

Medals in New Sports, We will Do it!

Yes, We will Do it!

Many, many congratulations.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-speech-during-the-launch-of-developm:
Lieutenant Governor Shri V. K. Saxena ji, all senior officials of the BRO and the Airport Authority, all officials of the Union Territory, other distinguished guests, my dear brothers and sisters.

“Ladakh si Mi-Mangs Kunla, Jullay!”

Today, another chapter is being added to the progress and development of Ladakh. I am happy that I am becoming a part of this occasion through technology. Today, several important development projects have been inaugurated in Ladakh. Through these projects, travel will become easier for many people, electricity facilities will improve in some places, water availability will increase in others, and the conservation of our ancient heritage will also receive new strength. Just now, I was watching that there was snowfall in Zanskar, and I was seeing the enthusiasm of the people of Zanskar, their excitement in waving the Tricolour even while the snow was falling.

Friends,

This is my Leh, my Ladakh. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the people of Ladakh for these projects. I also congratulate all the engineers, workers, and local companions involved in these projects. I especially appreciate the companions of the BRO.

Friends,

Some time ago, I had the privilege of laying the foundation stone for the terminal building of the Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh. And it is my good fortune that today I have also had the privilege of inaugurating this important project. This terminal, built at a cost of about six hundred and fifty crore rupees, will increase the airport’s annual passenger capacity from one million to three and a half million. The number of flights here can also increase by up to three times. This terminal has another special feature. Keeping Ladakh’s harsh climatic conditions in mind, geothermal technology has been used in it. Solar energy has also been incorporated. This is the country’s first airport terminal equipped with geothermal heating facilities in India. Congratulations to all of you. Our effort is that modern infrastructure should develop in Ladakh while also ensuring complete care for the environment here. This airport terminal will also provide new energy to the tourism sector in Ladakh. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all my brothers and sisters of Ladakh for this modern airport terminal.

Friends,

The other projects inaugurated today are also of great importance. Today, the Nimmu–Padum–Darcha road has been dedicated to the people of Ladakh. About two thousand five hundred crore rupees have been spent on it. A journey that earlier took around twelve hours can now be completed in approximately three hours. This means that not only will travel time be saved, but this road will also greatly support trade and commerce.

Friends,

Earlier, I had the privilege of laying the foundation stone and inaugurating the power transmission line connecting Srinagar and Leh. Today, the Hanu hydroelectric project and its associated transmission line have also been inaugurated. We all know that a reliable electricity system brings not only light, but also illuminates lives. It brings major changes to life. Many new activities become possible in villages. Children’s education, healthcare services, and small local businesses, every sector will benefit from it. Work is also progressing on a modern electricity generation project in the Puga Valley.

Friends,

Today, forty reservoirs built under Project Amrit Him Sarovar have also been dedicated to the people of Ladakh. These will help farmers obtain irrigation water whenever needed.

Friends,

It has always been said that life in Ladakh is very difficult because of nature. Natural conditions do present their own challenges. But unfortunately, despite these circumstances, previous governments did not give priority to the development of Ladakh. Today, however, the development of Ladakh is a major priority for the central government. Since becoming a Union Territory, even greater attention has been given to its development needs. Until 2019, Ladakh had about 1,800 kilometres of road network. Today, it has increased to more than 4,000 kilometres. Earlier, there were nineteen major bridges here. Today, their number has increased to about seventy-five. The number of helipads has also increased from seven to more than forty. Earlier, only about three and a half percent of houses in Ladakh had access to tap water. Today, nearly 99 percent of homes have access to tap water. The number of beds in Ladakh’s hospitals has also doubled. Along with this, work on important projects such as the Zojila Tunnel is progressing very rapidly. Once completed, it will provide Ladakh with improved year-round connectivity to the rest of the country.

Friends,

The central government is also focusing on creating new avenues of prosperity in Ladakh. Today, opportunities in tourism are increasing here. Winter tourism and adventure tourism are being promoted. Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, the central government and we are developing more than forty border villages in Ladakh, and we call them the “first villages” of India. This is creating employment opportunities even in remote areas.

Friends,

Earlier, Ladakh had around one hundred and fifty homestays. Today, their number has increased to three thousand. Greenhouse farming has also been consistently promoted in Ladakh. Today, there are eleven thousand greenhouses here. These have created new possibilities for increasing farmers’ incomes.

Friends,

The demand for a High Court Bench in Ladakh had also existed for a long time. Our government has fulfilled that demand as well. In August this year, approval was granted for the establishment of a High Court Bench in Ladakh. This will make both administration and the justice system more accessible.

Friends,

Today, digital technology is also bringing many new opportunities closer. Whether it is hotels, restaurants, homestays, or local products, online business is opening new avenues of income. That is why we have expanded BharatNet and high-speed internet in Ladakh and other remote areas. Continuous work is also being done to ensure easier access to government services, to enable youth to study online, and to connect local entrepreneurs to national and global markets.

Friends,

We are paying special attention to the new generation of Ladakh. The youth here should receive quality education, opportunities to learn new technologies, and should not have to depend on other cities. Therefore, a major Centre of Excellence is being established in Leh. Proposals are also being advanced for satellite campuses of IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu. These will create better opportunities for higher education, research, and advanced skills for the youth of Ladakh within their own region.

Friends,

Ladakh also has enormous potential in sports. The youth here have created a distinct identity in areas such as ice hockey, winter sports, and mountaineering. I am happy that efforts are being made to promote sporting talent through Ladakh’s new sports policy. Our effort is to ensure that young people here receive better training and facilities so that they can achieve new milestones at national and international levels.

Friends,

The products that all of you create in Ladakh through your hard work are truly excellent. You already know that whenever I meet foreign guests, I often present products made in Ladakh as gifts and also tell them about all of you. I have gifted products made in Ladakh to the Chancellor of Germany, the Prime Minister of Sweden, and the President of Kyrgyzstan. The pashmina of this region, sea buckthorn, local handicrafts, and fruits such as apricots all carry immense commercial potential. That is why we granted a GI tag to Ladakh’s apricots. Today, their demand is increasing across the world. Our effort is to ensure that these products find new markets, receive better branding, and that the benefits reach the producers directly. We are also paying special attention to the pastoralists of the Changpa community. Efforts are being made to further strengthen the identity of the pashmina associated with their hard work and traditional skills. Commercial cultivation of flowers in high-altitude regions is also being promoted in Ladakh.

Friends,

The cultural heritage of Ladakh is a priceless treasure of our nation. The ancient monasteries here, the Buddhist traditions, and the local festivals must be preserved and safeguarded for future generations. In this direction, the contribution of the revered Kushok Bakula Rimpochee ji is a great inspiration for all of us. Our government’s effort is that people across the world become familiar with the culture and traditions of Ladakh. Keeping this mission in mind, India’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park has been inaugurated in Leh today. This will further strengthen efforts to preserve Ladakh’s ancient heritage. Future generations will be able to understand this heritage, and visitors from around the world will also become acquainted with Ladakh’s rich history.

Friends,

I am confident that together we will take Ladakh to new heights of development. With this, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you for these many development works.

Thank you very much. Jullay!
texts.pms-address-at-the-bloomberg-new-economy:
Namaskar!

Excellencies, delegates from around the world, leaders from business and industry, policymakers, and my friends.

A very warm welcome to all of you to India. A short while ago, Mr. Bloomberg shared his thoughts here. Reflecting on his 30-year journey, he mentioned that I am his friend. He is senior to me in age and is a highly successful person in his professional field. He is not only successful but also deeply committed. The affection he has for India is something I have experienced very closely, and therefore, on a personal level, I have always respected and admired him. Even today, his affection for India and his sentiments towards India on global platforms have consistently been a source of very positive energy. For that, sir, I express my heartfelt gratitude. Every year, this Forum brings together some of the finest minds in the world. Discussions here take place on the economy, technology, energy, and global affairs. And this time, for the very first time, the event is being held in India. I warmly congratulate Mr. Bloomberg and his entire team for this decision. You have chosen the right place at the right time.

Friends,

This year’s Bloomberg Economic Forum is focused on the new powers emerging around the world. Every era has had its own sources of power and its own definition of power. But in the 21st century, especially in this third decade, a major transformation is taking place. Today, Technology is Power, Data is Power, Knowledge is Power, Innovation is Power.

But friends,

The real question is not who possesses power. Rather, the question is how that power is being used. Will technology advance only a few people? Or will it create new opportunities for millions? Will knowledge remain the strength of only a select few? Or will it enhance everyone’s capabilities? It is from here that a new idea emerges. And that idea is: Power to Empower. Power to Empower. Beyond Power to Control lies Power to Enable. Beyond Power to Compete lies Power to Collaborate. Beyond Power to Succeed lies Power to Help Others Succeed. And therefore, the vision with which I have come here today is: Power to Empower.

Friends,

This idea is not new to India. In our tradition, it is said: “Vidya Vivadaya Dhanam Madaya, Shaktih Paresham Paripidanaya; Khalasya Sadhoh Viparitam Etat, Jnanaya Danaya Cha Rakshanaya.” Its essence is that whoever possesses knowledge, wealth, or power, what matters is how they use it. In other words, the true value of power lies in its purpose. And it is very important to understand this philosophy in today’s world.

Friends,

This human spirit of Power to Empower is not merely a lesson meant to be preached to others. It is something that our traditions have taught us over thousands of years. And in India, we have demonstrated this by incorporating it into our governance and our work culture. Therefore, I will continue my remarks through examples from India itself.

Friends,

As all of you know, India is the Mother of Democracy. India has more than one hundred languages, nearly eighty thousand registered newspapers and publications, and more than one thousand satellite television channels. And not only that, in this age of social media, India has more than five hundred million YouTube users and more than five hundred million Instagram users. In our country, people openly debate different issues, and citizens discuss diverse viewpoints. In the present era, one factor that has played a major role in enabling this is digital power.

Friends,

Until about twelve or thirteen years ago, there was a time in India when access to mobile phones and the internet itself was a form of power. Whoever had access also had information, knowledge, and opportunities. After 2014, when a new government came to power in India and we were given the opportunity to serve, India placed great emphasis on making mobile data affordable. As a result, today a student in a small town can access digital learning. A small shopkeeper in a village can reach new customers. A young person can enroll in online courses. In other words, connectivity in India has not merely connected people; it has connected opportunities as well. This, indeed, is Power to Empower.

Friends,

To those guests who have come from abroad, I would encourage you to experience India’s digital payments ecosystem. In our country, a street vendor and a large car showroom may operate at completely different scales, but both use the same digital payments ecosystem. This is the strength of inclusive technology.

Friends,

Whatever capabilities India possesses, we do not believe in keeping them confined within our own borders. We continuously share them with the Global South and with our partner countries. We are sharing our experience in Digital Public Infrastructure with other nations so that they can develop digital systems according to their own needs. During the COVID period, we also developed the CoWIN platform, which was open source. In other words, our constant effort has been to ensure that India’s capabilities open new doors of possibility for other countries as well. In other words, our strength should empower humanity.

Friends,

The power of innovation works in the same way. Transforming an idea into a product, and turning a problem into a solution, is in itself a tremendous capability. But when such opportunities reach a larger number of people in society, the balance of power becomes more equitable and its impact multiplies many times over. India’s startup journey is an example of this transformation. Before 2014, India had only a few hundred startups. Today, the country has more than 250,000 startups. Nearly half of these startups come from small cities and towns. More than forty-five percent of startups have at least one woman Director or Partner. In other words, opportunities for innovation are reaching more people, new talent is emerging, and new solutions are being created.

Friends,

This focus on the purpose of power is equally important in governance. The government possesses authority, but its purpose should not be to make citizens dependent on the system. Rather, its objective should be to ensure that citizens become capable and empowered. India is moving along this very path. Following this path, India has lifted 250 million people out of poverty over the past decade, a number greater than the population of many countries in the world.

Friends,

You may also have heard about the JAM Trinity and Direct Benefit Transfer. By using technology, we have created a system through which government assistance reaches beneficiaries directly in their bank accounts. This has reduced corruption, increased convenience for citizens, and established a direct pathway between the government and the people.

Friends,

This same philosophy of Power to Empower is visible in India’s global engagement. During the COVID pandemic, vaccine manufacturing capacity became extremely important. The question at that time was whether the benefits of this capability would remain limited to only a few countries, or whether vaccines would also reach those nations and people who lacked such facilities and capabilities. India chose the path of empowering humanity. We supplied vaccines to more than one hundred countries. Our manufacturing capability became a source of assistance for other nations as well. Let me give you another interesting example. A few months ago, India hosted the AI Impact Summit, and Mr. Bloomberg has just spoken very highly of that summit. There, we discussed not only the use of AI for humanity, but also how animals could benefit from AI. Nandan, who is seated here, can later share much more information about how this was done. In other words, the more capable and stronger India becomes, the more beneficial it will be for humanity and for the world.

Friends,

Power is not just the ability to move ahead. It is also the ability to empower others to move ahead. India believes that competition is important, but compassion is equally important. Innovation is essential, but its benefits must also be widely shared. National strength is necessary, but we must also contribute solutions to global challenges. Whether it is climate change, water governance, public health, or the responsible use of emerging technologies, the world needs capabilities that provide solutions and create new opportunities.

Friends,

Let me give you another example. Under the Paris Agreement, India made a major commitment to address climate change. In 2015, we set ourselves the target of achieving 40 percent of our installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030. India achieved this milestone in November 2021 itself, nine years ahead of schedule. India became the first G20 nation to do so. This was not merely about fulfilling a commitment; it was also a reflection of India’s evolving energy journey.

Friends,

In 2014, India’s renewable energy capacity stood at about 75 gigawatts. Today, it has reached approximately 300 gigawatts. In other words, we have added nearly four times more capacity.

Friends,

This energy transition underway in India is also creating new opportunities. Today, we have schemes such as PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM. One scheme is connecting households to solar power, while the other is enabling farmers to generate solar energy and reduce their input costs through its use. Through these two schemes, India has achieved more than 30 gigawatts of solar capacity. It is estimated that they will reduce carbon emissions by more than 30 million tonnes annually. In other words, solar power is not only becoming a means of protecting nature, but also a means of empowering people.

Friends,

In this global race for power, India is moving forward with a different mindset. And this decade itself bears witness to that.

Friends,

This decade of the twenty-first century has brought unprecedented global challenges. If we look back at the last six years, we witnessed a global pandemic. Then wars broke out in different regions. As if that were not enough, disruptions emerged in trade, critical minerals, and energy supplies. The world begins to find a way out of one crisis when another crisis appears. Things that once connected the world are now being turned into weapons. Supply chains, energy, minerals, payment systems, and technology are increasingly becoming instruments of pressure and dominance. The routes created by globalization over past decades have, in many cases, become chokepoints. Amid all this, Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way every sector functions. At the same time, many countries are facing rapidly growing challenges related to ageing populations. In such circumstances, the world is confronted with a fundamental question: trust. Trust that supplies will continue during times of need. Trust that promises made will also be fulfilled. Trust that a partner country will stand by you during moments of crisis. And it is here that India stands before you with a different outlook and a different way of thinking.

Friends,

India’s progress in the twenty-first century is a story of advancing together with everyone and carrying everyone along. When the world needs affordable medicines, one out of every five generic medicines comes from India. When solutions for digital identity and payments are required, the world looks to models developed in India. When the world needs talent, it places its trust in India’s skilled youth. Today, India is home to more than 2,000 Global Capability Centres that are providing services to companies across the world.

Friends,

It is clear that whenever the world needs a steady pillar, India extends its hand in support, recognizing its responsibility. We do not grow at anyone’s cost. We grow with the world, and for the world.

And friends,

India does not seek credit for what it does. The world proudly says that India gave Zero to the world. This Zero benefited all of humanity. Yet India never asked for royalties in return. Even today, India works with the same spirit. The ideas we offer for addressing contemporary challenges also reflect this outlook. Throughout history, many global organizations have been created, each serving its own interests. But consider the kind of global platforms India has created. Consider the institutions we have established and compare them with what has emerged elsewhere in the world. What have we contributed? The International Solar Alliance. What have we contributed? The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure. What have we contributed? The Big Cat Alliance, the Global Biofuel Alliance, the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), and Mission LiFE, Lifestyle for Environment. These are initiatives that benefit everyone and contribute to the well-being of all life.

Friends,

The ideas that India has brought forward are before you. The vision of One Sun, One World, One Grid. The belief in One Earth, One Family, One Future. The vision of One Earth, One Health. In other words, India places emphasis on connecting and coming together. And even in this, power is used to empower others.

Friends,

In a world filled with uncertainty, India offers the assurance of reliability and stability. In the April-June quarter of this year, India’s growth rate stood at 7.8 percent. And this growth rests on a strong foundation. Twelve to thirteen years ago, India’s current account deficit was more than four percent of GDP. Last year, it declined to approximately half a percent, standing at 0.61 percent. Today, our foreign exchange reserves exceed 700 billion dollars. Our banking system is in its strongest position in many decades.

Friends,

It is because of this strength that India’s sovereign ratings are being upgraded. Today, India’s confidence is at an unprecedented high. We are pursuing reforms with a clear policy direction. Through GST, we transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market. We enacted the Insolvency Law. Twenty-nine labour laws have now been consolidated into four simple labour codes. Hundreds of minor business-related offences have been decriminalized. And we have not stopped there. India’s reform express continues to move ahead at high speed. For us, reforms are not a compulsion. Reforms are our conviction.

Friends,

Thousands of years ago, our Vedas gave us a mantra: “Sangachchhadhwam Samvadadhwam Sam Vo Manamsi Janatam. Let us repeat that mantra today: Let us walk together. Let us speak together. Let us strive to understand one another. Because when we walk together, our strength grows. Through dialogue, our understanding deepens. And by understanding one another, we can jointly solve great challenges. This is the essence of Power to Empower. It means not limiting our power solely to our own progress, but using it to create new opportunities for others as well. I am confident that this very platform of the Bloomberg Economic Forum will become a major platform for advancing this spirit. Once again, my very best wishes to all the participants for this event. Thank you very much. Thank you.
texts.pms-address-during-golden-jubilee-celebr:
Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Arlekar ji, Dr. L. Murugan ji, Thiru Rajmohan ji, Thiru Nainar Nagendran ji, Dr. Girija Seshadri Amma ji, Thiru R. R. Gopal ji, my young friends, teachers and parents, my Tamil brothers and sisters, Vanakkam.

Friends,

Today is the first day of Navratri. To have the good fortune of coming to Tamil Nadu, the sacred land of Shiva and Shakti, and to have the opportunity to meet the devotees of Goddess Saraswati, makes this a truly wonderful beginning to Navratri for me. I can also see the enthusiasm of my young friends. I can feel this positive energy, this excitement. I can see the future of India in your eyes.

Before I begin, I would like to say that today I landed in Chennai ten minutes ahead of schedule. However, because of the way the programmes were arranged and some unavoidable delays, I was late in reaching you. I arrived later than expected, and this caused inconvenience to you all. For that, I sincerely seek your forgiveness.

Friends,

Today’s youth want to become the strength behind the vision of a developed India. The new ideas and new solutions needed for a developed India will determine not only India’s future but also the future of the world.

Today, the world is looking for solutions. And you have the potential to provide those solutions.

Friends,

Today, India offers infinite opportunities. I want every young person to see their future on that larger canvas. Because this is your time. This is your time. This is your opportunity. I am fully confident that we will fulfil this dream. Together, We Will Do It!

Together, We Will Do It!

Together, We Will Do It!

Together, We Will Do It!

Friends,

There is also an interesting inspiration behind my visit here today. A few months ago, our Girija Amma met me in Nagercoil along with some children. Their dedication, their self-confidence, and their devotion to the future of the country left an extraordinary impression on my mind. During that meeting, she invited me to this Golden Jubilee celebration. First, there was her affection; second, there was my own regard for this historic institution. At that very moment, I firmly decided that I would definitely attend this programme. On this occasion, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the Vishva Hindu Vidya Kendra and the entire Hindu Vidyalaya family for this remarkable journey of fifty years.

Friends,

Today, Vishva Hindu Vidya Kendra is celebrating its Golden Jubilee. This milestone is great, and its journey is equally inspiring. In 1975, this institution began as a small school in West Mambalam, Chennai. At that time, it had only seven students. Facilities like those available today did not exist. There was no permanent building. Resources were limited. But there was one thing: firm determination and an unwavering spirit of service. That is why, despite every challenge, this institution kept moving forward. Over time, this small effort grew into a major educational movement. Today, you have fifteen institutions across different parts of Tamil Nadu.

Friends,

On this occasion, I also respectfully remember the contribution of Shri Jaigopal Garodia ji. He made an important contribution towards the construction of the school building. Today, I also congratulate all the teachers, staff members, parents and alumni who have made the journey of Hindu Vidyalaya successful. Fifty years of dedication. Fifty years of commitment. Fifty years of shaping young lives.

Friends,

This institution is also an example of how an educational institution creates patriotic citizens along with providing education. I had also mentioned this in my Mann Ki Baat programme. Girija Amma gave the children a simple idea: each child should save just one rupee every day and dedicate it to the country’s soldiers. When thousands of children joined this resolve, around forty lakh rupees were collected. Indeed, what an inspiring example!

Friends,

Small contributions can make a big difference. Even a small effort can create a very large impact. Whether it is supporting those in need during times of disaster or participating in cleanliness campaigns, these values form the great legacy of the Hindu Vidyalaya family.

Friends,

On this occasion, I would also like to remember the great saint Tiruvalluvar. His teachings are extremely important for all students. Recently, I had the opportunity to present a Russian translation of the Thirukkural to President Putin of Russia. The Thirukkural is an extraordinary guide for everyone who wishes to continue learning throughout life. In one of his famous kurals, Tiruvalluvar teaches us that it is not enough merely to learn something; it is equally important to apply it in our lives. And this is a great lesson for all of you students as well.

Friends,

You must all have read Mahakavi Bharatiyar extensively. The city of Kashi also played a very significant role in his life. The spiritual and national awakening that filled the atmosphere of Kashi had a deep influence on his thinking.

Friends,

I am a Member of Parliament from Kashi. Even today, the people of Kashi remember Mahakavi Bharatiyar. His words, “Achamillai, Achamillai” (Fearless, Fearless), inspire us to live without fear. Therefore, I would like to tell all the young people here: Give yourself a chance without fear. Work on your ideas. Dream big. Think differently. And be fearless.

Friends,

My understanding of India has been shaped by my travels across different parts of the country and by learning from the people I met there. In the early 1990s, I was also part of the Ekta Yatra from Kanyakumari to Kashmir. My first acquaintance with Girija Amma happened during that very journey. Since then, our association has continued.

Friends,

My travels gave me the opportunity to understand the diversity of India from close quarters. The love I have for the Tamil language and Tamil culture has also emerged from those very experiences.

Friends,

That is why I encourage you to discover India. Wherever you go, carry Tamil culture with you. Share Tamil poetry, stories and traditions with your friends. Make friends with people whose backgrounds may be different from your own. The unity of our nation is built by the friendships you make.

Friends,

Today’s new generation is receiving opportunities to fulfil its dreams that are truly unprecedented. Look at how the entire educational landscape of the country is changing today. In 2014, India had around 750 universities. Today, that number has grown to more than 1,300. The number of colleges has also increased from about 38,000 to more than 52,000. In recent years, the country has gained many new IITs, IIMs, IIITs, and AIIMS institutions.

Friends,

Today, the new education policy is improving the quality of education in the country. The global recognition of Indian institutions is also growing continuously. In the QS Rankings of 2015, India had only 14 universities. In the latest rankings, that number has increased to 52. The meaning of these figures is very clear. More institutions. More choices. And more opportunities for you.

Friends,

Every young person has different dreams and different talents. For example, many of you may wish to make sports your career. Therefore, the country is ensuring that sports do not remain limited only to entertainment. That is why new sports facilities are being created across India today. Young athletes are receiving better training and support. And India’s stature in the world of international sports is also rising.

Friends,

India is preparing to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games. We are also moving ahead with the dream of hosting the 2036 Olympics. In the coming years, when major global sporting events are held in India, our youth will have both the platform and the opportunity to showcase their abilities. Therefore, the youth of India now have the platform, the potential, and the support. It means the opportunities are endless! I am confident that your generation will take India to new heights in the world of sports as well.

Friends,

After coming among all of you today and feeling your dreams, my confidence has become even stronger. I can say with certainty that India’s future will be glorious. And the biggest heroes of that future are all of you. I have faith in your talent. I have faith in your confidence. I have faith in your capability. And therefore, today I would like to repeat some major resolutions together with all of you. After what I say, you must repeat: We Will Do It! Will you repeat it? Certainly?

Developed India by Twenty Forty Seven.

Developed India by Twenty Forty Seven. We Will Do It!

Say it with me: We Will Do It!

Developed India by Twenty Forty Seven, We Will Do It!

Top Three Economy, We Will Do It!

Self-Reliant India, We Will Do It!

Global Manufacturing Hub, We Will Do It!

Hosting the Olympics, We Will Do It!

An Indian on the Moon, We Will Do It!

Yes, We Will Do It! We Will Do It!

Developed Tamil Nadu, We Will Do It!

Developed Tamil Nadu, We Will Do It!

Developed India, We Will Do It!

Thank you so much.

Nandri, Vanakkam! (Thank You, Namastey!)
texts.pms-address-during-the-launch-of-develop:
Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Arlekar ji, Chief Minister Shri C. Joseph Vijay ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet Shri L. Murugan ji, Shri Nainar Nagendran ji, my Tamil brothers and sisters, Vanakkam.

It is a pleasure to be in Chennai with all of you. This is a historic day for Tamil Nadu. Today’s programme involves projects worth thirteen thousand crore rupees. We are inaugurating many completed projects and laying foundations for new ones. Some will make daily travel easier. Others will strengthen industry and trade. Together, they will create jobs for young people across Tamil Nadu. I congratulate the people of the state on this occasion.

Today marks the beginning of the sacred festival of Navratri. On this auspicious occasion of Navratri, and in Tamil Nadu, the sacred land of both Shiva and Shakti, I also had the good fortune of receiving the blessings of Lord Shiva at the Jalakandeshwar Temple before coming to this programme. From this sacred land of pilgrimage in Tamil Nadu, I extend my heartfelt greetings for Navratri to all the people of the country.

Friends,

Today is also the birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Jayaprakash Narayan ji and Bharat Ratna Nanaji Deshmukh. The lives of both these great personalities inspire us to work with even greater dedication towards the service of the nation. From this stage, I pay my respects to both these great personalities.

Friends,

A short while ago, I had the opportunity to visit the Brain Research Centre at IIT Madras. The research taking place in this field can create many new opportunities in the area of public health. Apart from this visit, I also had the opportunity to dedicate another stretch of the Chennai Metro to the people.

Friends,

From temple to metro, these experiences of Tamil Nadu reflect the spirit of today’s India. India draws inspiration from its cultural strength, advances through scientific progress, and creates new opportunities through modern infrastructure. Our heritage and our aspirations for the future are moving forward together.

Friends,

A few days ago, with your blessings and the love of the people of the country, I crossed an important milestone of twenty-five years as Head of the Government. In October 2001, I took oath as Chief Minister. Since then, the people of the country have given me the opportunity to serve first as Chief Minister and then as Prime Minister. During these twenty-five years, my faith in two strengths of democracy has continuously grown stronger. First – the people of the country. Second – cooperative federalism. I have always followed the mantra that the development of the nation comes through the development of the states.

Friends,

As Chief Minister, I personally understood the expectations of states. Therefore, after becoming Prime Minister, I not only tried to fulfil those aspirations, but also made every effort to ensure that every state could achieve its own aspirational goals.

Friends,

As Chief Minister, I had the opportunity to interact many times with Karunanidhi ji and Amma Jayalalithaa ji. And after becoming Prime Minister, I had the opportunity to work with Jayalalithaa ji, O. Panneerselvam ji, E. Palaniswami ji, and M. K. Stalin ji. Governments changed, but my commitment to the development of Tamil Nadu and service to its people always remained unwavering. And today, with that same commitment, we are moving this journey of Tamil Nadu’s development forward together with Chief Minister Joseph Vijay ji.

Friends,

Today, urban development is one of our major priorities in Tamil Nadu. I have always believed that urbanisation is not a challenge, but an opportunity. And public transport plays a very important role in this. When transportation is good, it improves people’s ease of living. We all know that merely widening roads is not enough to create better transportation. In modern cities, we need holistic infrastructure. And therefore, over the past decade, we have undertaken a massive expansion of metro networks across the country. In 2014, metro services operated in only five cities of the country. Today, metro services operate in twenty-five cities across the nation. In 2014, India’s metro network was about 250 kilometres. Two hundred and fifty kilometres. Today, this network has crossed 1,100 kilometres. I am pleased that with this expansion of Chennai Metro, this network is growing even further. This work has been carried out so that ordinary citizens living in Chennai, working families, students, and senior citizens can all travel with greater ease and complete their journeys in less time.

Friends,

We have to strengthen India by empowering our states. Therefore, the central government is promoting manufacturing in states like Tamil Nadu. Every Indian takes pride in Tamil Nadu’s manufacturing sector, its small industries, and every individual working in them. Today, initiatives of the central government, whether Make in India or Vocal for Local, are also benefiting Tamil Nadu.

Friends,

Today, from components to technology and finished products, the central government is strengthening the entire product chain in every state. As a result of these efforts, today we are the world’s second-largest mobile manufacturer. Since 2014, our electronics exports have increased elevenfold. Our defence exports have increased fiftyfold. And our engineering exports have also set new records.

Friends,

Because of this growth in manufacturing, millions of direct and indirect jobs have been created for the youth of the country. And in this manufacturing growth of India, the people of Tamil Nadu have made a highly commendable contribution. Today, we are laying the foundation stone for an advanced lubricant base oil project. This will create new employment opportunities here and will also greatly help in reducing the country’s imports. To build a strong manufacturing sector, we need good roads. We need railways and ports for the transportation of raw materials. And when such infrastructure is built, it creates a large number of employment opportunities at different levels.

When construction takes place, engineers get work, technicians get work, workers get work, everyone gets employment. Employment opportunities are also created in factories connected with cement, steel, and equipment, as well as in smaller companies. And when a project is completed, improved connectivity helps industries and services move forward. That is why the rail and road projects being inaugurated and launched today are going to be extremely important for the progress of Tamil Nadu.

Today, port infrastructure is also being strengthened across the country so that the shipping sector can reach new heights. Tamil Nadu has a very important role in this as well. In this direction, the central government has recently taken a significant decision. With an investment of about seventeen thousand crore rupees, the VOC Port at Thoothukudi is being developed as a world-class mega container and green energy hub. Once this project is completed, even the world’s ultra-large container vessels will be able to dock here easily. This will help transform Tamil Nadu into a global hub for industry and transportation.

Over the past few years, both the speed and efficiency of Indian ports have improved. Because of increased speed, the turnaround time of ships at ports has been reduced by half. As a result, Indian products are now reaching global markets faster than before.

In our vision for the ocean economy, our fishermen play a very important role. Therefore, through the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana and several other schemes, projects worth thousands of crores of rupees have been approved for Tamil Nadu. Fishing harbours are being upgraded here. Fishing landing centres are being developed. Focus is being placed on cold chain facilities. Assistance is also being provided for purchasing transport vehicles to keep fish fresh.

Friends,

Whether it is modernising the Chennai Fishing Harbour for our fisherman brothers or developing the Seaweed Park in Tamil Nadu, the central government is supporting these efforts as well. Through the Kisan Credit Card scheme, fishermen are now also able to access working capital more easily. Today, fish production in the country has grown rapidly. Last year, our seafood exports reached their highest levels ever, both in quantity and value terms. This has improved the lives of our fishing families and people living in coastal communities.

Friends,

We want to build a Tamil Nadu that keeps reaching new heights. And for this, whatever support is needed from the Centre, we stand with you with full commitment. Let us together realise the resolve of a developed India through a developed Tamil Nadu. With this spirit, once again, I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you for these projects.

Nandri, Vanakkam!!! (Thank You, Namastey).
texts.pms-address-at-the-inauguration-of-10th-:
My colleagues in the Union Cabinet, Jyotiraditya Scindia Ji, Minister of State Chandrasekhar Pemmasani Ji, ministers from various state governments, all members of the GSMA Board, representatives of telecom operators from across the world, industry leaders, experts, my young friends who have come from different colleges and startups across the country, ladies and gentlemen.

Today is October 8, a special day for India. We celebrate this day as Air Force Day. I pay my respects to all our brave Air Warriors and extend my greetings to the nation on Air Force Day.

Friends,

As Scindia Ji just mentioned, only yesterday I completed 25 years of serving the nation as the Head of Government. For me, this has been a natural and continuous journey of service. I express my gratitude to every citizen of the country and every friend of India across the world for their good wishes.

Friends,

It is also a coincidence that on this occasion, the India Mobile Congress is completing ten years. This year, India was chosen to host the GSMA Board meeting. I welcome and congratulate all of you representatives of telecom operators, industry leaders, experts, academia, and startups who have come here from across the world.

Friends,

This very morning, we received the news that the renowned actor Nana Patekar Ji is no longer among us. He was an outstanding artist who won the hearts of audiences through a wide range of roles. Nana Patekar Ji dedicated his life to the honour, pride, and glory of the Tricolour. He never allowed himself to be confined; like a bird, he soared across the skies of cinema. Through his films, he launched powerful attacks on disorder and injustice in society. He was a true revolutionary who worked against social evils. His words were powerful, and his silence was equally impactful. He consistently supported firm action against those who worked against the nation. I pay my tribute to Nana Patekar Ji and express my condolences to his family members and admirers.

Friends,

I have had the opportunity to join you at several editions of the India Mobile Congress. This platform has witnessed how the telecom sector and digital connectivity have evolved. In 2022, from this very stage, we launched 5G in the country. In 2023, I spoke about how India was moving from 5G Roll-out to 5G Reach-out. Today, we can all see that 5G connectivity has reached every district of the country. More than 550,000 base stations are now operating across India, providing 5G services. Mobile internet speeds have increased tenfold compared to 2022.

Friends,

At the 2024 edition of India Mobile Congress, we witnessed the presence of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). At that time, we discussed the need for global standards for the digital world. Last year, we deliberated on Invest, Innovate, and Make in India. The position that India has achieved today in the telecom sector owes much to India Mobile Congress. Over the years, this platform has emerged as a stage for India’s progress and India’s aspirations. Therefore, I extend special congratulations to all of you.

Friends,

This year, you have chosen the theme of your deliberations as “Scale Without Boundaries.” I would like to share India’s experience of how we have turned the dream of scaling beyond boundaries into a reality.

Friends,

When we talk about telecom, discussions often revolve around networks, spectrum debates, towers, reach, and speed. But for the people of India, telecom has meant much more. Over the past decade, the mobile phone has emerged not only as a tool of modern communication but also as an important instrument of good governance. This has remained at the core of our Digital India vision.

Friends,

Today, we hear that data in India is affordable, mobile phones are affordable, and the user base has expanded dramatically. All of this is true. But how did it happen? And why was all this done? When we understand this, India’s focus and priorities become crystal clear.

Friends,

Until a decade ago, the digital divide was a major challenge in India. Modern technology was increasingly becoming a privilege. In other words, only those with resources could benefit from modern technology. India was also moving in that direction. Through the Digital India campaign, we resolved to change this situation and placed the mobile phone at its centre. This was a major effort towards the democratization of technology. For this purpose, all necessary reforms were carried out in the telecom sector and infrastructure was expanded. We also focused on ensuring that mobile phones and other telecom hardware would be manufactured in India itself.

Friends,

As a result of these efforts, mobile phones and data became far more accessible and affordable for ordinary Indians. Today, this is enhancing the ease of living of our citizens. During the COVID period, we witnessed how almost everything came to a standstill. Yet offices continued functioning, banks remained operational, and education continued in India. This was made possible by India’s digital ecosystem. Mobile and internet connectivity ensured uninterrupted access to education, healthcare, payments, and government services. Today, even children from remote villages and underprivileged backgrounds can access quality knowledge. Digital learning is increasingly becoming accessible to everyone.

Friends,

Let me share a statistic that further demonstrates the impact of Digital India. We have a platform called DIKSHA for online education. During the COVID period, by July 2022, more than 5 billion learning sessions and nearly 600 billion learning minutes had been recorded on this platform. Our effort now is to connect nearly 250 million students to all our digital and online education platforms.

In other words, friends,

The revolution in the telecom sector has directly benefited Indian citizens. As you know, India is diverse in every sense, in language as well as geography. Such diversity can also create many inconveniences in people’s lives. Mobile connectivity has transformed this diversity into convenience. Earlier, most banks were located in cities, hospitals were concentrated in urban areas, and government offices were typically available only at block or district headquarters. Any government service required significant investment of both time and money. Digital governance has changed these conditions. Today, hundreds of government services are available through mobile phones. Government assistance is now transferred directly to beneficiaries’ accounts. Through Direct Benefit Transfer, nearly ₹50 lakh crore has reached beneficiaries directly in their bank accounts. As a result, nearly ₹5 lakh crore has been prevented from falling into the wrong hands. This is not a small figure. Nearly ₹5 lakh crore has been saved from misuse.

Now tell me, those whose easy earnings have stopped, will they love Modi? Did I do the right thing or not? Should this have been done or not? Should such wrong practices be stopped or not? They may shout and scream as much as they want, but I have made up my mind and I will continue in this direction.

If the old system had remained in place, around ₹5 lakh crore of government money would have been lost through leakages and would have filled the pockets of such people. We stopped this. Now that money reaches the rightful beneficiary, and the savings are being utilized for productive purposes.

Friends,

Under the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme, we have already deposited more than ₹4 lakh crore directly into the bank accounts of farmers. This amount is transferred every four months, and the farmer receives a notification directly on his mobile phone. This money has reached crores of small farmers who, in the past, often remained beyond the reach of government schemes.

In other words, friends,

The mobile phone is no longer merely a medium for communication. It has ensured less travel, less waiting, less cost, and greater convenience. This is the greatest citizen dividend that technology can deliver.

Friends,

Over the past decade, India’s telecom infrastructure has expanded continuously. Towers have been installed in remote areas, optical fibre networks have expanded on an unprecedented scale, and data has become more affordable. This has also given rise to entirely new sectors of the economy. It has created new consumers in technology, entertainment, and education, while simultaneously nurturing a new generation of creators. Take gaming as an example. It is estimated that today more than 500 million people in India are connected to the gaming ecosystem in one way or another. A large proportion of them are young Indians. Youth from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities are also actively participating. They are not only playing games but competing in e-sports, creating gaming content, and building new gaming businesses. In other words, the mobile phone in India has become both a gaming console and a creation studio.

Friends,

The telecom revolution in India has brought a similar transformation in the world of content. Better and faster connectivity, coupled with affordable data, has taken video-sharing platforms, social media, and regional OTT services to villages and small towns. As a result, many language-related barriers and limitations have been removed. Today, the content creation industry alone is worth thousands of crores of rupees in India and provides income opportunities for millions of people. In other words, the mobile phone has democratized content creation in India.

Friends,

At a time when telecom and digital technology are playing such a critical role, it is equally important that we strengthen the security framework associated with them. The security of phones and the security of networks are priorities for all of us. An ordinary citizen does not think in terms of protocols or architecture; for them, trust is what matters most. When they receive a call, they should know who is calling. When they receive a message, they should know whether it is genuine or fake. When they make a payment, they should be confident that their money is secure. When they provide their data through a form, they should know that their information is protected.

Friends,

Technology achieves scale only when it earns trust. And we all know that cyber fraud and cybercrime do not respect borders. They have already crossed boundaries. A person sitting in one country may commit a crime in a third country with assistance from a second country. We are also witnessing how serious a challenge deepfakes have become. Therefore, it is necessary that we work on a global framework to address these issues. Governments, technology companies, telecom operators, and financial institutions must all become part of such a framework. I would also urge GSMA and telecom operators around the world to come together and create a global mechanism that can stop such fraud even before it reaches people. India has learned a great deal through its own experiences, and India is always ready to share those experiences with the world.

Friends,

Only four years remain in this decade. The discussions that take place at this edition of India Mobile Congress will strengthen the roadmap for the next decade. And this roadmap will guide not only India but the global mobile market as well. Over the past years, India has progressed from being a consumer to becoming a creator. Now India is moving towards a future where products and designs will originate in India, and their technology and intellectual property will also belong to India. To achieve this, every necessary incentive is being provided and every necessary reform is being undertaken. In other words, the reform express is moving rapidly forward in the telecom sector as well. We are modernizing laws that are decades old. Through the Telecommunications Act, we have created a modern regulatory framework. We are also rationalizing structural burdens such as AGR and bank guarantees, transforming burdens into opportunities. The GatiShakti Sanchar Portal has accelerated Right of Way approvals through digital processes.

Friends,

India’s semiconductor and semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem is also gathering momentum. Commercial production has already started at five locations. In the next phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, our focus will be on the entire supply chain. In other words, India is taking major strides in every area associated with the telecom sector.

Friends,

Over the years, India Mobile Congress has achieved a great deal. However, the journey of development is one of continuously crossing new milestones. We have before us the grand resolve of a Developed India, and for that we must continuously broaden our efforts. The technologies showcased here certainly have their own importance. But IMC should be remembered for the partnerships that were forged here, for the research projects that were launched here, for the products that reached the world from here, and for the innovations that emerged from India and served humanity. We must transform IMC into a platform that serves as a junction for technology, research, industry, investment, and ideas. I am confident that all of you will continue to work towards this goal with complete dedication. With this expectation, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-press-statement-during-joint-press-s:
Your Excellency, Mr. President, Delegates from both countries, Friends from media,

Namaskar!

I am very happy to warmly welcome the President of Switzerland to India.

First of all, I appreciate his commitment to India-Switzerland relations. In October last year, with his personal support, we implemented a historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries. This is India’s first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe.

It is also an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity. Through this, we aim to achieve the targets of $100 billion in investment in India and 1 million direct jobs over the next 15 years.

Friends,

The friendship between India and Switzerland goes back centuries. In the 19th century, Swami Vivekananda saw a glimpse of the Himalayas in the Swiss Alps. Mahatma Gandhi also spent time in Switzerland and interacted with its people. The memories of these historic visits continue to resonate in our friendship even today.

Today, innovation, infrastructure, and advanced technology are strong pillars of our partnership. And through today’s summit, we are going to give our partnership a new momentum and take it to new heights.

Friends,

We have taken several important decisions to increase market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries.

This will help increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods to Switzerland. At the same time, we will attract new Swiss investments into key sectors in India, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability. Through these initiatives, we will work together to develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the world.

Friends,

Today, we identified new opportunities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. We also agreed to further deepen cooperation in nuclear energy.

The Varanasi ropeway, Jewar Airport in Noida, and railway and tunnelling projects in mountainous areas are shining examples of our infrastructure cooperation. To further strengthen this cooperation, today we signed an agreement on transport, mobility, and infrastructure.

We invite Swiss infrastructure companies to invest in India at a large scale and participate in capacity building, design, and manufacturing.

Friends,

Science and technology cooperation is also a strong pillar of our partnership. I am very pleased that we will soon launch new joint research projects in priority areas such as health, clean energy, and space. We also welcome the agreement with the University of Zurich to build the capacity of India’s science start-ups.

Given the growing popularity of Yoga and Ayurveda in Switzerland, we also had a meaningful discussion today on deepening cooperation in these areas.

Friends,

People-to-people ties are the greatest strength of our partnership. The Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement and the Young Professionals Agreement signed today will open up many new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals, and young people.

Friends,

Both India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue, and diplomacy. We will continue to work together for global peace and stability.

Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace.

We also agree that reforms in global institutions are essential to address the growing global challenges.

Friends,

I am grateful to the President of Switzerland for visiting India with a large business delegation. On October 7, in his presence, we will host the “Prosperity Summit” with India-EFTA business leaders. This summit will serve as an important platform to turn the promise of our trade and investment partnership into concrete outcomes. I also extend my very best wishes to all the business leaders participating in this summit.

Your Excellency,

In February this year, India hosted the world’s largest AI Summit. Next year, Switzerland will take this journey forward through the “Geneva AI Summit.” I extend my best wishes to Switzerland for the success of the Geneva AI Summit. I am confident that together, we will continue to work towards making AI responsible, inclusive, and human-centric.

Once again, thank you very much for your visit to India and for being a strong supporter of India-Switzerland relations.
texts.pms-address-at-the-centenary-celebration:
My colleagues in the Union Cabinet, Dr. Jitendra Singh Ji, P. K. Mishra Ji, T. V. Somanathan Ji, Ajay Kumar Ji, all the esteemed members of the UPSC, Chairpersons of the various State Public Service Commissions who have come from different states, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.

Before I begin today’s discussion, I would like to mention an incident that occurred yesterday.
