More of our police personnel had to lay down their lives than the number of soldiers who lost their lives in war, so that ordinary citizens could live in safety. Naxalism had left the land soaked in blood. When you gave us the opportunity to serve in 2014, we made a resolve on that very day to free the country from Naxalism. Today, I am happy to say that Naxalite-Maoist violence may no longer even have the strength to take its final breath. We are moving towards eliminating it completely. In areas where Naxalites once fired their guns, where the land was once stained with blood, today, in those very Naxal-affected regions and areas, the Tricolour of development, trust and endeavour is flying high because they have been freed from Naxalism.

My dear countrymen,

But we must not underestimate this challenge. We need to be even more cautious about this challenge. For years, individuals with a Maoist ideology had made their place in the corridors of power in the country. Even as advisors on government committees, this Maoist ideology influenced policy.

My dear fellow citizens,

We have succeeded in eliminating armed Naxals from the forests and liberating the country from that menace. However, while the armed Naxals are gone, the mental Naxals remain, and these mental Naxals are on the lookout for an opportunity. They are looking for ways of violence and anarchy. They are resorting to various tactics to drag society onto the wrong path. We must identify these mental Naxals, isolate them, and steer the nation’s youth toward the mainstream effort of transforming India into a developed nation.

My dear fellow citizens,

Building a secure India is the responsibility of us all. Whether the challenge is within or beyond the borders, India is prepared for any situation. The nature of warfare is changing today; there is no longer a guarantee that conflict will be confined to the borders. Modern warfare can target refineries, the banking sector, or data centers, in a sense, a new form of combat where infrastructure and factories are being destroyed. We announced ‘Mission Sudarshan Chakra’ some years ago, and work on it is progressing rapidly. Today our defence exports have increased by almost 50 times. Our weapons are reaching about 100 countries. India’s reputation is gradually increasing on the global stage. In these changing times, we must focus on defense equipment and enhance the capabilities of our armed forces; But at the same time, citizens will also have to be prepared. The civil defence systems that have developed in our country in accordance with the wars of the last century have become outdated and hence, I am announcing today from the Red Fort that, in the coming days, we will create a vibrant network of civil defence. We will familiarize them with modern systems. What arrangements can be made to protect citizens from modern crises? We are going to create a huge voluntary force of civil defence to overcome modern challenges.

My dear countrymen,

The contribution of our sisters and daughters to nation-building has become a source of great inspiration for us all. Whether in fighter jets or civil aviation, our daughters are at the forefront. They are leading the way in the sports arena as well. Our daughters are seen leading the most in the process of admission in STEM education. Even in the armed forces, daughters graduating from the NDA are demonstrating the capability to lead the nation’s military with great confidence and authority. To see the true strength of my daughters, I recently visited a semiconductor plant in Sanand, where tribal daughters from various corners of the country were working. They came from villages where people did not even know what a passport was. Those daughters went abroad, got training and today they are working in chip manufacturing and with great confidence. I was really impressed by the confidence I saw in them. We had set a target of making 3 crore sisters ‘Lakhpati Didis’ and have already surpassed that goal. Now, we are moving forward with the aim of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis. The creation of 3 crore new Lakhpati Didis signifies a massive transformation in the rural economy driven by the power of women.

My dear countrymen,

Today, in Panchayats, Municipalities and Municipal Corporations a large number of our women are becoming public representatives and are guiding the country, solving problems, providing very capable leadership and keeping this in mind, we passed the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in the Parliament. Yet, for one reason or another, this dream has repeatedly fallen victim to the political arena over the past 40 years. Today, standing here beneath the shadow of the Tricolour on the ramparts of the Red Fort, I appeal to and urge all the political parties of the country. Come, let us become worshippers of the power of those women. Let us step forward to uphold their dignity and ensure that our mothers and sisters secure 33% representation in the Legislative Assemblies and the Lok Sabha as soon as possible, so they may contribute to shaping India’s policies. It is the need of the hour and I once again urge all the political parties, come and join in the cause of women’s respect by implementing women reservation, you also take the credit, you also take the fame, but give rights to my mothers and sisters.

My dear countrymen,

The resolve for a developed India will be fulfilled only when development reaches the last person. Before 2014, only 25 crore people had social security cover, only 25 crores.

Friends,

Only 25 crores in the last 5-7 decades, we have provided social security cover to 100 crore countrymen within a decade. Under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, even the elderly above 70 years of age are getting free medicines up to Rs 5 lakh. Crores of families have got a huge facility due to this and because of this Ayushman card, Rs 2 lakh crore which was to be spent on medicines and operations, has been saved for my families, they are poor families, they are middle class families, they have received such significant support!

My dear countrymen,

Today, I need your help with a task. I am seeking assistance from all of you. I want the youth to take the lead in this. Just an hour or two of your time can empower the nation significantly. You will wonder what power I can give to the country in one or two hours, let me tell you. You are about to become a great power, and therefore, an environment should be created in every home. These days, the census is underway in the country. Census work is going on, counting is going on and counting is not just about figures. Policies are made from its details, plans are made, the country prepares its roadmap for moving forward and hence it is very important to have accurate information. Sometimes the representatives who come from the government are in such a hurry that sometimes they write the same spelling, sometimes they write it differently and due to this, ultimately, we face problems in getting the accurate results. Now that technology is available, a decision has been made allowing you to submit your census details yourself using your mobile phone. Later some clerk will come, some representative will come, they will discuss the details with you, if your family sits together and completes the registration digitally—ensuring there are no errors in spelling or information—the accuracy of the data will greatly aid the nation’s progress. That is why I urge the youth of the country to sit down with their families and familiarize themselves with the entire form. First fill the form on paper, if there is any mistake, correct it and then upload it digitally through technology. Just imagine, the country will accomplish this massive task, and the nation’s time and energy will be utilized for a constructive purpose. That is why I urge the youth of my country to actively participate in this census exercise.

My dear fellow citizens,

I spoke of the ‘Panch Pran’ (five pledges) from the Red Fort. These five pledges have provided immense strength to the nation, empowering it to move forward with a sense of self-pride and the capability to surpass its goals. We have to keep eradicating the mentality of slavery every moment. Drawing inspiration from the visions of the India dreamt of by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, Babasaheb Ambedkar, Pandit Nehru, Sardar Patel, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru, Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee, Bhagwan Birsa Munda, and Jyotiba Phule, let us march ahead. Let us reiterate this resolve: the nation’s interest must come before our own, and duty must define our identity. I say to all my countrymen—this is our time, this is our moment, and this is our resolve. Let us transform dreams into resolve, resolve into capability, and capability into success. Let us make every step a step of development, let us join step with step, let us connect our hearts, let us remain connected to the goal, one lamp will light thousands of lamps, let us together build a developed India. With this very sentiment, I extend my heartfelt best wishes to you all on this auspicious occasion.

Say it with me:

Bharat Mata ki Jai!

Bharat Mata ki Jai!

Bharat Mata ki Jai!

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Vande Mataram!

Thank you very much!
texts.pms-speech-during-release-of-former-pres:
Our former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji, Honorable Speaker of the Lok Sabha Om Birla ji, Mrs. Savita Kovind ji, all the senior dignitaries seated in the hall – I may not be able to mention everyone, but it gives me great joy that this feels like a family gathering.

Brothers and sisters,

Today we have the occasion of releasing Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji’s autobiography. I am happy that I too have had the fortune of being part of this program. I have had a long association with Kovind ji, the opportunity to know him closely, to receive his guidance as President, and along with all this, his special affection and warmth toward me – this has been a great treasure in my life. From what I have understood of his life, from what I have seen of his capabilities, I can say with full confidence that Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji’s autobiography will become a heritage for Indian democracy and Indian society. His life journey, his contribution to society and the nation – there is so much I could speak about, but at a book release only a “curtain raiser” should be given. You must read the book fully to gain its complete benefit.

Friends,

To know Kovind ji’s life journey in his own words, to read his writing, his experiences – this will give the new generation much to learn. I warmly congratulate Ram Nath Kovind ji for this autobiography.

Friends,

Kovind ji has given his book a very apt title – “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles.” The meaning is that life and its struggles are personal, but the victories that came from those struggles belong to the Republic of India, to Indian democracy.

Friends,

We often see that human nature is such that people credit themselves for success, and blame society for difficulties. But when the heart is generous, when Indian values are present, then a person does not waste time finding faults in society. He focuses on the positive side, and considers society an equal partner in his success. Kovind ji’s autobiography and its title are examples of this. Look at his life – born in a very ordinary family in Kanpur Dehat. He has described, and written in his book, how one summer day a fire broke out in his house. His mother, forgetting her own safety, tried to save the household items. For a mother in a simple family, every item is a means of raising her children. In that effort, she was trapped in the fire and passed away. Imagine – at such a young age, to lose one’s mother in this way, how painful it must have been. I was fortunate that my mother lived beyond 100 years and blessed me. Even so, I still feel her absence.

Friends,

This painful incident could have broken anyone, but it made Kovind ji stronger. A neighbor mother helped in his upbringing. From this he understood the strength of social unity and harmony. After this incident, his father’s role became even greater. The way his father managed the family, gave values to the children – that is why Kovind ji considers his father his hero.

Friends,

Amidst these childhood struggles, Kovind ji made education the path to strengthen himself. He worked hard, did not let lack of resources become a weakness. And he reached a height that people could not even imagine then – he became the President of a vast country like India.

Friends,

Even after reaching such a high position, Kovind ji’s humble personality and simplicity remained intact. I remember, as Prime Minister when I went to meet him at Rashtrapati Bhavan, he would do things beyond protocol. He would come to the car door to see off the Prime Minister. I used to request him not to do this, but he never left his humility till the end. After becoming President, when he went to his village Paraunkh, he touched the feet of his teachers and paid respect. He bowed to the soil of the village and thanked the ordinary people. The whole country saw that emotional scene. His conduct presented to the world a picture of Indian values that every Indian is proud of.

Friends,

In centuries of slavery, our country lost much economically and socially. Our ancestors struggled for centuries. Mahatma Gandhi, Babasaheb Ambedkar, Jyotiba Phule, Savitribai Phule – so many great figures dreamed of a new India, where even the poorest and most deprived could reach the summit. Personalities like Kovind ji, through their labor and ability, not only changed their own lives, but played an important role in realizing that centuries‑old dream and vision. Our efforts in this direction continue. In the future, we need many youths like Kovind ji, who are not defeated by troubles, who do not despair before difficulties, but who have the courage to make every goal easier through hard work. This change will fulfill the resolve of building a strong India. From here will emerge the path to self‑reliant and developed India.

Friends,

For building such youth power, Kovind ji’s autobiography can be an important source of inspiration.

Friends,

In his autobiography, Kovind ji has also described in detail his experiences with Morarji Desai. The spirit of service to the nation that was within him, the learning and path he gained by working with Morarji bhai – Kovind ji made politics and social service his path. He remained dedicated to his duties. He made service his goal. His tenure in Parliament is witness to this. As Governor too, he set an example. As President, we saw the same dedication. Even after retiring from the highest post of President, he did not rest. He is still working on important subjects like One Nation, One Election. He is awakening the nation. This is a subject whose solution can begin a new chapter in Indian democracy. I believe the people of the country can learn much from Kovind ji’s dedication and spirit of service.

Friends,

Remaining active in social life, finding time for an autobiography is very difficult. Kovind ji has done this work for all of us, because his life contains so much in which people from poor and deprived backgrounds can see reflections of their own lives. How an ordinary family, even in difficult circumstances, does not compromise with purity and honesty of life. How those ideals later become the foundation of our lives. How the values of hard times give us light throughout life. How this purity gives us strength for national service. While fulfilling responsibilities in different positions, Kovind ji has continuously given this inspiration to society.

Friends,

I am confident that Kovind ji’s autobiography will preserve not only the memories of his life, but also important memories of our democracy. Once again, I extend my best wishes to him for his autobiography. And I especially urge the young generation – this is the age of reels, social media influencers pull you here and there. In this age of shortcuts, remember one thing. At railway stations it is written – some people jump across the tracks instead of using the bridge. There it is written: Shortcut will cut you short. Even if you want to go by shortcuts, I urge the youth – read autobiographies of whoever you admire. Autobiographies give you the chance to understand the events of history in a different way. They are close to history. That is why I want Kovind ji’s effort to benefit future generations, especially the youth. Many congratulations. Thank you very much.
texts.pms-interaction-with-indias-cwg-champion:
Prime Minister– Here, I have been living in this house for about 12-13 years now. If I have regularly and every time received someone, if I have met someone, it is the players. For the last 10-12 years, because of your hard work, because of your efforts to bring continuous victories to India, and because of the tradition of crossing new heights of success, the work that perhaps we could have done by going to schools and saying “play, do this, do that,” your medals inspire them far more.

Prime Minister– You had promised me last time that both your daughters would become players?

Player– Yes sir, they are still young, but in the next Commonwealth Games, three medals will come from one house.

Prime Minister – For sure.

Player – Yes sir.

Player – When I was running, when my event was on the 29th, that day was Guru Purnima. So that day I gave a gift to my Guru.

Prime Minister – You have brought great honor. So many tears were flowing, I felt as if every drop of those tears was turning into a gold medal.

Player – I was very happy, emotional too that day. The happiness was more, and I cried because in the Paris Olympics I had missed a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life, we face so much. In these four years, I faced so many things – injuries all the time, family problems, everything. It was very difficult to face those four years. And when I stood on the podium, sir, and our flag went up, and our national anthem played, sir, we cannot stop ourselves, tears just come out.

Prime Minister – Very, very good.

Prime Minister – I do not consider this achievement only yours. This victory becomes a great inspiration for future generations.

Player – Everyone was afraid of us, saying that if they fight India, they will lose the first fight itself, and we won’t get a medal.

Prime Minister – So they assumed it.

Player – Yes sir.

Prime Minister – What happened, you were fighting with the restaurant people?

Player – We had such good performances, it was the last day, everyone had won, and all Indians were there. I felt a little bad. So I spoke to them politely, requested them, and then they agreed, and it was changed.

Prime Minister – This situation of victory, happiness, joy, with your companions, when the games are over, the mood of laughter and fun – at such a time, to look at the map and register it, and immediately, not only when medals are given does the nation stand, but from within the nation feels it. I tell you truly, this video is not ordinary. People will remember it for a long time. Even boxers around the world have now begun to fear you.

Player– Certainly sir, everyone was scared. One after another, gold medals kept coming, and in the end it was like an explosion. The way we are getting support, back‑to‑back competitions, it is a big thing. And all our young athletes, many of them have come through the Khelo India scheme, and this is bringing a big change in sports itself.

Prime Minister– If you raise the prestige of Khelo India, prestige will not come just by cutting ribbons. You must play as a small student, a young boy, a young player plays. This will be a big contribution. Because we have to go much further, bring many more medals. On Kargil Vijay Diwas, whose victory was it?

Player – That day was Kargil Day, and the day I fought Pakistan was the same day. I am from the Indian Army, so I had already resolved that I must defeat Pakistan. And I defeated Pakistan 5-0. I dedicated that victory to our Indian Army’s Kargil heroes.

Prime Minister – You must remember this. And since you yourself are from the Army, I truly believe that the emotion you expressed – dedicating your medal to the Kargil victors – added great glory to that victory. And you defeated exactly the one who had to be defeated.

Player – Talking of Pakistan reminds me of an incident, sir. In 2015 World Military Games, my first fight was against Pakistan. The military people called and said, “Don’t lose to Pakistan.” So I won the first round 4-1, the second round 3-2. But both our heads clashed, both got cuts, and we both went to the hospital for stitches. But I won the fight.

Prime Minister – Yes.

Player – After that, both went to the hospital for stitches. Then in 2014, when you first became Prime Minister, our Army coach was Narendra Rana. He thought for a while and then told me, “Brother, can I say something?” I said yes. He said, “Brother, your name is Narendra, your coach’s name is Narendra, your Prime Minister’s name is Narendra. I have started to hate the name Narendra.”

Prime Minister – It is not only that you increased the number of medals. You have prepared a whole generation.

Player – My heart is beating fast, sir.

Prime Minister – Don’t worry.

Player – But…

Prime Minister – If you wish, you will get a medal for speaking too.

Player – In my friend circle, someone used to say that when I advised them for their good, they would ask, “Are you meeting Modi?”

Prime Minister – Yes.

Player – In Haryanvi they would say, “Are you meeting Modi, that he listens to you?” So today I have met you, sir. I can tell them, yes, I met Modi ji.

Player – In the Commonwealth Games I won a silver medal. Then I gave credit to sir. My dream was to win a medal once. But there was no training center. After joining SAI, I trained hard and won a medal. So I happily gave credit to sir, because I improved a lot.

Prime Minister – For me it is a matter of great honor. You worked hard, and you remembered me. I am very grateful, my friend.

Prime Minister – You were practicing in Varanasi, right?

Player – Yes sir.

Prime Minister – How is the stadium?

Player – Sir, it is good. I went there for 10-12 days of training, because I had gone to the temple, so I trained there. And I want to settle there too, because I like Kashi Vishwanath very much, sir.

Prime Minister – You were training in Bhopal, right?

Player – Yes sir.

Prime Minister – Did you go to Ujjain?

Player – Yes sir, I went to Ujjain too.

Prime Minister – Good, near Mahakal also.

Player – Yes sir.

Prime Minister – You went near Kashi Vishwanath once.

Player – Yes sir.

Prime Minister – It is the month of Sawan now.

Player – I will go home and then go there, sir.

Prime Minister – Okay.

Player – SAI has also supported me a lot, sir. Because of that I reached here. And I was also in the Khelo India scheme in 2018, the first Khelo India. I won a silver medal there. I saw you at the opening ceremony. I won a medal there, got the scheme, and reached here, sir.

Prime Minister – Sports arrangements are one thing, but the country wins medals when a sports culture is built in the country. Friends, you have done a great job. You have made the country proud. I congratulate you very much. And believe me, you will be victorious in the future too, and once again we will meet here. Thank you very much. Best wishes.

Prime Minister – This is the third time in a row you have brought a medal for the country.

Player – Thank you sir.

Prime Minister – Many blessings, child.

Player – And thank you so much. I am eating laddoo from sir’s hand. Yesterday was my birthday, so today from sir’s hand…

Prime Minister – Congratulations, wonderful.

Prime Minister – Smile, my friend.

Prime Minister – Whoever plays, will blossom ( Jo Khelega, Wo Khilega).
texts.pms-address-at-the-57th-convocation-cere:
Union Minister of Education Prahlad Joshi ji, my friend Harish Salve ji, Professor Abhay Karandikar, IIT Delhi Director Professor Rangan Banerjee, all professors, distinguished guests, and all student companions,

Today, a new journey begins in the lives of all you talented youth of the nation. You are living through a memorable moment of life – filled with enthusiasm, excitement, dreams, and emotions. To be part of this moment, to come to the IIT Delhi campus, and to share this experience with you, is very special for me too. The last time I joined a convocation here, the whole country was passing through the Covid period. Then I was connected virtually. But today, I am present among you, and that makes me very happy.

Friends,

Just as your families feel proud today, I too feel proud of you. Because you are not just receiving a degree – you are stepping out with dreams to do great things for the nation. Many students have also received medals for their achievements, and I congratulate you all for this. But if there had been one or two daughters, it would have been even better. Sorry – not just one or two, there should have been more. Today, some new initiatives related to AI have also been launched at IIT Delhi, and I extend my best wishes to you all for them.

Friends,

All of you, and all the students, are present in this program today, but in some corner of your minds, something else must be going on. I am not Baba Bageshwar, but surely something is running in your minds. Each student has their own picture of tomorrow. Some are waiting for their first salary. Some are preparing for a new beginning in a new city. Some companions are dreaming of their first startup. Some have set their sights on the next competitive exams. Everyone’s path is different, everyone’s dream is different. Yet there is one common feeling in all your minds – remember the day when you had your first day at IIT Delhi, and now this day of convocation has arrived. You must be thinking, wasn’t it just yesterday that orientation happened, and now convocation has come? From orientation to convocation, this journey must give you immense satisfaction. And at the same time, you must be excited for the beginning of a new chapter of life. That is why I say – live this moment fully. In the future, when big responsibilities come upon you, these old memories will surely take you back to those days. They will energize you. Every hostel has its memories – Kumaon, Aravali, Karakoram, Vindhyachal, Nilgiri, Kailash, Himadri – the stories of inter‑hostel competitions, old quarrels, so much to recall once more before you leave.

And friends,

It is not just about studies. Perhaps Jiia Sarai’s poha is calling some of you today. Maybe the parathas of Satpura mess are on your mind. Some of you may want to spend a few more moments at Wind T. If you go there, remember me too. Some may wish to revisit their department once more. Some may want to sit again at their favorite adda.

And friends,

In these emotional moments, I must tell you – whenever life gives you a chance to look back, you will remember this campus life, your friends, teachers, mentors, and support staff who became your family, your professors who took responsibility to shape talents like you, and this “Insti” which gradually became your home. In every success, you will remember them. You will be thankful to them. Therefore, carry them as an asset when you leave. Do not forget them, do not leave them behind – take them with you. My suggestion is, before leaving, meet every member here once more. And wherever you go, try to keep this bond fresh forever.

Friends,

You are stepping out at a time when the world is changing very fast. Strategic equations are shifting rapidly. Global power balance is changing every moment. And the biggest force behind this is the speed of technology. No one can say with certainty what the world will look like in the next 20–30 years.

But friends,

Whenever times of change come, challenges also come, and new opportunities are created. The world will change, technology will change, industries will change, professions will change. But amidst all this, remember my words – those who keep learning will keep winning. Those who dare to find new solutions to new challenges will turn challenges into chances. And this is exactly what you have learned at IIT Delhi. After all, what does your degree say? Is it only proof that you passed exams, achieved a good CGPA, or secured a good placement? Certainly, all these have their importance. But I believe your degree tells the world that you know how to solve difficult problems. Think of your IIT Delhi journey – reaching here was not easy, nor was the study easy. But you did not give up. This degree was not earned in a day. Every subject, every project, mid‑sem, end‑sem – these small steps brought you here. Life too runs on this principle. Whenever a challenge seems too big, do not be afraid – break it into smaller parts. You have seen in labs how problems seemed like dead ends, how simulations took hours or days, but eventually you solved them and created something new. In life too, difficulties will come. But the nature of difficulties is that they never come alone – they bring opportunities with them. Everyone must stay alert, stay aware, and keep remembering what this institute has taught you.

Friends,

I want to share some practical aspects of life with you. Campus life and life outside campus are very different. In IIT exams, there is a syllabus. But in the exam of life, everything is out of syllabus. Remember, in campus life everything was clear – what to study, which assignment to complete, which exam to give. But life runs differently. There is no fixed course, no question paper. Many times, no one even tells you what the real question is – you have to identify it yourself. I have seen the journeys of many IIT alumni. Their success was not only because they gave the right answers, but because they identified the questions that the world had stopped asking. They solved problems that others had accepted as unsolvable. That is why, keep curiosity alive, keep your learning instinct awake, keep your awareness sharp. Question what is blindly accepted, and have the courage to find solutions. This thinking will give you a unique identity.

Friends,

You all know that every generation faces its own challenges in its time period, and every generation has its own national responsibility. Our country saw the era of slavery, when the only goal of that generation was India’s independence. They sacrificed, they struggled for long years. Today, we breathe in free India because of their penance, sacrifice, and dedication.

And friends,

In today’s era, our challenges are different, and so are our responsibilities. In the next 30–35 years, whatever you do will shape the journey of a Viksit Bharat. Therefore, every decision of yours should also be based on how it benefits the nation, which need of the country it fulfills. Today, India is working towards economic self‑reliance, technological self‑reliance, industrial self‑reliance – building the strong foundation of a Viksit Bharat. On this foundation, you must construct a grand and beautiful Viksit Bharat.

Friends,

Your role in this journey is immense. The stronger the youth, the stronger the nation. With this vision, we have opened many sectors that were once closed to youth. Because of modern policies, new sectors are emerging for young people.

Friends,

Last time, when I joined your seniors’ convocation virtually, I spoke about reforms in the space sector. Back then, almost all work in this sector was done by the government. But today, the same space sector has become a sky of opportunities for thousands of youth. Our young people are building launch vehicles, launching rockets, achieving feats that only a few countries in the world have managed. Somewhere, a young engineer proudly says: “First in my bloodline to build a rocket.” The semiconductor sector is another example. When we took steps in this direction, some doubted India’s ability. They said India cannot do this. But today, production has begun in the first semiconductor units. I firmly believe – from chip to ship, everything will be made here, by your hands. And somewhere, a young person confidently says: “First in my bloodline to make a chip in India.”

Friends,

Look at our drone sector. Youth are creating new possibilities. Drones are being used in agriculture, delivering medicines, and helping in defense and security. And somewhere, a young innovator says: “First in my bloodline to make a drone.”

Friends,

India’s startup revolution has been shaped and powered by youth like you. Many founders have emerged from this very institute. If one institute can achieve so much, imagine the strength being built across the nation. Unicorns, digital payments, fintech – all have given millions of youth the chance to do something new for the first time.

Friends,

There are many more sectors where India is beginning a new journey, and the nation looks to you with responsibility and hope. Artificial intelligence, data centers, critical minerals, deep sea exploration, batteries, power storage, energy security, electric mobility, quantum computing – all these fields await your talent, innovation, and leadership. And I too am waiting.

Friends,

Another great opportunity before you is research. The country needs new research, and we are equally focused on it. The Prime Minister’s Research Fellowship is giving talented youth opportunities. The Research Development and Innovation Scheme has been launched to support ideas. The National Research Foundation has been established to strengthen science and research. Funding of up to one lakh crore rupees – one lakh crore – is being arranged for the research sector. I am saying this in English too: One Lakh Crore.

Similarly, friends,

Access to academic resources has been made easier. Through One Nation One Subscription, prestigious research journals are now available even in the smallest towns without extra cost.

Friends,

I know we still have a long way to go in this direction, and it can only happen with your commitment to research. The nation expects it from you, and most importantly, trusts you.

Friends,

Now let me talk about distraction. When we set out to achieve big goals, one major distraction comes – comparison. Who got what package, which company, which city, which country, who started a startup. In today’s social media age, this comparison never ends. But remember, life is not a leaderboard. Your real race is not with others, but with yourself. Every day, strive to be better than yesterday. And take care of your physical health and mental health too.

Friends,

Once again, I congratulate all students. I extend special congratulations to your parents and families, to your teachers, and to all those who stood by you at every step of this journey. May your future be bright, may you continue to reach new heights. With these good wishes – thank you very much.

Namaskar!
texts.pms-speech-at-the-launch-of-nasha-mukt-y:
Namaskar!

Today, all of us citizens of India have united for a great and important resolve. Saints from across the country, governors representing different states, chief ministers, other public representatives, and more than one crore young companions connected from over 28,000 locations are part of this program. On this auspicious occasion, I especially welcome and congratulate the millions of youth who have joined for this noble pledge. This campaign is for the individual, for the family, for society, and most importantly, for the nation.

Friends,

For the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan, the name Nasha Mukt Yuva itself makes the resolve clear. As India sets the goal of becoming a developed nation, it is essential that our youth remain healthy in body and mind, full of self-confidence, and always free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the purpose of the campaign. We must all resolve that our youth understand the dangers of addiction, remain aware, and stay away from it. The National Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan now plays a major role in this resolve.

Friends,

As the MP from Kashi, I am proud that this campaign began last year as a pilot project on its sacred soil. Along with scientific clarity, it carries spiritual energy, blessings of saints, and our great cultural heritage. It embodies the cultural dedication that has rejected intoxication for centuries. That is why more than 125 spiritual organizations have joined us for the welfare of millions. Social organizations and NGOs have also taken this pledge. Together, through the Kashi Declaration, a roadmap was prepared. Today, the idea that arose from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign begins across the country.

Friends,

Some efforts, when done individually, can feel tiring or discouraging. But when they become collective movements, when millions walk shoulder to shoulder, even those who could not act alone gain new energy. Collective strength is powerful, and today this campaign will touch every young heart. Just a short while ago, millions of youth across the country took the pledge of freedom from addiction. You resolved to keep your lives free from drugs, and to spread the message of de-addiction in your schools, colleges, and communities.

Friends,

This pledge taken today will continue for 100 weeks. Every Sunday, activities related to art, culture, sports, meditation, spirituality, and service will be organized. The message of de-addiction will reach new people. These 100 Sundays will be 100 strong steps toward a drug-free India.

Friends,

Today, lakhs of students from thousands of schools, colleges, and universities are connected online with this program. Lakhs of volunteers from My Bharat are also participating. Our NSS youth are with us too. From different regions, institutions, and backgrounds, more than one crore youth are united today. You are the leaders of this great movement. You have strengthened my belief in how aware, intelligent, and responsible India’s youth are toward their duties. I extend my best wishes to all of you for this campaign.

My young friends,

You are the Amrit Peedhi of India. In the next 20–25 years, you will shape your own lives, and it is you who will carry the nation to its goal of becoming a developed India by 2047. You will be the ones sitting at the summit, enjoying the fruits of that achievement. The country needs your energy, imagination, and talent. That is why, for the sake of the nation and for your own lives, it is essential to remain free from addiction. Drugs distract focus and gradually pull youth away from their dreams. The short play performed just now beautifully conveyed the problem, the crises it creates, and the collective path to overcome it. Though brief, it was not just a play – it was a powerful message, awakening us and inspiring us to fight.

Friends,

Today we see our youth excelling in startups, leading in AI, raising the tricolor in sports, and setting new records from space to science. But when a young person falls into drug addiction, it is not just one youth who loses – a dream dies, a family breaks, society suffers. Addiction robs a mother’s smile, shatters a father’s hopes, weakens a sister’s bond, steals a younger brother’s role model, and leaves elders watching their child waste away before their eyes. When this happens in families and society, the nation’s strength also weakens. Enemies exploit this, conspiring to trap our youth in addiction as part of their terror designs, flooding drugs to earn money and destroy countries like ours. That is why we must protect every youth from falling into this trap.

Friends,

By staying free from addiction, you must protect your potential. Remember, drugs may give a temporary “high,” but they bring your career and family life “low.” We must never give addiction any acceptance.

Friends,

Our society has always seen addiction as evil. Saints and gurus have warned us against it. Even the Guru Granth Sahib says: “Jitu peetai mati doori hoi baralu pavai vichi ai. Aapna paraia na pachhanai khasmahu dhake khai.” – meaning, when a substance clouds wisdom and discernment, when one forgets the difference between self and others, such intoxication leads only to downfall.

Friends,

Our culture has always given warnings and shown ways to escape addiction. Social support, the strength of yoga and meditation, all empower our inner self against drugs. Today we also have rehabilitation centers. So if a youth falls into addiction, it does not mean all doors are closed. Families must not hide it out of social prestige. Seek help, talk openly, consult experts, and use medical support to free your child. Build a culture of open dialogue at home, so you can notice early signs – withdrawal, secrecy, late nights, unusual demands for money – and intervene before it is too late.

Friends,

I appeal to professors in colleges and universities: along with academics, talk to students about the dangers of drugs. Start a movement in your campuses. Your efforts can bring big results. And remember, those who fight and overcome addiction are not weak – they are true warriors. Society must respect them, embrace them, and give them a second chance. Their courage, not their past, defines them.

Friends,

The government stands firmly with the youth in this campaign. Strict action is being taken against drug traffickers. Arrests have multiplied, and drugs worth thousands of crores have been seized. This shows how tough our government is against drugs. I am confident that the central and state governments will continue this mission in full force. I believe our youth will remain free from addiction, preserve their energy, and advance the resolve of a developed India. Seeing so many revered saints before me today, I bow to them with respect. Spiritual and social organizations across the country, with their devotees and youth, can take this campaign forward. In the coming 100 weeks, if each organization takes responsibility for one week, leads activities nationwide, and organizes major events every Sunday, imagine the scale of the movement we can build. I thank the saints, acharyas, and leaders of organizations for blessing this noble cause. I especially congratulate the more than one crore youth who have joined today. I commend the volunteers of My Bharat – whatever they resolve, they achieve. Recently, I met some of them who spent a week in India’s border villages, once called the “last villages,” now proudly called the “first villages.” Their experiences were inspiring. Today, they have organized this massive program, a symbol of their awareness and dedication to the nation. I congratulate and salute them. I am confident that through your collective efforts, this movement will reach every home, every young heart, and become a great deterrent to drug traffickers. Let us all move forward together. My best wishes to you all!

Thank you very much!
texts.pms-address-during-inauguration-of-the-s:
“Ellarigu Nanna Namaskaragalu.”

Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission Belur Math President Most Revered Swami Gautamananda Ji Maharaj, Shri Ramakrishna Ashram Mysuru President Revered Swami Muktidananda Ji, Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission Trustee Revered Swami Yadvendrananda Ji, Governor Shri Thaawarchand Gehlot Ji, Chief Minister Shri D.K. Shivakumar Ji, Member of Parliament Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar Ji, MLA Vijayendra Yediyurappa Ji, K. Harish Gowda Ji, other dignitaries, revered saints, and brothers and sisters.

First of all, I bow to Mother Chamundeshwari, the presiding deity of Mysuru. Just two days ago, we all also celebrated Guru Purnima. As you all know, where my journey began and where I am today, Ramakrishna Mission has a very important contribution to it. Three months ago, I went to Belur Math in Howrah. I had the opportunity to engage in satsang with all the revered saints. It is my good fortune that today I have again received the opportunity to meet the saints associated with Shri Ramakrishna Ashram in Mysuru, my guru-brothers, and to take their blessings. Because of the presence of all of you, today on this holy land of Mysuru, I am experiencing a completely different energy. I respectfully bow at the feet of all you saints.

Friends,

Mysuru has been a center of India’s eternal cultural consciousness. The temples here, the traditions and festivals here, the Mysuru Dasara, its grand palaces, its music and literature, India’s heritage is embedded in every particle of this city. And it brings great satisfaction to see this. This city has preserved and nurtured this heritage with equal skill. The memories of Shri Ramakrishna Ashram and Swami Vivekananda Ji are also a rich part of Mysuru’s heritage. A little while ago, I also went to that historic building where Swami Vivekananda Ji spent some time during his stay. So many scholars and thinkers of Karnataka have been associated with this place. When great personalities like Rashtrakavi Kuvempu were in Mysuru, he also had a deep connection with Shri Ramakrishna Ashram. Today, through the inauguration of the Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Center, that is, Viveka Smaraka, we are giving a new expansion to this mission. For this, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to Shri Ramakrishna Ashram and all the scholars associated with it.

Friends,

The transformation from an individual into a great personality does not happen all of a sudden. For this, we have to give countless tests of life. One has to do sadhana, undergo penance, burn oneself, and consume oneself. After gaining fame, the world stands behind you. But, at the time of penance, it is not easy to recognize great personalities. The one who recognizes the seeker in their penance also becomes a partner in their success.

Therefore, brothers and sisters, Mysuru had such an important contribution in the life of Swami Vivekananda. About 130 years ago, Swami Ji came to Mysuru while traveling as a young sannyasi. At that time, his fame was not like this. But the thoughts were equally high. Among the people who recognized him at that time and joined him, one prominent name was that of the then Maharaja of Mysuru. When Swami Vivekananda Ji was in America, he wrote a letter from there to the then Maharaja of Mysuru. In that, he himself mentioned the support of the Maharaja.

Friends,

Swami Vivekananda Ji had assimilated Indian consciousness. He had assimilated the scriptures which say – “Para paropakarartham yo jivati sa jivati”. That is, in reality, only he lives who lives for others. Walking on this very mantra, this Shri Ramakrishna Ashram of Mysuru completed its hundred years last year. Whether it is services related to education and health, or relief work during natural disasters, Shri Ramakrishna Ashram has kept the legacy of Swami Vivekananda Ji alive. I believe that Viveka Smaraka will become a pilgrimage site for spiritual elevation for seekers and devotees. Swami Vivekananda Ji’s inspiration was – ‘Shiva jnane jiva seva’. That is, service to living beings is service to Shiva. Therefore, in this Viveka Smaraka, we have to shape such youth for whom the interest of society and nation, the pain of the poor and underprivileged, are above their own happiness and sorrow. Youth for whom ‘Nation First’ is the supreme mantra, and service to Mother India is their life goal.

Friends,

Swami Vivekananda Ji considered youth education to be the strong foundation of nation-building. He himself had seen how countries of the world were educating their youth. But unfortunately, India was enslaved then. India’s youth were also bound in the chains of slavery. From that era until now, the youth of India have covered a long journey. The youth of India who were once in chains are today giving momentum to the world’s development. Today, India’s economy is growing at the fastest pace. Because of whom? Because of the capability of India’s youth. Today, India has the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Because of whom? Because of the capability of India’s youth. Today, India has become the world’s second-largest mobile phone manufacturer. Because of whom? Because of the capability of India’s youth. Today, the Digital solutions made in India are becoming an inspiration for many countries around the world. Because of whom? Because of the capability of India’s youth. Today, India is moving forward rapidly on a new journey of semiconductor manufacturing. Because of whom? Because of the capability of India’s youth. Today, India is writing new chapters in AI, Deep Tech, Space Technology, and Innovation. Because of whom? Because of the capability of India’s youth.

Just a few days ago, we saw that the youth of India did wonders in space. For the first time, a rocket of a private company built by youth reached space. Today, whatever the sector may be, Indian youth are demonstrating their strength. We are all seeing around us that today a youth engaged in even the smallest business is driving India’s digital economy forward. He is making a new start through Mudra loans. He is leading the country’s startup revolution. Whether it is the Atmanirbhar Bharat campaign or the Make in India campaign, behind its success is the strength of India’s youth.

Friends,

In any country, the capability of youth becomes the power of that nation only when they get the right opportunities, when they get the right direction, and when they get the confidence to dream big on their own land and fulfill them. And in this, our educational institutions play a very big role. I am happy that today the number of educational institutions in India is continuously increasing. In the last 12 years, more than 650 new universities have been built. In the last 12 years, about 14 thousand new colleges have been built. More than 4 thousand new ITIs have been created. 9 new IIMs, 7 new IITs, and 13 new AIIMS have also been established. Today, MBBS seats in the country have reached around 1 lakh 40 thousand. The number of medical colleges has increased to 823.

Friends,

On one hand, we are modernizing the education infrastructure. At the same time, the education system is also being molded according to modern needs. The National Education Policy is becoming a medium to prepare the youth of India according to the 21st century.

Friends,

Work has also been done on a large scale in school education. More than 14 thousand PM SHRI schools have been developed across the country. So that education does not remain merely bookish and innovation and scientific temperament develop in children, for this, more than 10 thousand Atal Tinkering Labs have been established.

Friends,

Along with education, Swami Vivekananda Ji considered equality equally important for national upliftment. That there should be no discrimination in education, no discrimination in opportunities, today this has become the vision of the country. Today, daughters are also taking admissions in Sainik Schools. Daughters are contributing to the nation in NDA. Today, facilities have been made to study medicine and engineering in the mother tongue. Because of this, discrimination in opportunities based on language is being curbed.

Friends,

It is equally necessary for youth power to remain healthy, disciplined, and full of self-confidence. In countries that give importance to sports, the youth there develop these three qualities rapidly. Therefore, today sports are being seen as an important stream of nation-building. Events like Khelo India Youth Games, University Games, Para Games, and Winter Games have given a platform to youth across the country to showcase their talent. Today, modern sports infrastructure is expanding across the country, facilities are increasing through Khelo India Centers, and new talent is being identified from villages to small towns.

And friends,

Today, the results of this campaign are also clearly visible. India’s performance in international sports competitions is improving. Our players are creating new records, our daughters are increasing the pride of the country.

Friends,

Like Swami Vivekananda Ji, Viveka Smaraka inspires us to work for a larger purpose. At such a place, I want to make a few requests to our youth.

Friends,

Mysuru has often been ranked among India’s cleanest cities. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the people here for this. On this occasion, can we take a pledge that in the future we will continuously strengthen the resolve for cleanliness? We should conserve the natural resources here. We should take pledges related to the environment. We will have to work in mission mode to save every drop of water.

Friends,

Today itself, the Kannada translation of ‘Valmiki Ramayana’ has also been released here. I also want to make an appeal related to the Kannada language. Karnataka is the land of great writers and poets. Kannada-speaking people have always been known for their reading culture. In this era of smartphones, this nature should be encouraged further. Can we inspire the younger generation to connect deeply with Kannada literature?

Friends,

Mysuru is famous for its silk, sandalwood, and handicrafts. Whenever we gift someone, can we ensure that it is made by the hands and sweat of an Indian? This will promote our culture, and at the same time, another family will also get financial support.

Friends,

The responsibility to fulfill the dream of the India that Swami Vivekananda Ji saw lies on today’s generation. I believe Viveka Smaraka will work as an energy source for this. Once again, bowing to the revered saints, guru-brothers, and the people of Mysuru gathered here, I pause my words. Thank you very much to all of you.
texts.pms-address-at-the-launch-of-development:
Bharat Mata ki Jai.

Bharat Mata ki Jai.

Bharat Mata ki Jai.

Governor of Andhra Pradesh Abdul Nazeer ji, Governor of Goa and son of this soil Ashok Gajapathi Raju ji, Chief Minister, my friend Chandrababu Naidu ji, Deputy Chief Minister brother Pawan Kalyan ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet full of youthful energy brother Ram Mohan Naidu ji, Chandrasekhar Pemmasani ji, Bhupathi Raju Srinivasa Varma ji, Minister of the state government brother Nara Lokesh ji, present other public representatives, ladies and gentlemen.

Andariki Namaskaram!

Friends,

Today is a very important day for the development of Andhra Pradesh, for the vision of Swarna Andhra. On this very auspicious occasion, in an auspicious month, I have received the privilege of coming to this sacred land of North Andhra. First of all, I bow down at the feet of Lord Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy. I pay my respects to Sri Kurmanatha Swamy and Maa Pydithalli Ammavaru.

Friends,

Today, development projects worth around 18000 crore rupees have been inaugurated, dedicated to the nation, and had their foundation stones laid here. Along with the airport, these projects are also connected to Andhra’s road connectivity. Projects related to energy security are also included in these. These development works are a symbol of the speed with which Andhra is moving forward at this time. I give my heartiest best wishes to all of you for these projects.

Friends,

Today’s event is also about creating new history, new records. Today, on one hand, new records of development are being set, while on the other hand, a cultural record of Dhimsa dance has also been set, and this is the speciality of Chandrababu that he has touched two horizons. On one side, the construction of an airport – a system touching the high sky – and on the other side, the creation of a world record of Dhimsa dance by my tribal sisters here; I especially appreciate this vision of Chandrababu.

The performance of more than Thirteen Thousand tribal sisters and daughters, their enthusiasm, their discipline, and the pride of tribal culture – this scene was truly wonderful. In this, there was a glimpse of the country’s diversity as well as the tribal heritage preserved generation after generation. I congratulate all of you, and especially my tribal sisters and daughters, for this performance.

Friends,

This land is the land of Alluri Sitarama Raju. On the land where Alluri Sitarama Raju ji dedicated his life to tribal interests, today a new airport of Andhra Pradesh is starting on that very land. This airport is the runway for the growth of Andhra and North Andhra. This is the launch pad for a better future for the youth of Andhra. I extend my heartiest congratulations to the people of Andhra Pradesh and to the people of the country.

Friends,

Earlier, when airports were built, the names of the airports used to be attributed to a single family. We changed this tradition. We linked the name of the airport in Ayodhya with Valmiki, we linked the name of the airport in Punjab with Sant Ravidas Ji.

And friends,

The Central NDA Government has taken the decision that the name of this new airport will be after Sri Alluri Sitarama Raju. Whichever citizen of Andhra Pradesh travels from this airport, whichever citizen of the country and the world travels from this airport, will get inspiration for public service and national service in the name of Alluri Sitarama Raju ji.

Friends,

In the past twelve years, the country’s aviation sector has made extraordinary progress. Until 2014, only 74 airports were operational in the country. Today, this number is 166. There was a time when air flights were limited only to big cities. In the NDA government, today ordinary people from small towns are also travelling by flights. In twelve years, not only has the number of airports increased, but due to our UDAN scheme, poor families are also getting the opportunity to sit in an aeroplane today. This scheme has helped the poorest of the poor fulfil their dream. Just a few days ago, the government launched the second phase of the UDAN scheme. Twenty-nine thousand crore rupees will be spent on this as well.

Friends,

The country has achieved another major milestone in the aviation sector. Just a few days ago, the Spoke Airport Model that was launched in Kashi has reached Amritsar in Punjab today. Due to this, more than twenty-five international destinations will be connected from Amritsar. I congratulate the people of Punjab from this land of Andhra for this achievement as well.

Friends,

Our Andhra Pradesh has always been the growth engine of a developed India. For our efforts towards Andhra’s development to move forward at double engine speed, I had asked for the blessing of a double engine government from the people of Andhra; and today, under the leadership of Chandrababu Naidu ji and under the leadership of Pawan Kalyan ji, the entire NDA team is working for Andhra Pradesh at double speed.

Friends,

Today the country is continuously strengthening the Blue Economy. Our vision is that this entire region develops as a Coastal Economic Corridor. With this very goal, our old ports from Visakhapatnam to Krishnapatnam are being modernized. Apart from this, we are also building new ports in Mulapeta and Ramayapatnam.

Friends,

Along with port development, a network of highways and expressways is being prepared across Andhra. Projects like the Visakhapatnam-Raipur Expressway are giving speed to this entire region.

Friends,

So that this entire region connects easily with the country’s major industrial hubs, work is currently underway on railway projects worth around one lakh crore rupees in Andhra Pradesh today. Electrification of the state’s entire rail network has been completed. More than seventy railway stations here are also being modernized.

Friends,

Today, PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan is also playing a big role in the development of this region. Through PM Gati Shakti, rail, port, and airport are being connected together in this entire region. When this modern logistics network is prepared here, industries will get better connectivity, farmers will benefit, and Ease of Doing Business will also increase.

Friends,

Andhra Pradesh has always been a forward-thinking state. In software, IT, and the tech sector, the youth of Andhra have made their mark across the whole world. And that is why the government wants to connect the talent here with the development power of Andhra Pradesh. Andhra Pradesh and the country must benefit as much as possible from the talent of our talented youth. For this, our focus is now on futuristic tech industries like semiconductors. Laying the foundation stone of a new semiconductor plant in Visakhapatnam is a huge step in this direction. Under the leadership of Chandrababu, our Andhra will now become a hub for manufacturing along with software. This will create futuristic jobs in Andhra and a new environment will be created for tech industries.

Friends,

In the world economy, anywhere, the creation of any growth center cannot happen with just one factory; an entire ecosystem is needed for that. Today in Andhra Pradesh, we are creating that same ecosystem of growth. Chandrababu Naidu ji works day and night at a personal level. As a result of this, today many big companies of the world want to come here to invest.

Friends,

Along with semiconductors, work is also taking place here on AI infrastructure and data centers. Google has also announced a Fifteen Billion Dollar AI and cloud infrastructure campus here. Many other global companies are seeing new possibilities here. The youth of the country along with Andhra Pradesh are getting a huge benefit from this.

Friends,

Andhra’s industrial growth story is not limited to digital tech alone. In Nakkapalli, the Central Government is also providing support for a large bulk drug/pharma park. Because of this, Andhra Pradesh will also develop as a major pharma hub of the country. In the field of green energy, an investment of more than Five Lakh Crore Rupees has taken place in the Rayalaseema region alone. Today, I reassure all of you people of Andhra Pradesh again that our government—this double engine government—will continue to work day and night to realize every such possibility.

Friends,

You can gauge the speed with which work is happening in every sector in Andhra Pradesh today from the fact that in the last 3 visits alone, I have launched projects worth two lakh crore rupees here. I am happy that in this development journey of Andhra, ‘North Andhra’ is also becoming empowered. We are developing the Visakhapatnam Economic Region, V.E.R, as a major industrial center of the country. Our goal is for V.E.R to become a major economic hub of Asia. Everything from this airport to the semiconductor unit is part of this mission.

Friends,

Our government’s mantra is – Investment to Employment; therefore, the government has increased Investment from its side as well, and we are inspiring the private sector to invest too. You also know that when Investment increases, manufacturing increases; when manufacturing increases, exports increase; when exports increase, new job opportunities are created; and when employment increases, people’s income increases, families’ lives become better; and we are seeing this happening in Andhra Pradesh.

Friends,

I have full confidence that all the projects that have been started here today, whose foundations have been laid, will make a huge contribution to fulfilling the pledge of Swarna Andhra and Viksit Bharat. Under the leadership of Chandrababu ji, Andhra Pradesh is becoming a huge source of energy to fulfill the dream of Viksit Bharat. I once again congratulate the people of Andhra Pradesh very much for all these projects.

Thank you very much!

Bharat Mata ki Jai.

Bharat Mata ki Jai.

Bharat Mata ki Jai.

Thank you very much!
texts.pms-address-during-viksit-vibrant-villag:
Friends,

It was wonderful speaking with you all today. Union Cabinet colleague Mansukh Mandaviya ji, Minister Raksha Khadse ji, and youth companions from across the nation have joined us.

This program is truly special. Youth from nearly 250 districts of India are connected with this programme, and I warmly welcome you all.

Friends,

A few years ago, we created the My Bharat platform. Today, millions of young people across the country are part of it, and they are doing commendable work. From the Viksit Bharat Dialogue to the Vibrant Village Program, you have shown your strength and capability.

Friends,

During the Young Leaders Dialogue, I shared an idea: instead of only connecting virtually, why not step onto the ground, experience India, live India, and understand India? The aspirations for development in villages can only be felt by visiting them. In our border villages, the desire for progress is matched by a deep sense of patriotism. Often, it feels that for them, the nation comes first, and personal comforts later.

That is why the purpose was for youth from different districts to travel to villages in Himachal, Uttarakhand, and Ladakh. To see how people live, what they eat, how they work, their culture, their way of life, their challenges. To witness how people in the first villages of the nation remain alert for the country’s security, and how close their bond is with the rest of India. This experience was meant for our youth. The enthusiasm shown was extraordinary. Nearly 300,000 youth participated in this competition, and more than 400 were selected. You stayed for a week in these remote villages – places unknown to you. You tried to live their life, blended into their culture, connected your own traditions with theirs. This is perhaps the finest example of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat.

Friends,

This program is special for me personally as well. When I was away from government and politics, I often visited such border villages. I built long-lasting connections with many of them. Even after entering government, I never miss an opportunity to visit border villages. You all know that for the past 25 years, I have celebrated Diwali at the border with our brave soldiers. Some of the villages you visited are ones I have been to myself. As you described your experiences, I could see those old memories vividly. Your experiences were equally inspiring – some spoke of the thrill of high mountain ranges, others of the warmth and affection of border villagers, some of the dreams of children, and some witnessed the courage and discipline of our army. Truly, the Vibrant Village experience was remarkable. Coincidentally, today is Kargil Vijay Diwas. Many of you visited areas around Kargil, where our brave soldiers triumphed in the most challenging conditions. You saw this with your own eyes. I congratulate you all for being part of this program and for gaining such enriching experiences.

Friends,

A developed village is the foundation of a developed India. The journey of building a developed India is ongoing, and in this journey, the role of youth is immense. When the youth connect with the ground, they broaden the vision of a developed India. It strengthens their resolve to live for the nation and to contribute to it.

Friends,

In this campaign, you must have experienced how difficult life is in border villages. Yet, despite every hardship, the people of these villages live patriotism every moment. Until a few years ago, border villages were called the “last villages” and left to their fate. Roads, electricity, water, schools, hospitals – all basic facilities were absent. You may have heard many such stories from the people there. They must have told you about the earlier conditions. And we should be proud that even in such circumstances, their patriotism never weakened, not even a fraction.

That is why, friends,

Our government has considered these border villages as the nation’s first villages. The first villages where the morning sun greets India, and where the last rays bid good night. Where the tricolor first converses with the wind. Where the world sees India for the first time. This change in thinking has transformed our border regions. In many villages, electricity reached for the first time since independence, roads reached for the first time, tap water reached homes for the first time, gas connections reached kitchens for the first time. In cities, these may seem ordinary, but for those people, they are life-changing. Farmers and orchard owners now find it easier to take fruits and vegetables to big markets. Better connectivity means life no longer stops – it moves nonstop. And you must have seen that even in these remote villages, excellent internet connectivity is now available. You described it with such joy.

Friends,

Every facility has another benefit – tourism is flourishing in these regions. Villages that had become deserted are now lively again. Daughters are going to schools and colleges. A good environment for education and earning is being created. The Vibrant Village Program is accelerating this development further.

Friends,

The journey of developed vibrant villages is a powerful medium of connecting everyone. And now your responsibility has increased even more. Your journey is one of unity through participation. The more India’s youth know the border villages, the more easily they will know India, connect with every corner of India, and strengthen the nation. Remember, in those villages there were no guest houses or hotels for you. The entire village itself became your host. And your stay was not just about accommodation – it became a cultural classroom. You received more satisfaction and respect than facilities. What you experienced cannot be learned in any classroom. Share these experiences with other youth. Inspire them to visit border villages. The more youth go and stay there, the more they will see and understand the nation. And as people begin to visit, facilities will reach those villages even faster.

Friends,

Our government is promoting tourism in border villages. You can expand these efforts. I urge each of you to share your experiences with at least 100 other young people. Stay connected with people in your region. If you took photos or videos there, share them widely on social media. Collaborate with local content creators to promote nature and culture. If you saw local products, think about how to promote them in your area. The internet has plenty of information, but you can share authentic knowledge about these villages. Visit these villages again with your friends and family. I also encourage schools, colleges, and universities to organize educational tours to border villages.

Friends,

I have always firmly believed that India’s youth like you will shape the 21st-century world. This is the true destiny of India’s youth. Today’s youth are both the energy of a developed India and its greatest beneficiaries. When youth power connects directly with the nation’s challenges and solutions, the future will surely be bright. With this spirit, I once again extend my best wishes to you all.

Thank you very much.
texts.pms-remarks-at-the-start-of-monsoon-sess:
A warm welcome to all of you.

The monsoon is beginning to show its positive impact, and the Monsoon Session of Parliament is also commencing. Be it the monsoon or the Monsoon Session, when both are proactive, they become highly productive. And when both are productive, they contribute to the well-being of the nation and of all living beings. With this hope, we pray that the monsoon remains proactive and that the Monsoon Session is equally productive.

Friends,

In the past month, the country has achieved many milestones, filling citizens with pride. These achievements span national, international, and even space domains. For India, these have been moments of glory. Just before the Monsoon Session last year, an Indian citizen reached the International Space Station. And only the day before yesterday, a young Indian start-up accomplished an extraordinary feat. There are only a handful of countries in the world where private enterprises have demonstrated such capability. Our young innovators have taken India’s aspirations to new heights in space, and this is a truly remarkable achievement. I am told that the average age of the team working at the Skyroot start-up is just 28 years. It is these young minds who have made this possible. I am not talking about a 56-year-old young man; I am talking about a start-up whose team, with an average age of just 28, has planted India’s flag in the realm of space. They certainly deserve our heartfelt congratulations. More importantly, such achievements instil immense confidence in our nation and further strengthen India’s standing as a respected and trusted partner in the world.

Friends,

This is no coincidence; it is a powerful message—a message that the capabilities and aspirations of India’s youth are as limitless as space itself. There can be no greater inspiration for the nation than this.

Friends,

It is the result of the reform express that the country has boarded, which enables our youth to take such bold steps and succeed.

Friends,

Recently, a major oil refinery was dedicated to the nation in Rajasthan. A few weeks ago, the country’s third semiconductor plant was inaugurated. Just days ago, a green hydrogen-powered train was launched – a facility available in very few countries. But the hydrogen train India has dedicated to its citizens is the most powerful engine-driven and the longest in the world. This is the outcome of the dedication of India’s scientists, engineers, innovators, entrepreneurs, and workers, all working with a mission for the nation.

Friends,

We know well, and the world is concerned, that war-like situations keep arising. The war in West Asia has posed a major crisis for countries like India, dependent on others for energy. Petrol, diesel, LPG, fertilizers, chemicals – all faced disruptions. Yet, India continued to grow at 7.7 percent, becoming the fastest-growing major economy in the world. This reflects India’s strength and its determination to scale new heights with enthusiasm and energy. As the Monsoon Session begins, the country has picked up speed, and Parliament’s spirit can infuse new energy into this momentum. A positive spirit is essential to achieve national goals. Our House has many experienced parliamentarians, regardless of party, whose knowledge and wisdom are needed by Parliament and the nation. Therefore, Parliament must function, meaningful discussions must take place, and collective resolutions must be made to move the country forward. This is the demand of the times and the aspiration of the youth. Today, the demand is that voices filled with patriotism and national devotion find a proper platform in Parliament, to raise their voices and guide the nation. I am confident that where facts and logic prevail, there is no room for disruption. Strong arguments and strong facts allow voices to be raised calmly yet powerfully. I hope Parliament’s discussions are enriched with facts and logic, every voice gets an opportunity, and every idea receives respect. This is our role in Parliament. I invite all MPs to participate actively in this session. This morning, the Speaker also welcomed MPs through social media. I join my voice with his.

Thank you all very much.

Namaskar.
texts.pms-speech-at-the-launch-of-multiple-dev:
Mr. Gulab Chand Kataria ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet J. P. Nadda ji, Ashwini Vaishnaw ji, my fellow parliamentarian Manish Tiwari ji, and here in the auditorium many legislators, ministers, and MPs are present. I also see many distinguished personalities today, familiar faces from long ago.

Brothers and sisters,

It is a special joy to be among you today.

Friends,

Chandigarh is not just a city – it has been a model of development for India. Chandigarh is known for planned growth, for its identity as a city of better lifestyle and ease of living. It is recognized for advanced medical facilities, and above all, for the blessings of Maa Chandi. That is why the development of Chandigarh has always been a priority for the NDA government. You may recall, about a year and a half ago, the country made a major reform in its justice system. We replaced the Penal Code with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita – a justice-based legal framework instead of punishment-based laws. And the implementation of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita began right here in Chandigarh.

Friends,

In recent years, projects like the Integrated Command and Control Centre, smart traffic management, smart parking, and digital governance have been undertaken to make Chandigarh hi-tech. More than ₹2,500 crore has been spent on this mission. Even today, several new projects related to health, education, and infrastructure are being launched here. I congratulate all residents of Chandigarh for these initiatives.

Friends,

Before coming here, I was in Jind, Haryana, and after this I will go to Jalandhar for Punjab’s development programs. Between these two, today’s program in Chandigarh is taking place. Because Chandigarh connects Haryana, Punjab, Himachal, and the entire region. The development of Chandigarh not only transforms the lives of its residents but also benefits the people of Haryana, Himachal, Punjab, and Jammu & Kashmir. In terms of medical services, Chandigarh is a major hub for this entire region.

Friends,

When I lived in Chandigarh, I often had to go to PGI. Why? Because someone from our colleagues or their families – whether from Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Himachal, or Haryana – would come here for treatment, and it was natural for me to visit them. That is why I know how important PGI has been for the health needs of people across this region.

Friends,

Today, advanced healthcare facilities at Chandigarh PGI are being expanded. The Advanced Neurosciences Centre, Advanced Mother and Child Centre, and Critical Care Hospital Block will provide better treatment to lakhs of people. I remember attending PGI’s convocation in 2015. I am glad that today I am virtually meeting many old colleagues there again. In this decade, PGI’s capacity has expanded greatly. I appreciate the management, professors, and young doctors of PGI Chandigarh and extend my best wishes to them.

Friends,

When we talk about health, we all know how important cleanliness is. That is why when our government was formed, we launched the Swachh Bharat Mission. Millions of toilets were built, India was freed from open defecation, campaigns were run for cleanliness in public places, and initiatives were started to make cleanliness a part of our lifestyle. The Swachh Bharat rankings of our cities are part of this effort, and Chandigarh has consistently worked to perform well in them.

Friends,

I also want to appreciate retired IPS officer Inderjit Singh Sidhu ji of Chandigarh. He is known as the “Broom Warrior.” He awakened a new consciousness about cleanliness in Chandigarh and inspired people. For this, our government honored him with the Padma award this year.

Friends,

Cleanliness is not a one-day task – it is a way of life. I am happy that cleanliness has been linked with today’s program as well. Under the Swachhata Se Swagat initiative, a special cleanliness campaign was carried out. I saw on social media that leaders and citizens alike were engaged in cleaning. It created a joyful atmosphere across the country. I proudly congratulate all residents of Chandigarh for this initiative.

Friends,

Such cleanliness campaigns have proven very helpful in preventing many diseases in the country.

Friends,

There was a time when the world expressed concern about India’s health sector. Whenever a major disaster was anticipated, people questioned what would happen in India.
